"May they bestow that gate of the world, which is pure, luminous, radiant, and glorious; which yields the streams of immortality in many ways; and which, moving through the world, establishes the well-placed [state]—the Sudhita.
Having recited this mantra, which removes all malevolent grahas...
One should consume [the remainder] and sprinkle one's body, as well as one's sons, friends, and dependents.
Furthermore:
"The water from Viṣṇu’s feet, when drunk, destroys the sin of ten million killings; yet that very same water, by the falling of a single drop upon the ground, incurs eightfold sin. (Hbhv 9.18)
Now, regarding the greatness of drinking the water used for washing the feet [of the Lord], as told in the *Pādma Purāṇa* in the dialogue between Gautama and Ambarīṣa:
"He in whose stomach remains the water left over from Hari’s bath..."
O best of sages, having bowed down deeply, let the dust of your feet be accepted.
In that very same Devadūta-vikuṇḍala-saṃvāda it is said:
"For those men who constantly drink the water from the Śālagrāma stone, what need is there for the consumption of thousands of *pañcagavya*? (Hbhv 9.20)
What is the use of resorting to millions of sacred fords (tīrthas), if one were to constantly drink the meritorious water from the Śālagrāma stone? (Hbhv 9.21)
A man endowed with the spirit of devotion who drinks even a single drop of water from a Śālagrāma stone shall never again drink the breast milk of a mother. (Hbhv 9.22)
Furthermore:
Those by whom the water of the Śālagrāma stone is always and constantly drunk burn away all hells and the painful dwelling in a womb. (Hbhv 9.23)
In that very same [text], in the dialogue between Śrī Yama and Dhūmraketu:
"Whoever drinks even a single drop of the water from a Śālagrāma stone, being one who has exerted effort on the path of devotion, shall be liberated from all sins. (Hbhv 9.24)
In that very same [work], in the dialogue between Pulastya and Bhṛguṛatha, regarding the majesty of the water from the feet [of the Lord]:
"O Bhṛguṛatha, I shall tell you of the greatness of the water from the feet;
it is more purifying than all other holy fords and is the destroyer of ten million murders. (Hbhv_9.25)
When the head is held and [the feet] are honored, all the deities are satisfied;
indeed, in the Kali age, the water from the feet of Hari is the atonement for sins. (Hbhv 9.26)
Furthermore:
The water of the Sarasvatī purifies after three days, that of the Narmadā after seven days, that of the Gaṅgā immediately, and that of the Yamunā by its mere sight. (Hbhv 9.27)
These waters purify through bathing, seeing, and performing ritual acts;
however, in the Kali age, the water from the feet of Hari purifies by its mere remembrance.
Moreover:
"Whatever fruit is constantly obtained by worshipping ten million *liṅgas*, that fruit is increased a hundred thousandfold when one offers the water from the feet of Hari to one's father. (Hbhv 9.29)
Whether one is impure, of evil conduct, or burdened with a great sin,
a human being is always purified by touching the water from the feet of Viṣṇu.
Even one who is burdened by millions of sins, if at the time of death he places water from his feet upon the head and face of another's body, does not go to the abode of Yama.

Even those for whom there is no gift-giving, no oblation, no private Vedic study, and no worship of the gods—by drinking the water from [the guru's] feet, they too attain the supreme goal. (Hbhv 9.32)

What will he achieve at Puṣkara during the month of Kārttika when the moon is in conjunction with the asterism Kṛttikā, if for him the water from the feet of Hari is as constant as Puṣkara itself? (Hbhv 9.33)
O Blessed One, when the month of Vaiśākha coincides with the Viśākhā constellation,
he will perform [the rite] at the great pilgrimage site of Piṇḍāraka in Ujjayinī.
What need will there be for bathing at Prayāga during the month of Māgha for one who constantly possesses the water from the feet of Hari at Prayāga? (Hbhv 9.35)
When the day of awakening arrives, what need is there for him in Mathurā?
For he who possesses the water from Hari’s feet has the eternal bath in the Yamunā.
What [difference is there] for one who has died in the north-flowing Gaṅgā, when the water from Viṣṇu’s feet remains in his very mouth? (Hbhv 9.37)
Furthermore:
"He who, having abandoned the water from Viṣṇu’s feet, goes to other sacred fords, is a fool who discards a priceless jewel and desires a clod of earth. (Hbhv 9.38)
A region equal to Kurukṣetra is considered to be a single drop of water from the washing of the feet.
Wherever [this] falls, inexhaustible merit constantly arises in that house;
for sons, too, merit equal to that of the *piṇḍa* offering at Gayā is produced.
Those who perform the libation for the ancestors with the water from the feet of the Lord shall have no fear of asuras, nor of that which arises from pretas or rakshasas. (Hbhv 9.41)
There is no fear of disease, nor is there any fear caused by obstacles;
there are no wicked beings, nor those with terrible eyes, and indeed no fear arising from wild beasts.
Planets do not cause harm like predatory beasts, and fierce thieves perish;
what need has he for traveling to sacred fords or for beholding celestial rishis? (Hbhv 9.43)
Upon whose head the water from the feet arising from the Śālagrāma stone is placed,
Mārtaṇḍa becomes well-pleased, Keśava becomes well-pleased,
Brahmā becomes thoroughly pleased, and Saṅkara becomes well-pleased. (Hbhv 9.44)
Whoever recites this greatness of the water for washing the feet before Keśava goes to the supreme abode where the Lord Janārdana dwells.
In the *Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Śrī Brahmā and Nārada:
"If an expiation has been incurred—whether it be the *kṛcchra* penance or the *aghamarṣaṇa*—even he attains purification instantly by drinking the water from [the Lord's] feet. (Hbhv 9.46)
Impurity shall never exist for those who place the water from [the Guru's] feet upon their heads and those who drink it; this applies both in birth and in death.
Even at the time of death, he whose water is seen upon the feet here attains a good destination, even if he has been excluded from the ranks of those of virtuous conduct.
Even those who drink what is undrinkable, those who eat what is unfit for food,
those who approach women who should not be approached, and those men of sinful conduct—
these too quickly become worthy of honor by the immediate service of his foot-water.
Furthermore:
Having eaten impure food or even the drink of sinners, one becomes purified by drinking the water from the feet of Hari after having offered [it]. (Hbhv 9.50)

O observer of noble vows, by drinking the water from the feet of Hari, one attains purification of the body more swiftly than through the *taptakṛcchra*, the *pañcagavya*, the *mahākṛcchra*, the *cāndrāyaṇa*, the *pārākṛcchra*, or even the *parāka* penances. (Hbhv 9.51)
Aloe-wood, saffron, camphor, and even ointment—
when they have come into contact with the water from Viṣṇu’s feet, they indeed become the purifiers of purifiers.
O son, even water that has been purified by the glance of the powerful Viṣṇu removes sin; how much more so, then, the water from his feet?
For this purpose, my son, being devoted to Viṣṇu, I bear [this] upon my head;
today I drink it, for its greatness is known to me. (Hbhv 9.54)
"You are my beloved, my eldest son; it was for that reason that I spoke thus.
However, this secret of mine must never be told to one who is unworthy."
Always wear it upon your head and consume it constantly;
O son, you shall attain liberation from the sufferings of birth, death, and old age.
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"It bestows immediate fruit, is meritorious, destroys all sins, is the most auspicious of all auspicious things, and annihilates all suffering. (Hbhv 9.57)
The auspicious water from Viṣṇu’s feet is meritorious and destroys bad dreams;
it is the destroyer of all calamities and the eradicator of all diseases.
It pacifies all calamities, wards off all evil, bestows all auspiciousness and happiness, and grants the fruits of all desires. (Hbhv_9.59)
It bestows all accomplishments, brings prosperity, increases all virtuous qualities,
pacifies all enemies, and grants all enjoyments.

By pouring a stream of water from the feet upon the head, one obtains the fruit of visiting all holy fords; by performing the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), one gains the merit of serving Prayāga, Prabhāsa, Puṣkara, and the holy ford of Pṛthūdaka. (Hbhv 9.61)

Whatever fruit is obtained at Cakratīrtha, and whatever fruit one might obtain by going to the Sarasvatī and Gayā, that same excellent fruit one receives from pouring water for the feet upon the head. (Hbhv 9.62)
In the Skanda Purāṇa:
"The greatness of the water from the feet [of the Lord] is known only to the god Śaṅkara,
by whom the Gaṅgā, fallen from Viṣṇu’s foot, was borne upon his head."
There is no place for evil within the bodies of embodied beings.
He whose entire being, both external and internal, is indeed pervaded by the water from [the Lord's] feet;
he in whose stomach resides the water from the feet and the food offering (naivedya) of Viṣṇu.
Evil finds no foothold; it perishes of its own accord, even if one is seized by a planet of great evil or overwhelmed by hundreds of diseases.
By drinking the water from Hari’s feet, one is liberated; there is no doubt in this matter.
Those who always bear the water from Hari’s feet upon their heads [attain liberation]. (Hbhv 9.66)
What will you achieve in this world with your desires for ten million sacred fords?
This alone is the supreme dharma; this alone is the supreme austerity;
this alone is the supreme sacred ford: that one should drink the water from the lotus feet of Viṣṇu.
In that very same [text], in the dialogue between Śiva and Umā:
"Sins go to dissolution in the water from the feet of Hari when merely touched (pṛte); how much more so the water from the feet of Viṣṇu that has fallen from the Śālagrāma stone! (Hbhv 9.68)
O beloved, it especially removes sins such as the killing of a Brahmin;
if one is liberated by the water from Viṣṇu’s feet while alive, one shall slay all the messengers of Yama and attain the world of Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 9.69)
In that very place, in the dialogue between Śiva and Kārttikeya within the *Śrī-śālagrāma-śilā-māhātmya*, it is said:
"O Mahāsena, by him the most dreadful dwelling in a womb has been severed, because he always drinks the water from the Śālagrāma stone of Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 9.70)
For those men who constantly drink the water from the Śālagrāma stone, what need is there for them to consume thousands of *pañcagavya*? (Hbhv 9.71)

When an occasion for expiation has arisen, what is the use of gifts, what is the use of fasts, or of the Cāndrāyaṇa penance and pilgrimages? Having asked [the preceptor], one becomes pure by [drinking] the water used for washing his feet.
In the *Bṛhannāradīya*, at the beginning of the narrative concerning the hunter:
"He who would bear the water from Hari’s feet for even a single moment is as one who has bathed in all sacred fords and is likewise most dear to Viṣṇu. (Hbhv_9.73)
The auspicious water from the feet of Hari pacifies untimely death, destroys all diseases, and brings to rest all suffering.
In that very place, at the conclusion of that narrative, it is said:
"By the touch of the water from Hari’s feet, the hunter was cleansed of his sins;
having ascended a divine celestial chariot, he then spoke to this sage. (Hbhv 9.75)
O Sage, because you have sprinkled the water from Hari’s feet upon me,
I have therefore been led by you to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
In the *Haribhaktisudhodaya* it is said:

"Having merely touched its water with her foot, the Gaṅgā indeed became the bestower of liberation to those who remember her; how then can the water from the lotus feet of Viṣṇu, the assembly of the virtuous, ever be surpassed? (Hbhv 9.77)
That fire of the three-fold affliction which cannot be extinguished by all the oceans is quickly quenched by the mere water from the lotus feet of the glorious Viṣṇu.

The armor impenetrable by the weapons of battle, the medicinal herb that quenches the fire of worldly existence—this water for the feet, which purifies all parts in every way, should always be held by those whose state is pure. (Hbhv 9.79)
He who drinks the water from the lotus feet of Viṣṇu, which is eternal and brings about immortality,
drinks the nectar of the gods month after month.
Even he who says, "Its greatness is only this much," is fearless;
surely, one who assigns a price to a priceless jewel incurs sin.
Elsewhere it is also said:
"He is a true celibate, he is one who observes vows, and he is always pure, in whose mouth, head, and body there is the water from Viṣṇu’s feet. (Hbhv 9.82)
One should resort to the water of the Śālagrāma stone, which removes all sins; it serves as an atonement for the misdeeds committed since birth. (Hbhv 9.83)
For this very reason, it was stated by Lord Brahmā in the *Tejodravina-pañcarātra*:
"O son, having taken water separately from the channel of the back, one should sprinkle it upon the heads of devotees; for that [water] consists of all sacred fords (*tīrtha*). (Hbhv 9.84)
The greatness of the water for washing the feet is renowned in all the scriptures;
for who indeed could be able to write it down, even if they were to count the drops of the ocean?
And especially, having placed water for the feet together with *tulasī* leaves in a conch shell and given it to the Vaiṣṇavas, one should drink from it oneself as before. (Hbhv 9.86)
Now, regarding the greatness of the water used for washing the feet (*pādodaka*) offered by Śaṅkha,
as related in the *Skanda Purāṇa* within the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada:
"Having offered the water for washing the feet of the high-souled Vaiṣṇavas into the conch..."
Whoever should give [food] mixed with *tulasī* shall obtain the merit of a hundred *cāndrāyaṇa* fasts.
Having taken the water from Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet and placed it upon his conch shell,
the Vaiṣṇava who constantly carries it upon his head is a sage, the best of ascetics.
In the *Pādmapurāṇa*, in the dialogue between the divine messenger and Vikuṇḍala:
"If one drinks the water from a *śālagrāma* stone held in a conch shell, it destroys ten million killings; of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv_9.89)
In the *Agastya-saṃhitā*:
"For those who drink the water from a Śālagrāma stone scented with *tulasī* leaves, there is no further drinking of mother's milk. (Hbhv 9.90) Thus it is said.
Having sipped water that purifies Śrī Viṣṇu and the Vaiṣṇavas—which embodies all sacred fords—one should indeed perform the ritual rinsing of the mouth (ācamana). Hbhv_9.91.

Thus it was said by Śiva in the Skanda Purāṇa: "He who, having drunk the water from Viṣṇu’s feet, subsequently sips water for purification out of delusion while still impure, is declared a slayer of a Brahmin. (Hbhv 9.92)
And the Śruti says:
"The Blessed One is pure; the feet of the Blessed One are pure;
the water from the feet of the Blessed One is pure."
There is no sipping of water after drinking that [liquor], just as there is none after drinking Soma. (Hbhv 9.93)
And in the *Sauparṇa*:
"He who, out of delusion, sips the water from Viṣṇu’s feet as well as the water from the feet of a devotee, is declared a slayer of a Brahmin. (Hbhv 9.94) Thus it is said.
Then, one should place a conch shell filled with pure water and provided with scents, flowers,
and unbroken grains (akṣata) above and below in front of the Blessed One.
Now, regarding the greatness of placing the conch before the Blessed One, as told in the *Skanda Purāṇa* within the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the section on the majesty of the conch:
"In front of Vāsudeva, [one should place] the conch along with flowers, water, and unbroken grains (*akṣata*)."
If one should behold a conch shell that has been worshipped, prosperity is not difficult for him to attain.
"Prosperity is attained from every side for him before whom Vāsudeva has water-born [lotuses] with flowers, along with *dūrvā* grass and unbroken rice grains. (Hbhv 9.97).
Then, becoming devoted, [he worshipped] the Lord in a grove of glorious *tulasī*.
Having fully honored him, one should worship that beloved of the feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Now, regarding the worship of Śrī-Tulasī and the forest:

having first offered the *arghya* and then worshipped her with perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice, and so forth, one should praise that Blessed Lady and prostrate like a staff after making one's request. (Hbhv 9.99)
Now, the mantra for the water offering (arghya):
"O Goddess, abode of Śrī, who are eternally honored by a stream of prosperity—for the sake of the glory of Śrī—accept this water offering given by me with devotion; homage be to you! (Hbhv 9.100)
O Tulasī, you were created by the gods in ancient times; you are worshipped by both deities and asuras. Remove my sin, accept this offering, and homage be to you! (Hbhv_9.101)
O Tulasī, you who generate great grace, increase all prosperity, and eternally remove mental anguish and physical disease— homage be to you! (Hbhv_9.102)
O Tulasī, you who are gracious, grant me my prayer: bestow prosperity, fame, renown, long life, as well as happiness, strength, nourishment, and righteousness. Hbhv_9.103 //
The verse of salutation in the Avantṛ-khaṇḍa:
She who, when seen, pacifies the entire multitude of sins; when touched, she purifies the body.

Salutations to that Tulasī, who is worshipped by those free from disease, who sprinkles [the ground] and terrifies Death himself, who brings about proximity to the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa, who is planted and established at His feet, and who bestows the fruit of liberation. Hbhv_9.104 //
O Bhagavatī Tulasī, in this ocean of the nectar of your majesty, I, a base being, desire to leap in greed; may that be forgiven by you. (Hbhv_9.105)
Now, regarding the greatness of the worship of the Tulasī grove, it is stated in the Skanda Purāṇa:
"On the twelfth lunar day of the month of Śrāvaṇa, during the conjunction [of the moon with the asterism], through the worship of the Śālagrāma stone..."
Whatever fruit is proclaimed for the attainment of union [with the deity], that same fruit is obtained through the worship of Tulasī.
In the Gāruḍa [Purāṇa]:
"O Lord of Birds, whatever merit is gained by men through fasting on the Jayantī day with the fruit of the dhātrī tree, that same merit is obtained through the worship of tulasī. (Hbhv 9.107)
Whatever fruit has been ordained by the gods for one intent on bathing at Prayāga or for one engaged in the liberation of living beings, that same fruit is obtained through the worship of Tulasī.
In the *Agastya-saṃhitā*:
"Indeed, when [this] is worshipped, it bestows the desired fruit upon all four castes and stages of life, and especially upon women and men. (Hbhv 9.109)
The *tulasī* plant, when planted, watered, seen, or touched, purifies;
when propitiated with effort, it bestows the fruit of all desires. (Hbhv 9.110)
Now, regarding the greatness of the worship of the Tulasī grove:
for those who, having circumambulated it, offer salutations constantly, not even an atom of sin remains for them. (Hbhv 9.111)
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, at the conclusion of the narrative of Yajñadhvaja:
"O twice-born ones, all auspicious fortunes increase day by day for that person in whose house Tulasī remains while being worshipped. (Hbhv 9.112)
For this very reason, in the *Pādmapurāṇa*, in the dialogue between the divine messenger and Vikuṇḍala, it is said:
"O best of Vaiśyas, when every fortnight has arrived, even Brahmā and the other gods perform the worship of the Tulasī grove on the twelfth day. (Hbhv 9.113)
Therefore, regarding the greatness of the praise of *śrī-tulasī*:
"The man who constantly praises *tulasī* with a mind focused on no other is always beloved by the ancestors, the gods, and human beings. (Hbhv 9.114)
Now, regarding the greatness of the Tulasī grove, it is said in the Skanda Purāṇa:
"One does not fix one's affection elsewhere except for a grove of Tulasī."
The God of gods, the Lord of the world, [is especially effective] in the Kali age.
Having abandoned thousands of sacred fords and even all the mountains,
Keśava dwells eternally in the grove of Tulasī during the Kali age.

Those men by whom groves and gardens of *tulasī* have been looked upon with longing, and those by whom they have been planted according to the prescribed rite, have attained the supreme state. (Hbhv 9.117)
That place where there is no Dhātrī tree bearing fruit, nor a grove of Tulasī, nor Vaiṣṇavas, is equal to a cremation ground. (Hbhv 9.118)
But those who plant [trees] on this earth for the sake of Keśava during the Kali age—what can even Yama, dissatisfied along with his Kiṅkaras, do to them? (Hbhv 9.119)
The planting of Tulasī should be performed, especially on the day of Śravaṇa;
Puruṣottama forgives thousands of offenses.
That man who plants the meritorious *tulasī* in all temples and sacred fields— that is a holy site (*tīrtha*) of the Wielder of the Discus.
O best of Brahmins, the grove of *tulasī* was sprinkled with water from jars and mechanical contrivances, and the three worlds were refreshed by streams of water. (Hbhv 9.122)
In that very same [text], in the dialogue between Śrī Brahmā and Nārada:
"Wherever the wind goes taking the fragrance of the tulasī, the ten directions shall become purified, as shall the fourfold classes of living beings. (Hbhv 9.123)
O twice-born one, wherever there is the shade produced by a grove of *tulasī* trees, there a *śrāddha* should be offered for the sake of the satisfaction of the ancestors. (Hbhv 9.124)
O Nārada, wherever a multitude of *tulasī* sprouts falls, there the offering of funeral cakes (*piṇḍa*) made results in inexhaustible benefit for the ancestors. (Hbhv 9.125)
In that very same place, it is said:
"Seen, touched, meditated upon, fashioned, bowed to, heard, planted, served, and constantly honored—the auspicious *tulasī* [is thus revered]. (Hbhv 9.126)
Those who daily worship the *tulasī* plant in nine ways every day shall dwell in the abode of Hari for thousands of millions of *yugas*.
As long as the planted *tulasī* spreads its roots, for that long it expands a thousand million merits in the Kali age. (Hbhv 9.128)
O Sage, as long as Tulasī, planted by men upon the surface of the earth, grows with its branches, twigs, buds, flowers, and fruits, [so long does it flourish]. (Hbhv 9.129)
Those born in their family, those who will be born, and those who have died—
throughout a kalpa, for a thousand yugas, they shall dwell in the abode of Hari.
And in that very same *Āvantya-khaṇḍa*:
"Blessed are those whose sprout-like hands gather *tulasī*, and those who, for the sake of Keśava, plant it upon the earth in the Kali age. (Hbhv 9.131)
In bathing, giving gifts, meditation, consuming [food], and the worship of Keśava, Tulasī burns away sin; even in the Kali age, it does so through planting and cutting.
In the *Khaṇḍa* on the Command of Yama regarding his own messengers:
"O soldiers, those who are adorned with *tulasī*, those who mutter the name of *tulasī*, and those who guard groves of *tulasī*—these must be avoided from afar. (Hbhv 9.133)
In that very same *Dhruvacarita*:
"In whosever house Tulasī is worshipped daily, the messengers of Yama never approach that house. (Hbhv 9.134)
In the *Pādmapurāṇa*, in the dialogue between the divine messenger and Vikuṇḍala, it is said:
"O Vaiśya, by planting a grove of *tulasī*, one does not see Yama;
for a *tulasī* grove removes all sins and grants all desires. (Hbhv_9.135)
O Vaiśya, that house in which a grove of Tulasī stands indeed becomes a sacred pilgrimage site; the messengers of Yama do not enter it. (Hbhv 9.136)
Those who plant *tulasī* dwell in the world of the gods for as many thousands of years as there are petals on its leaves.
Having smelled the fragrance of *tulasī*, the ancestors, with minds satisfied,
depart mounted upon Garuḍa to that abode of the Discus-Wielder.
O best of Vaiśyas, beholding the Narmadā, bathing in the Gaṅgā,
and the touch of a Tulasī leaf— these three are considered equal.
Through clothing, protection, sprinkling, showing, and touching, the *tulasī* burns away the sins accumulated by men through speech, mind, and body. (Hbhv 9.140)
Whatever fruit is obtained from a thousand mango trees and a hundred peepal trees,
that indeed is obtained by a single branch of the *tulasī*.
He who plants *tulasī* while engaged in the worship of Viṣṇu rejoices in heaven for eleven times ten thousand ages.
In that very same [text], the *Vaiśākha-māhātmya*, it is said:
"The holy places beginning with Puṣkara, the rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, and the gods beginning with Vāsudeva all dwell within a leaf of *tulasī*. (Hbhv 9.143)
Tulasī quickly removes even very many evils, such as the suffering of poverty and the affliction of disease, just as the myrobalan fruit removes diseases.
In that very same *Kārttika-māhātmya* it is said:
"In whatever house Tulasī shines, protected by [ritual] sprinklings of water, the messengers of Yama indeed avoid that house from afar. (Hbhv_9.145)
Those men who perform the libation for the ancestors with *tulasī* water, their ancestors remain satisfied by that water for ten thousand years. (Hbhv 9.146)
And those who have performed service for him through protection and by binding him as a child—by those who have thus served Hari, no further deliberation need be made in this matter. (Hbhv 9.147)
The sages should never show contempt for this [tree] because of its state as a tree, just as they do not despise the body of Vāsudeva which enjoys the realm of Vaikuṇṭha. (Hbhv 9.148)
The form of the Śālagrāma stone is seen on earth as stationary;
likewise, Tulasī, having attained union with Lakṣmī, possesses a body for enjoyment.
Furthermore, for the welfare of the world, she assumed a stable form upon the earth;
touched, seen, or protected by her, she destroys even the greatest sins.
In the *Agastya-saṃhitā*:
"The daughter of Janaka is the beloved of Viṣṇu, the Lord of the three worlds, and likewise Tulasī is the sole purifier of all the worlds. (Hbhv_9.151)
Where there is a grove of Tulasī plants surrounded by hundreds of other flowers,
Rāghava himself shines there together with Sītā.
Even the area extending for a *krośa* in every direction around a grove of *tulasī* plants becomes a purifying place,
just like the water of the Gaṅgā.
O Lord of Sages, those who cast off their lives in the presence of the Tulasī plant do not suffer the torments of hell; they proceed to the supreme state.
Moreover:
O you whose wealth is austerity, those who behold [the deity] in the morning with undivided vision destroy, in that very instant, the sin committed during the day and night. (Hbhv 9.155)
In the Gāruḍa [Purāṇa]:
"O illustrious son of Vinatā, liberation has been granted by that person who has planted a grove of tulasī for the sake of living beings. (Hbhv 9.156)
O Lord of Birds, by him who has planted *tulasī* in a sacred grove, a forest, or a house,
the seven worlds have been established through his spoken truth.
Whoever should rest for even a moment in a grove of *tulasī* is liberated from the sins committed across ten million lifetimes; there is no doubt about this.
Whoever performs circumambulation while reciting the Thousand Names in a grove of *tulasī* daily shall obtain the fruit of ten thousand sacrifices. (Hbhv 9.159)
In the *Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya*:
Viṣṇu is ever-present in the grove of tulasī, longing [to see] whether some fortunate person might offer him even a single unblemished leaf. (Hbhv 9.160)
In the *Bṛhannāradīya*, within the section concerning the Gaṅgā, the name of the Gaṅgā is proclaimed as that which cuts through the evils of saṃsāra;
likewise, devotion to Tulasī is [proclaimed] in the work of Hari. (Hbhv 9.161)
Wherever there is a grove of *tulasī* plants and wherever there are lotus forests,
and wherever there is the recitation of the *Purāṇas*, there Hari is ever present.
In that very place, in the dialogue between Śrī Yama and Bhagīratha:
"O lord of men, I shall describe the fruit of the merit for those who plant *tulasī*; listen as I speak. (Hbhv 9.163)
Accompanied by seven crores of kinsmen on both the mother’s and the father’s side,
he who has attained Nārāyaṇa shall dwell for more than a hundred kalpas.

For as many blades of grass as one removes from the root of the *tulasī*, for that many instances of the killing of a Brahmin (*brahmahatyā*), it indeed severs them; of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv 9.165)
Whoever sprinkles even a mere handful of water upon the *tulasī* shall dwell together with Him who reclines upon the ocean of milk as long as the moon and stars endure. (Hbhv 9.166)
O King of kings, listen to the great fruit of merit for one who makes a fence of thorns or a wall of wood around a *tulasī* plant. (Hbhv 9.167)
O Lord, for as many days as the obstruction of the thorns remains,
for that long shall a yuga remain in the state of Brahmā, joined with the three families.
O Lord of Men, he who constructs a wall for Tulasī,
together with his three lineages, shall attain the same form as Viṣṇu.
Therefore, in that very same place, at the conclusion of the narrative of Yajñadhvaja, it is said:
"Service to Tulasī is difficult to obtain; association with the virtuous is difficult to obtain;
and devotion to Hari is difficult to obtain for those falling into the ocean of saṃsāra. (Hbhv 9.170)
Whatever fruit is obtained through well-performed sacrifices completed with excellent sacrificial fees,
that same fruit, multiplied ten millionfold, is gained by planting the beloved [tree] of Hari. (Hbhv 9.171)
Those who offer *tulasī* for the worship of the gods,
or plant it in a pure place, are said to possess an imperishable world.
O King, upon seeing a tulasī plant that has been planted by a man on the earth,
Yama becomes dejected of countenance and shall erase that record.
O Brahmin, he who utters the *tulasṛti* mantra three times a day from his mouth constantly obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows.

O best of birds, by him who has planted a *tulasī* plant, everything has been given, offered in sacrifice, recited as mantra, and performed as a *śrāddha* at Gayāśiras; and penance has been performed. (Hbhv 9.175)
Tulasī, when heard of, longed for, seen, planted, watered,
or bowed to, burns away all evil like the fire at the end of an eon.
That Vaiṣṇava who causes a grove of *tulasī* to be planted in a temple of Keśava attains an imperishable station together with his ancestors.
Elsewhere also it was said by Viṣṇu in the past: "Whoever performs a śrāddha for the ancestors in a grove of tulasī plants has, in effect, performed a śrāddha at Gayā. (Hbhv 9.178)
Upon seeing a dense grove of *tulasī*, one is liberated from sin;
O tiger among sages, in every way, even a killer of a Brahmin shall become a partaker of merit.
Furthermore, in the *Skānda Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Vasiṣṭha and Māndhātṛ, it is said:
"O King, O highly fortunate one, when the third lunar day of the bright fortnight is conjoined with Mercury and the Śravaṇa asterism, Tulasī is exceedingly merit-bestowing. (Hbhv_9.180)
Now, by way of a digression, the greatness of clay, tulasī, wood, and also of a leaf offered to Kṛṣṇa is being written. (Hbhv 9.181)
Now, regarding the majesty of *tulasī*, clay, wood, and so forth,
as stated in the *Skanda Purāṇa* in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada:
"That clay which has been touched by the roots of *tulasī* that have entered the earth..."
It should be known as equal to ten million sacred fords; it should be held with effort in one's home.
O best of the twice-born, in whichever house the earth from the root of a *tulasī* plant always remains upon the body, that person is no mere mortal; he is a deity. (Hbhv 9.183)
If one who has smeared himself with *tulasī* and clay should give up his life-breaths,
Yama would not be able to even look upon him, even though he were joined with hundreds of sins.
For those who apply the clay from the root of the *tulasī* plant to their heads,
their obstacles perish and the planets likewise become favorable.
O tiger among sages, wherever the earth, wood, or leaves of the *tulasī* plant remain in a dwelling, that place is indeed the immovable station of Viṣṇu.

Now, O best of the twice-born, the accomplishment of the *vṛtti* [is taught] right there for the sake of auspiciousness elsewhere, as well as for the purpose of destroying defects and for purification.
A wise person should bring earth adhering to the roots of the Tulasī plant.
Janārdana, being pleased with whoever indeed wears that root-clay upon his head, grants him the boons he desires.
In the *Bṛhannāradīya*, in the section concerning the Gaṅgā:
"A streak of clay originating from the root of a *tulasī* plant, produced from the footprints of a devotee of Hari, and arising from the Gaṅgā, leads one to the very form of Acyuta. (Hbhv_9.189)
In the Gāruḍa [Purāṇa]:
"In that house where there is a piece of Tulasī wood—whether dry or fresh—no sin whatsoever takes hold in that house during the Kali age. (Hbhv 9.190)
In the Śrī-Prahlāda-saṃhitā as well as in the Viṣṇu-dharmottara:
"Leaves, flowers, fruits, wood, bark, branches, sprouts, and shoots—all originating from the *tulasī*, as well as its roots, soil, and so forth, are purifying. (Hbhv 9.191)
For those brahmins who perform a fire sacrifice with a fire made from *tulasī* wood,
in every moment there arises merit equal to that produced by a hundred *agniṣṭoma* sacrifices.
Whoever cooks an offering with a fire of *tulasī* wood, that food offered to Keśava indeed becomes equal to Mount Meru. (Hbhv 9.193)
Those whose bodies are burned by the fire of *tulasī* wood shall never again return from the world of Viṣṇu in any way whatsoever. (Hbhv 9.194)
If one is seized by great sins, such as approaching those who should not be approached,
he is purified upon death by cremation with a fire of *tulasī* wood.
If one has not reached a sacred ford (tīrtha), nor performed the remembrance or chanting of Hari,
yet dies having been cremated with Tulasī wood, there is no rebirth.
If even a single piece of tulasī wood should be present in the midst of a heap of wood at the time of cremation, there shall be liberation even for one burdened by tens of millions of sins.
Those people by whom Janārdana has been propitiated throughout thousands of millions of births are consumed in this world by the fire of the wood of *tulasī*.
In the Agastya-saṃhitā:
"Whoever should diligently fashion a beautiful rosary and a necklace for the neck out of tulasī wood, that which has been made by him shall become inexhaustible. (Hbhv_9.199)
Now, regarding the greatness of wearing *tulasī* leaves,
as told in the *Skanda Purāṇa* in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada:
"He upon whose navel, mouth, head, or ears a leaf is placed..."
For one who constantly offers water from a *tulasī* plant, what need is there for sacred bathing places or sacrifices?
In that very same context, elsewhere it is said:
"By placing a *tulasī* leaf upon one's head, one destroys enemies, gains great merit, brings about prosperity, and eliminates disease; thus, one attains the Dharma. (Hbhv 9.201)
Whosoever in this world is a Vaiṣṇava, even if they follow false conduct or belong to no stage of life, purifies all the worlds by carrying *tulasī* upon their head. (Hbhv 9.202)
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, in the dialogue between Yama and Bhagīratha, it is said:
"O King of kings, for that man who constantly wears *tulasī* or even its wood upon his ear, there is no secondary offense (*upapātaka*). (Hbhv 9.203)
In the *Haribhaktisudhodaya*, it is said to the messengers of Yama regarding a Vaiṣṇava brāhmaṇa:
"We do not know why [we have been sent]; for Hari is indeed dear to Tulasī. He follows even one who is departing while protecting him with Tulasī in his hand. (Hbhv 9.204)
And in another ancient text:
"He who, devoted to Viṣṇu, places a *tulasī* leaf upon his head and performs religious duties, obtains imperishable fruit. (Hbhv 9.205)
In the Garuḍa Purāṇa:
"Upon seeing a tulasī leaf on the face, the head, or the ears, the Sun-god performs the cleansing of that person's misdeeds. (Hbhv_9.206)
O son of Vinatā, if one should consume *tulasī* three times a day, it is superior;
it effects purification of the body even without performing a hundred *cāndrāyaṇa* fasts.
In the *Skanda Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Śrī Vasiṣṭha and Mandhātṛ, it is said:
"Purification of the body resulting from the Cāndrāyaṇa, the Taptakṛcchra, the Brahmakūrca, or the drinking of Kuśa-water is surpassed by the consumption of Tulasī leaves. (Hbhv 9.208)
Likewise, it is well known that even a sinner, by eating the leaves of the *tulasī* plant while devoid of [evil] intent, attained a good rebirth. (Hbhv 9.209)

And likewise, in the Skanda Purāṇa, as related by Śrī Brahmā to Nārada at the conclusion of the story of the hunter (lubdhaka-upākhyāna) concerning the extraction of the nectar-lake (amṛta-saroddhara), there is this speech of the messenger of Viṣṇu to the messengers of Yama:
"O highly fortunate one, while the ocean of milk was being churned, Tulasī, whose form is according to her desire, was produced for the sake of uplifting the world. (Hbhv_9.210)
By the mere remembrance, sight, or even the chanting of her name, sins go to destruction; how much more so from the worship of Viṣṇu! (Hbhv 9.211)
Having abandoned flowers made of gold and the auspicious lotus-gems made of rubies, as well as other varieties of jewels, he instead grasps a leaf of *tulasī*. (Hbhv 9.212)
Even though the leaf produced from the *tulasī* was eaten by a hunter, he subsequently met his end, and his body was reduced to ashes. (Hbhv 9.213)
Just as the *nṛmāṃsa* (human flesh), whether white or black, brings about the destruction of all sins,
so too the leaf of the *tulasī* plant, when consumed, grants all desires.
Just as a fire that has gained strength consumes a forest and the like, so does the consumed leaf of *tulasī* burn away sin. (Hbhv 9.215)
Just as a man who is constantly devoted to devotion burns away his sin,
so too does the consumption of *tulasī* burn away that very accumulation of evil.
The merit arising from consuming *tulasī* leaves is not equaled by a thousand *cāndrāyaṇa* fasts nor by a hundred sacrifices to the ancestors.
Having committed thousands of sins in the earlier part of his life, a person may be liberated by consuming *tulasī*; this was heard from Hari in the past.
The messengers of Yama remain tormenting embodied beings with their sins for as long as a *tulasī* leaf does not rest upon their mouth or their head. (Hbhv 9.219)
The *dhātrī* and *tulasī*, which arose from the nectar of immortality and are beloved by Viṣṇu—when remembered, praised, meditated upon, or consumed, they grant all desires. (Hbhv 9.220)
In that very place, regarding Yama, the Blessed One spoke these words:
"If the *dhātrī* fruit and *tulasī* should be present in the mouth, on the head, or on the body at the time of death, there is indeed no miserable rebirth for such a person. (Hbhv 9.221)
Even if one is joined with great sins and has never earned merit anywhere, liberation is nevertheless seen if *tulasī* has been eaten. (Hbhv 9.222)
The hunter, having consumed a leaf of *tulasī* with his own body, has surely attained my state after bringing about the destruction of his previous [karmic] tendencies. (Hbhv 9.223)
And in another Purāṇa it is said:
"O best of Brahmins, if one fasts for twelve pure days and then consumes a leaf of *tulasī* on the following day, one obtains the merit of eight horse-sacrifices. (Hbhv 9.224)
In the same way, one who is protected by the touch of *tulasī* and the discus of Kṛṣṇa is known as a "kinsman of Brahman" (*brahmabandhu*) in the *Haribhaktisudhodaya*. (Hbhv 9.225)
Therefore it has been said:
"What is the wonder in this? Whether a leaf of Tulasī has fallen or water has fallen, [it is sacred] except for urine."
"Even the mud from the basin at the root of the Lord of the Ascendant (Viṣṇu) leads to the destruction of all sins. Thus,
if such is the majesty of a single leaf of the venerable Tulasī;
Nevertheless, that [offering] should not be accepted by Vaiṣṇavas unless it has been dedicated to Kṛṣṇa.
Because of the great fondness for *tulasī*, now the majesty of the *dhātrī* tree is being written down, as it arises in connection with the *tulasī* in all instances. (Hbhv 9.228)
Now, regarding the majesty of the *dhātrī* tree, in the *Skanda Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada:
"The man who, taking refuge in the shade of a *dhātrī* tree, worships the Discus-handed Lord (Viṣṇu), obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice for every flower [offered]. (Hbhv 9.229)
In that very place, it is further stated:
"O Sage, if one offers a funeral cake (piṇḍa) while touching the shadow of Dhātrī, the ancestors attain liberation through the grace of Mādhava. (Hbhv 9.230)
O best of sages, that great soul who wears the *dhātrī* fruit upon his head, his nose, his mouth, and indeed his body, is very difficult to find.
A person whose body is smeared with *dhātrī* fruit, adorned with *dhātrī* fruit, and who takes *dhātrī* fruit as food, becomes Nārāyaṇa. (Hbhv 9.232)
O Sage, whatever Vaiṣṇava in this world wears the dhātrī fruit becomes dear to the gods; what then need be said of human beings?
Any Vaiṣṇava in this world, even if he is of false conduct or evil intent,
purifies all the worlds when he carries a leaf from the dhātrī tree.
To him who constantly carries *dhātrī* fruits in the hollow of his joined palms,
the god Nārāyaṇa grants a single boon.
One should occasionally eat the fruit of the *dhātrī* from the hollow of one's cupped hands;
through the grace of the Wielder of the Discus, one attains fame and prosperity. (Hbhv 9.236)
The fruit of the *dhātrī*, *tulasī*, and clay originating from Dvārakā—his life is truly fruitful in whose house these three are found. (Hbhv 9.237)
Whoever drinks [water] mixed with dhātrī fruits and scented with tulasī leaves,
or carries it [on their person], shall obtain the fruit of ten million holy fords (tīrthas).
O best of Brahmins, in whatever house there may be water scented with *tulasī* leaves and *dhātrī* fruits, what need is there for cows to be recited? (Hbhv 9.239)
For one who has in their home an offering of *tulasī* leaves and the fruit of the *dhātrī* tree, as well as this Vaiṣṇava armor (*kavaca*), all sins are destroyed. (Hbhv 9.240)
And in the *Brahma-purāṇa* it is said:
"If the fruits of the *dhātrī* and *tulasī* should be present at the time of death, whether in the mouth, on the head, or on the body, there is indeed no sin for him. (Hbhv 9.241)

Having performed the worship of the Blessed One, one should not perform a ritual bath at a sacred ford (tīrtha), nor [engage in impurity] through contact with those who should not be touched in a temple or similar place. (Hbhv 9.242)
Now, regarding the specific time for bathing,
the *Smṛtyarthasāra* states:
"One should not bathe during a festival, at a sacred ford (*tīrtha*), or immediately after performing an auspicious rite."
Having followed after his friends and kinsmen, and having honored his chosen deity.
And in the Viṣṇu-smṛti:
"Having touched even a Caṇḍāla or an outcast who has come to the temple of Viṣṇu for the purpose of serving Viṣṇu, one should not perform a ritual bath. (Hbhv 9.244)
In processions of the gods, at weddings, during sacrificial implements, and at all festivals, there is no concern regarding contact with the untouchable. (Hbhv 9.245)
Having thus worshipped Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the morning immediately thereafter, a twice-born man—and a Brahmin especially—should study the scriptures according to his ability. (Hbhv 9.246)
As it has been said: "The Śruti and Smṛti are declared to be the two eyes of the Brahmins; one who lacks one is called 'one-eyed,' but one who lacks both is declared to be 'blind. (Hbhv 9.247)
Furthermore, in the *Kūrma Purāṇa* as cited by Vyāsa:
"That twice-born man who exerts effort elsewhere without relying upon the Śruti is utterly deluded; he is outside the Veda and should not be conversed with by the twice-born. (Hbhv 9.248)
A twice-born man should not be satisfied with the mere path of the Vedas;
for one who is devoid of the prescribed conduct sinks like a cow in the mud. (Hbhv 9.249)

"He who, having memorized the Veda according to rule, does not investigate the meaning of the Veda, is like a blind man and is equal to a Śūdra; he does not attain the true nature of the categories. (Hbhv 9.250).
Therefore, the learned Vaiṣṇava, having first memorized [the texts] daily with steadfastness, should then teach them.
And having offered that to Kṛṣṇa, one should strive for one's own livelihood.
And while living in this manner, one should approach virtuous people and listen to their excellent discourse.
In the seventh book [of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 7.11.18–20]:
"One may live by means of *ṛta* and *amṛta*, or by *mṛta* and *pramṛta*, or even by *satya* and *anṛta*; but never by one's own [unrighteous] livelihood. (Hbhv 9.253)
Gleaning grains is declared to be *ṛta*; what is obtained unasked is *amṛta*. Begging constantly is *mṛta*, while agriculture is remembered as *pramṛta*. (Hbhv 9.254)
Trade consists of both truth and falsehood; it is the dog-like livelihood of serving base men.
The pursuit of one's own material worlds for the sake of securing a livelihood is utterly censured by the virtuous, especially in the case of a Vaiṣṇava. (Hbhv 9.256)
Thus it has been said:
"Those who have described service as the 'dog's livelihood' have not spoken correctly;
for where is the dog that wanders at will, and where is the servant whose life is one of constant distortion? (Hbhv 9.257)
"Having eaten the food of those evil-minded lowest of the twice-born who live by performing the five *kṛtyas* for themselves, one should perform the *cāndrāyaṇa* penance. (Hbhv 9.258).
And when a livelihood through pure means is not established, one may eat the food of the Śūdra class.
In the same way, the wise person should understand from the scriptures what is to be grasped and what is not to be grasped.
And regarding the white mode of livelihood (*śukla-vṛtti*),
it is stated in the third section of the *Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"That which is obtained through receiving gifts, from a sacrificer, or likewise from a disciple..."
For a Brahmin, that white [karma] performed for those endowed with virtues is traditionally remembered as being of three kinds.
Wealth acquired from assistance in war, from fines, and from legal proceedings is declared to be the threefold "pure" wealth of a Kṣatriya. (Hbhv 9.261)
For the Vaiśyas, agriculture, trade, and cattle-rearing are declared to be pure;
for the Śūdra, that which is obtained through service to the twice-born is considered pure. (Hbhv 9.262)
Inheritance received in succession, what has been acquired together with one's wife, and all wealth that is pure—these are declared to belong to all [heirs] without distinction. (Hbhv 9.263)
Now, regarding what may and may not be accepted as food, it is stated in that very same *Kūrma Purāṇa*: "If a Brahmin, out of delusion or desire, should eat the food of a Śūdra..."
He who eats when there is no cause for distress does not go to a Śūdra womb.
For all the evil deeds of a person are established in their food; whoever eats another's food eats that person's transgression. (Hbhv 9.265)
A partner in business, a family friend, one's own cowherd, and a barber—
these among Śūdras are those whose food may be eaten by the wise after giving them a small gift.
Milk-rice cooked with oil, cow's milk, flour, oil-cake, and likewise oil—these may be accepted from a Śūdra. (Hbhv 9.267)
Aśvaghoṣa says:
One may eat cow’s milk, flour-meal, oil-cakes, and even cakes made with milk from a Śūdra. (Hbhv 9.268)
In the Atri-smṛti:
"He who eats the food of his own daughter eats the filth of the earth;
having eaten in the palace of a king, he is born as a worm in excrement. (Hbhv 9.269)

A slave, a barber, a cowherd, a family friend, and one who shares half his meal—these are those whose food may be eaten among the Śūdra class; likewise, one who has surrendered himself [to the teacher]. (Hbhv 9.270)
Honey, water, fruit, roots, firewood, and the gift of fearlessness—these, when offered, should be accepted even from a person of low status. (Hbhv 9.271)

Grain fallen upon a field of chaff, water from wells and cisterns, and milk found in a cow-pen—these are to be accepted even though they come from sources that are not normally acceptable. (Hbhv 9.272)
One should not accept drink, milk-rice, solid food, clarified butter, or salt when offered directly by hand; such a person is equal to those who eat the flesh of cows. (Hbhv 9.273)
In the *Manu-smṛti*:
"Even though the ocean and rock salt are directly perceived and most wonderful, the prohibition [of consuming them] refers to other [types]. (Hbhv_9.274)
If food is served in an iron vessel, the eater consumes it as if it were equal to excrement, and the giver shall go to hell. (Hbhv 9.275)
One should treat Brahmins who are cattle-herders, merchants, artisans, actors, those living abroad, or usurers just as one would Śūdras. (Hbhv 9.276)
And in that very same passage of the *Kūrma Purāṇa*:
"O Brahmin, a wise man should openly offer grass, wood, fruit, or flowers solely for the sake of dharma to Hari; otherwise, he would become fallen. (Hbhv 9.277)

O Brahmin, those who stand on the road seeking to satisfy hunger, and who know the Dharma, may take a handful of sesame, mung beans, barley, or rice; it is not otherwise—this is the established rule. (Hbhv 9.278)
Indeed, the food of Vaiṣṇavas should always be eaten and requested by Vaiṣṇavas;
however, the food of non-Vaiṣṇavas must be avoided like impure matter. (Hbhv 9.279)
And so it is stated in the *Pādmapurāṇa*, in the dialogue between Devadūta and Vikuṇḍala:
"A wise person should diligently request food from a Vaiṣṇava for the sake of purifying all sins; in the absence of such food, he should drink water. (Hbhv_9.280)
One who is burdened with great sins should go to the temple of a Vaiṣṇava;
he should beg for food as nectar, or in its absence, drink water. (Hbhv 9.281)
In the Viṣṇu-smṛti:
"The food of one learned in the Vedas, the food of a Vaiṣṇava, and the remains of an oblation—these purify sin down to the very nails, just as fire in husks purifies gold. (Hbhv 9.282)
In the *Skānda Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Bhagīratha:
"The food of a devotee of the Lord is pure; the water of Bhagīrathī is pure;
the mind intent on Viṣṇu is pure; and the vow of Ekādaśī is pure. (Hbhv 9.283)

Having eaten or drunk in the house of one who is not a Vaiṣṇava, whether knowingly or otherwise, purification is declared to be the Cāndrāyaṇa penance; his sacrificial rites and charitable works are always rendered fruitless.
And in the words of Śrī Prahlāda:
"O Lord of the Daityas, the food of one in whose house an image of Keśava does not reside must never be eaten; it is remembered as equal to forbidden food. (Hbhv 9.285)
O Lord, some who are skillful even at this time instruct one who is free from worldly livelihood, full of faith in recitation, and confident, to perform the recitation. (Hbhv_9.286)
Now, regarding the midday duties:
before bathing at midday, one should perform the midday rites after having personally procured flowers and other necessities, or having had them prepared by a servant or others. (Hbhv 9.287)
And if one is unable to bathe, one should perform the ritual bath at midday according to the mantras as prescribed by the Teacher;
if capable, one should perform the worship of the Blessed One as previously described.
Now, regarding the procedure for the Vaiṣṇava-Vaiśvadeva and other rites:
thereafter, the Vaiṣṇava should perform the divine rites such as the Vaiśvadeva, as well as the ancestral rites (paitra), using only this pure food offered to Kṛṣṇa. (Hbhv 9.289)
Thus it has been said: "In the sixth division of the day, one should perform the five great sacrifices (mahāmakha):
the sacrifice to the gods (daiva) should be performed by means of oblation (homa), while that to the spirits (bhauta) is by means of offering food (balidāna). (Hbhv 9.290)
The paternal [debt] is discharged by the gift of food to Brahmins, or by a paternal *bali* offering, or by the giving of some food, or by libations (*tarpaṇa*); thus it is fourfold.
The sacrifice to men (nṛ-yajña) is performed through the hospitable reception of guests with water and the utterance of "hanta";
the sacrifice to Brahman (brahma-yajña) is performed by the chanting of the Vedas or by the recitation of Purāṇas. (Hbhv 9.292)
Regarding its permanence, it is stated in the *Kūrma Purāṇa*:
"But that best of the twice-born who, being a twice-born man, does not perform the five great sacrifices..."
If that extremely deluded soul eats [it], he goes to the womb of an animal.
Now, regarding the procedure for the Vaiṣṇava Śrāddha:
on the day the Śrāddha is due, one should first offer food to the Blessed One; then, with that very remnant, the devotee of the Lord should perform the Śrāddha. (Hbhv 9.294)
And as it is stated in the Smṛti:

"The food intended for the ancestors must not be given to householders, those who maintain the sacred fires, children, deities, ascetics, and students, as long as the funeral rice-balls (piṇḍas) have not been offered. (Hbhv 9.295)
A general statement is certainly sublated by a multitude of specific statements contained within the Śruti, Smṛti, Purāṇas, and so forth. (Hbhv 9.296)
And so it is stated in the *Padma-purāṇa*:
"One should worship other deities with food offered to Viṣṇu;
that same food should also be given to the ancestors, for that conduces to infinity. (Hbhv 9.297)
In the *Mokṣadharma*, as spoken by Nārada:
"Adopting the Sātvata rite that had issued from the mouth of the ancient Sun, he worshipped the Lord of Gods, and with what remained from that, [he worshipped] the Grandfathers. (Hbhv 9.298)
In the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa:
"He who, at the time of a śrāddha, devotedly offers the remains of what has been eaten by Hari to the ancestors and the deities..."
By those very morsels mixed with *tulasī*,
the ancestors remain well-satisfied for ten million kalpas.
In the Skanda-purāṇa:
"Whatever is offered to Viṣṇu with the gods and ancestors in view—one should indeed make the gift for them in that very same manner. (Hbhv 9.300)
Indeed, by that very unguent which has adhered to the body of Mukunda, the Brahmins attain incomparable satisfaction when it serves as their ointment. (Hbhv 9.301)
A lump [of food] should be made with sandalwood for the satisfaction of the ancestors;
through this, the satisfaction of both the gods and the ancestors becomes inexhaustible.
When this has been done, there should be no doubt whatsoever regarding the *mahāpala*. (Hbhv 9.303)
In that very same Śrī Puruṣottama-khaṇḍa:
"If food intended for a śrāddha is looked upon by outcasts or others at the time of the rite, one should sprinkle it with water mixed with a tulasī leaf. (Hbhv 9.304)
That food mixed with the *naivedya* offering of Viṣṇu attains purity;
therefore, the remainder of Viṣṇu’s *naivedya* should be given to the twice-born, and especially so in the *piṇḍa* rite for one desiring the satisfaction of the ancestors. (Hbhv 9.305)
In that very same [text], in the dialogue between Śrī Brahmā and Nārada:
"O great sage, those men who have performed worship of Keśava for the sake of their ancestors abandon the suffering of hell and attain liberation. (Hbhv_9.306)
Blessed are those men in the world, especially in the Kali age,
O Sage, who constantly perform the worship of Hari for the sake of their ancestors.
O Sage, what is the use of offering many funeral cakes through śrāddha rites at Gayā and elsewhere,
when Hari is worshipped with devotion day after day for the sake of one's ancestors?
O best of sages, whichever person for whose sake the worship of Hari is performed, He shall deliver from dwelling in hell and lead them to the supreme state. (Hbhv 9.309)
O Nārada, he who gives a dwelling place for Hari with his ancestors in mind—O twice-born one, whatever is to be done for the ancestors has indeed been performed by him. (Hbhv 9.310)
And in the Śruti it is said:
"Nārāyaṇa alone existed in the beginning,
not Brahmā."
Not only these two, Heaven and Earth,
but all the gods and all the ancestors [are present].
All human beings eat what is eaten by Viṣṇu, they smell what is smelled by Viṣṇu,
and they drink what is drunk by Viṣṇu.
"Therefore, those who have destroyed [their vows] should eat what has been brought by Viṣṇu.
For this very reason, it was said by the Blessed One in the *Viṣṇudharma*:
"One should offer the most excellent food, dedicated to Me, as an oblation to the ancestors."
Living beings are always satisfied by consuming food offered to me.
Therefore, with every effort, that which has been offered to me should be given;
it is for me who dwells in the heart, and especially for the ancestors.
Furthermore, it is stated elsewhere in that very same work:

"Whatever food, whether solid or soft, is not first offered to the primary recipient, it should not be given to the ancestors or the gods; for from such an act, there would arise the need for expiation. (Hbhv 9.314)
In heaven and other realms, the Blessed Lord Hari was declared by the gods to be the first enjoyer;
thereafter, the gods were established by him as the partakers of sacrificial portions.
In the *Skanda Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya and Bhagīratha:

"If a Brahmin, considering a Vaiṣṇava who is devoid of learning to be a fool, should offer the *śrāddha* to him instead of to those who know the Vedas, that *śrāddha* becomes one belonging to the Rākṣasas. (Hbhv 9.316)
Even if one eats only a single morsel of food and takes only a single mouthful of water, that food is equal to Mount Meru and that water is like the ocean. (Hbhv 9.317)
In the *Brahmapurāṇa*, the word of Śrī Brahmā says:
"Keśava himself, together with the ancestors, eats the food of that householder in whose home a Brahmin with a body marked by the conch-shell (*śaṅkhāścitatanu*) partakes. (Hbhv 9.318)
And Smṛti says:
"Just as nectar in a vessel that once held liquor perishes in an instant, so too does a Śrāddha bereft of the Cakrāṅka; thus spoke Śātātapa. (Hbhv 9.319)
Furthermore, in the *Śrī Viṣṇu Rahasya*:
"If a man, out of delusion, places one dear to Hari in another's row, that lowest of men, a defiler of the row, shall fall into a terrible hell. (Hbhv 9.320)
Now, that which is forbidden for offering to the Blessed One, yet is offered to another, is indeed called "leftover" (ucchiṣṭa).
Therefore, one should not offer it to the Blessed One under any circumstances whatsoever. (Hbhv 9.321)
And likewise, in the eleventh book of the *Śrī-Bhāgavata*, in the words of the Blessed One (BhP 11.11.40):
"Even if it were offered, one should not employ even a glance at my form. (Hbhv_9.322)
In the Nāradīya:
"If one should offer the remains of the ancestral oblation to Hari, the Supreme Self, his ancestors become merely givers of seed and partakers of suffering. (Hbhv 9.323)
In the *Viṣṇudharma*, it is said that one should offer the remains of the sacrificial oblation (*havis*) to Hari; this becomes inexhaustible for the ancestors.
However, one must never offer the remains of the ancestors to Hari, the supreme teacher of Brahmā and the others. (Hbhv 9.324)
And elsewhere it is said:
"The ancestors such as Dakṣa and others are the servants, and the gods such as Indra and others are the masters;
therefore, one should never offer to Viṣṇu what remains from those [other] devotees. (Hbhv 9.325)
Having thus performed the necessary rites and having distributed [the food] among the Vaiṣṇavas,
one should eat the venerable and greatly blessed food together with one's kinsmen.
And so it is said in the *Prahlāda-pañcarātra*:

"Deceiving those dull-witted by means of wealth and other such things while remaining established in his own nature, one should offer the various articles of food offered to Hari to the Vaiṣṇavas. (Hbhv 9.327)
For this very reason, in the Vaiṣṇava Tantra it is said:

"A wise person should never give even a little of what has been offered to Hari to those who are not devotees or to those who are pierced by thorns [of sin]; for by giving it, he would go to hell. (Hbhv 9.328)
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"O fortunate one, Keśava is pleased with that person who does not offer to a non-Vaiṣṇava the remains of flowers (nirmālya) or the food offering (naivedya) presented to the deity. (Hbhv_9.329)
A Vaiṣṇava should not eat under any circumstances without having performed the worship of Kṛṣṇa,
nor indeed should he eat anything without first offering it to Govinda.
Now, regarding the faults of eating apart from worship,
the *Śrī Kūrma Purāṇa* states:
"By those devoid of dharma who have eaten without having worshipped Govinda..."
Food is equal to the excrement of a dog, and human flesh is equal to liquor.
Furthermore:
"Moreover, he who, out of delusion or laziness, eats without having performed the worship of the deities, goes to hell and is born here among pigs. (Hbhv 9.332)
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"One should worship Hari once, twice, or thrice a day;
a man who eats without having worshipped him shall go to the hells. (Hbhv_9.333)
And in the Nāradīya it is said:
"The wise have declared that the worship of Viṣṇu should be performed in the morning, at midday, and in the evening.
If one is unable to perform it in such detail, one should worship Keśava in the morning alone. (Hbhv 9.334)
At midday and likewise in the evening, one should offer even a handful of flowers;
or at midday, one may worship Hari either extensively or in brief.
One should eat only after having shared the meal; otherwise, one would go to hell.
Now follows the prohibition against enjoying what has not been offered,
as stated in the *Hayaśīrṣa-pañcarātra*:
"One should never eat without having first worshipped the Blessed Lord Janārdana."
One should not eat that oneself which one has not first offered to Viṣṇu.
In the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa:
"One should not eat leaves, flowers, fruits, water, food, drink, or medicine—whatever has been prepared for one's sustenance—without first having offered it. (Hbhv 9.338)
A man who eats without having offered [food] becomes subject to penance;
therefore, one should always eat only after having offered everything to Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 9.339)
In the *Pādmapurāṇa*, in the dialogue between Gautama and Ambarīṣa:
"O Ambarīṣa, one who eats in his own home food that has been cooked for himself but which has not been offered to Hari, remains in hell for seven kalpas. (Hbhv_9.340)

In that very same section, the Uttara-kāṇḍa, in the dialogue between Śiva and Umā (6.253.112): "The food of those who are not Vaiṣṇavas, as well as that of the fallen, and likewise that which has not been offered to Viṣṇu, becomes like the flesh of a dog. (Hbhv_9.341)
In the Viṣṇu-smṛti:
"But he who eats without having offered [food] to Hari, the Supreme Self, his ancestors sink into hell for eternal years. (Hbhv_9.342)
Therefore, in the dialogue between Gautama and Ambarīṣa:
"O Ambarīṣa, having offered new clothing, fruit, food, juices, and so forth, which have been enjoyed by Viṣṇu, they should indeed always be used by Vaiṣṇavas. (Hbhv 9.343)
In the *Viṣṇudharma* and the *Agni Purāṇa*:
"Having offered perfumes, food, excellent edibles, garlands, garments, and ornaments to the God of gods, they partake of what remains thereof. (Hbhv_9.344)
In the Gāruḍa Purāṇa:
"One should daily drink the water from the feet [of the Lord] and eat the food offering (naivedya) of Hari;
the remains should be worn upon the head—such is the instruction of the Vedas. (Hbhv 9.345)
In the sixth book, in the context of the *puṃsavana* vow [BhP 6.19.20]:
"Having dismissed the deity to its own abode, one should eat that which was first offered for the sake of self-purification and for the accomplishment of all desired aims. (Hbhv_9.346)
And in the eighth book, in the context of the milk-vow, [it is said]:
"One should give what has been offered to His devotee, or one may eat it oneself. (BhP 8.16.42) [Hbhv 9.347]
In the Gautamīya Tantra,
one should worship Hari daily with the white offerings (śuklopacāra);
having offered food to Kṛṣṇa according to the rules, one should eat it oneself.
Alternatively, if it is available, one should offer it with devotion to a Sātvata.

In the autumn of his sovereignty, the Lord—who destroys the momentary existence of those devoted to him—bestows upon his own household mindfulness, service, and the offering of his own food as a gift; the fruit of this is difficult even for Indra and the other gods to obtain. (Hbhv 9.349)
Now, the procedure for consuming the food offering (naivedya):
having seen the food of great grace (mahā-prasāda), one should bow to it and consecrate it seven times with the name of one's chosen deity or with the root mantra. (Hbhv 9.350)

Having set aside the portion for Dharmarāja and the others, having drunk the nectar of the *śrī* syllable, and having cast the *tulasī* leaf into it, one should recite these verses in Sanskrit: Hbhv_9.351.
For we are eaters of the remnants of that Hari, whose leavings even the stainless sages beginning with Brahmā, as well as the Siddhas and others, desire.
Moreover:
We are the eaters of the remnants of that Lord Kṛṣṇa, by whose name the masses of great sins are destroyed. (Hbhv 9.353)
We are the eaters of the remnants of that performer of wondrous deeds,
who by his childhood play struck down those various Pūtanās.
In the eleventh book [of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 11.6.46]:
"Adorned with the garlands, perfumes, garments, and ornaments enjoyed by You, and eating Your remnants, may we, as Your servants, conquer Your Māyā. (Hbhv 9.355)
Having first uttered "I spread the under-layer of nectar" according to the rule,
and having offered the five oblations to the vital breaths (prāṇa), they should eat in the presence of the Lord.
In the *Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Aurva and Sagara [ViP 3.11.77, 79–80, 82–3, 86–91, 95–6, 98], it is said:
"But one who has a hand full of excellent jewels should eat while remaining self-controlled and pure. (Hbhv 9.357)
O Lord of Men, one should possess the fragrance of merit and wear excellent garlands;
O Great King, one should not wear but a single garment, nor have hands and feet that are wet. (Hbhv 9.358)
With a pure face and joyful, one should eat facing the east or the north; a person should not eat with his face turned toward the intermediate directions, nor with a distracted mind. (Hbhv 9.359)
Having given food to his hungry disciples and likewise to householders,
the twice-born man should eat without anger from a recommended and pure vessel.
O Lord of Men, a person should not eat from a vessel placed on a seat, nor in an improper place,
nor at an improper time, nor when it is excessively crowded; having first offered a portion to the fire,
one should not eat without leaving a remainder, O Lord of the World, except in the case of [specific] persons.
A person possessed of discernment, becoming absorbed in that [practice], should eat honey, water, curd, ghee, and roasted flour;
however, he should first consume the sweet taste.
A person should first eat salty, sour, and sweet [flavors], then those that are pungent, bitter, and so forth;
first one should consume liquids, and in the middle, solid food.
Furthermore, even when one is weak or ill, one does not abandon the five morsels of food; that great silence is for the sake of nourishing the vital breaths.
Having eaten properly and then performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), facing either east or north,
one should again sip water as prescribed after washing the five parts [of the hands] from the base.
But a person who is healthy and of tranquil mind, having taken up his seat,
should perform the recollection of those deities who have not been worshipped.
May Agasti, Agni, and the submarine fire digest the food I have eaten without exception;
and may there be for me well-being arising from its transformation.
May they grant it, and may there be freedom from disease in my body.
Just as the Lord Viṣṇu alone is the sustainer of all senses, bodies, and embodied beings, being their primary essence—
by that truth, may this entire food be consumed.
May this thorough understanding of mine grant me health.
Having recited this and rubbed his own abdomen with his own hand, he should, free from sloth, perform those actions that grant ease without exertion. (Hbhv 9.369)
In the Kūrma Purāṇa, as spoken by Vyāsa:
"One should eat food facing either the east or toward the sun, seated on a prepared seat with the feet placed upon the ground. (Hbhv 9.370)
One who eats facing east gains long life; facing south, one gains fame;
facing west, one attains prosperity; and facing north, one eats according to the cosmic order (ṛta).
One should eat while the five [limbs] are still moist and having placed the vessel upon the ground;
Prajāpati Manu has declared that this is equal to fasting.
Having washed his feet and hands in a clean, plastered place,
and having sipped water with a moist face and free from anger, he should eat while possessing the five-fold moisture.
Having surrounded the food with water while reciting the Mahāvyāhṛtis, one should perform the ritual of *apośāna*, [reciting] "the spreading of nectar" (*amṛtopastaraṇam asi*). (Hbhv 9.374)
Then, having offered an oblation to Prāṇa joined with the *svāhā* and the *praṇava*,
he should thereafter offer one to Apāna, and immediately after that to Vyāna.

Then, having understood the reality of these, O twice-born ones, one should perform the offering for the sake of *udāna* and the fifth [offering] for the sake of *samāna*, within the self. (Hbhv 9.376)
Having meditated with a mind focused on the deity, the Self who is indeed Prajāpati, one should eat the remaining food as desired, accompanied by condiments. (Hbhv 9.377)
Having placed the lid of immortality above, one should drink the waters.
Furthermore, in that same [text]:
"Whatever one eats with the head covered, whatever one eats facing the intermediate directions, and whatever one eats while wearing shoes—one should know all that to be demonic. (Hbhv 9.379)
Not at midnight, nor at midday; not when naked, nor while wearing wet clothes;
nor while seated on a broken seat, nor even while standing in a vehicle.
One should not eat from a broken vessel, nor on the ground, nor from one's hands;
excessive eating is detrimental to health, longevity, and heaven; it is non-meritorious and despised by the world, therefore one should avoid it. (Hbhv 9.381)
Furthermore:
One should not lift up water with the left hand, nor drink it from the mouth.
In the Viṣṇu-smṛti:
"If water from the mouth falls into a vessel while one is drinking, that food becomes unfit to be eaten; having consumed it, one should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa penance. (Hbhv_9.383)
In the Mārkaṇḍeya [Purāṇa]:
"A wise man, whose mind is always fixed on the inner self while eating food, should not cause the food to increase through faults, except in the case of a physical ailment. (Hbhv 9.384)
And elsewhere it is said:
"One should eat with water other than that from the hand, and drink from anything other than a vessel;
having set aside the right hand, one should place the *nṛ* syllable in the left."
That food and drink would become unfit for consumption, equal to liquor.
For one who is satisfied should give that food, and the remainder for the satisfaction of the destitute.
Having sipped water correctly, one should pour water onto the thumb of the right hand.

Then, having recollected his cherished deity who bestows nourishment, being surrounded by his nearby, disciplined disciples, he should recite the mantras of the Lord of Food (*annapati*), beginning with:
"O Lord of Food, give us food" (*annapate 'nnasya no dehi*). (Hbhv_9.388) etc.
Then one should consume betel leaf as the grace (*prasāda*) of the Lord of the Cowherds;
together with learned and beloved ones, one should recite the divine, auspicious name of the Blessed One. (Hbhv 9.389)
Now, regarding the greatness of the food offering (*naivedya*), it is stated in the *Vārāha-purāṇa*:
"He who, having performed my very worship, attains there the highest perfection..."
He eats the remaining food with tranquility; what indeed could be more blissful than that?
In the Skanda Purāṇa:
"He who, having partaken of your offering, serves the Lord of Sacrifice (Yajñapuruṣa), has certainly served the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) with great intelligence. (Hbhv 9.391)
Furthermore, in that very same place:
"The water from the conch is more excellent than the best of holy fords; the water from the washing of the feet is weightier than the multitude of holy fords."
The remnant of the food offering possesses the merit of ten million sacrifices;
the remnant of the floral offerings is equal to the merit of vows and gifts.
Whoever daily eats the remains of the food offering mixed with *tulasī* leaves, especially sprinkled with the water from [the Lord's] feet, in the presence of Murāri;
One obtains the merit of ten million times ten thousand sacrifices.
In the Kali age, the fruit that is proclaimed for those who fast for six months is obtained by those who eat the remains of Viṣṇu’s food offering.
Furthermore, in that [text] regarding the majesty of the Śālagrāma stone:
"He who with devotion eats the food offering (naivedya) presented to the Śālagrāma stone obtains the fruit of ten million sacrifices a hundred thousand times over. (Hbhv 9.395)
Brahmins, householders, forest-dwellers, and mendicants should partake of the food offered to Viṣṇu; no hesitation should be made in this matter.
Having consumed the food offering (naivedya) of another deity, a twice-born man should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa penance;
having consumed the food offering of Keśava, he obtains the fruit of ten million sacrifices.
In that very same work, in the dialogue between Śrī Brahmā and Nārada, it is said:
"The fruit that is surely obtained by thousands of Agniṣṭoma sacrifices and even hundreds of Vājapeya sacrifices is attained simply by eating the food offering (naivedya) of Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 9.398)
He in whose heart is the form of Hari, on whose mouth His name, in whose stomach His food offering,
and on whose head the water from His feet and the remains of His flowers— that person is Acyuta Himself.
Furthermore:
"The food offering (naivedya) to Viṣṇu is declared purifying by the gods, Siddhas, and Ṛṣis;
having eaten the food offering of another deity, one should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa penance. (Hbhv 9.400)
Whatever merit is gained through ten million sacrifices or through ten million months of fasting,
that fruit is obtained by men from eating the food offering (naivedya) of Viṣṇu.

The dust of the tulasī plant, the consumption of the food offering (naivedya), and the wearing of the remains of the offering (nirmālya)—by whomsoever these are used, they destroy even the greatest sins. (Hbhv 9.402)
In the *Bṛhad-Viṣṇu-Purāṇa*:
"Whatever food, drink, and so forth is offered as an oblation (*naivedya*) to the Lord of the Universe is indeed changeless like Brahman; for as is Viṣṇu, so too is that. (Hbhv 9.403)
Those twice-born ones who prepare a modification [of food] for consumption [are likewise at fault].
Afflicted with leprosy and deprived of sons and wives, those brahmins go to hell from which they do not return again. (Hbhv 9.405)
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"He who, having offered fresh food, fruit, and flowers to Madhusūdana, eats himself afterwards—for him Keśava is pleased. (Hbhv 9.406)
In the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa:
"Whoever eats the remains of Mukunda's meal day after day, for every single grain of rice, there shall be merit exceeding that of a hundred Cāndrāyaṇa fasts. (Hbhv_9.407)
Elsewhere it is also said:
"That fruit which is obtained by men through eleven thousand fasts lasting for a month and ten million upoṣaṇas is attained simply by eating the food offering (naivedya) of Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 9.408)
Then, having sipped water as prescribed and having distributed the betel leaves and other items,
he himself, being self-restrained, should receive the great prasāda as a servant.
And so it is said in the Ninth Skandha, in the *Śrīmad-Ambarīṣa-carita* (BhP 9.4.20):
"I shall grant his desires, yet not out of a desire for my own pleasure,
but so that there may be devotion toward the refuge of those who praise the Supreme Lord."

Whatever greatness was previously described regarding the consumption of the food offering (naivedya) and the taking up of the remains of the offering (nirmālya), all of that should be understood to apply here as well. Hbhv_9.411 //
Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Great Grace" (Mahā-prasāda), in the *Śrī-Bhagavad-bhakti-vilāsa* composed by Śrī-Gopāla Bhaṭṭa.
10. The Chapter on Association with the Holy (Satsaṃgama-vilāsa)
The Tenth Chapter.
Homage again and again to those who are bees at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; by taking refuge in them even in some small way, even a dog may partake of their fragrance. (Hbhv 10.1)
Then, adorned with the marks of a Vaiṣṇava, one should go with humility to the auspicious assembly of the devotees of Śrī Kṛṣṇa to drink the nectar of the stories of Kṛṣṇa. (Hbhv 10.2)
And so says the Smṛti: "One should pass the sixth and seventh [hours] with the Itihāsas and Purāṇas. (Hbhv 10.3)
Now, the characteristics of the devotees of the Blessed Lord—generally, as stated in the *Laiṅga Purāṇa*:
"He for whom Viṣṇu alone is the deity is indeed remembered as a Vaiṣṇava. (Hbhv 10.4)
In this regard, there is a distinction:

even among those belonging to the Śaiva tradition—who possess vows, ritual actions, qualities, knowledge, enjoyments, births, and so forth—there are likewise devotees of Kṛṣṇa in various ways. (Hbhv 10.5)
Among these observances, devotion to vows that cause devotion to the Blessed Lord is the defining characteristic of a devotee of the Blessed Lord;
likewise, in the Skanda Purāṇa, in the dialogue between Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya and Bhagīratha, it is said: "A day joined with the remainder of the tenth [lunar day] is indeed dear to the Vaiṣṇavas."
O protector of the earth, those men who do not worship [in this way] are indeed true Bhāgavatas.
Even when their lives are at stake, those men do not eat upon reaching the day of Hari;
instead, they always keep a vigil at night, for they are truly devotees of the Lord.
Having observed the pure twelfth day (dvādaśī) accompanied by a night vigil,
even one who accomplishes it only briefly is indeed a devotee of the Lord (bhāgavata).
Those men whose devotion has not faltered and whose vows have not lapsed,
for whom the Lord of Śrī is most dear— they shall be true Bhāgavatas.

Among those who perform actions, devotion is caused by dedication to the Blessed One and so forth, or by regarding such acts as the command of the Lord; they are devoted to the conduct of the virtuous.
Those for whom life exists for the sake of dharma, sexual union for the sake of progeny, and cooking for the sake of the foremost brahmins—those men indeed should be known as Vaiṣṇavas. (Hbhv 10.10)
He who honors with devotion a traveler weary on the road who has arrived at his house at this time is a Vaiṣṇava, without a doubt. (Hbhv 10.11)
Those who delight in virtuous conduct, who are disciplined, compassionate toward all beings,
pure, and free from passion— they are indeed always true devotees of the Lord.
In the *Pādma Purāṇa*, within the *Māhātmya of Vaiśākha* during the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Ambarīṣa (5.94.8):
