"I consider him alone to be a Vaiṣṇava on this earth whose life is for the sake of dharma, whose dharma is solely for the sake of Hari, and whose days and nights are for the sake of merit. (Hbhv 10.13)
And in the Liṅga Purāṇa: "He who is pleased upon seeing those endowed with devotion to Viṣṇu and who promote the Śrauta and Smārta rites—he is proclaimed as a Vaiṣṇava. (Hbhv 10.14)
Devotion toward those possessed of virtues arises from a character endowed with excellent qualities such as compassion;
as stated in that very same section of the Skanda Purāṇa:
"O best of kings, those who consider their own suffering to be equal to the suffering of others [are truly compassionate]."
O King, those men who are devoted to the dharma of the Blessed One are indeed Vaiṣṇavas.
In the third book, in the dialogue between Śrī Kapila and Devahūti (3.25.21):
"Those who are patient, compassionate, friends to all embodied beings, who have no enemies, who are peaceful, virtuous, and adorned by goodness. (Hbhv 10.16)
In the fifth chapter, in the instruction to his sons by Ṛṣabha-deva (5.y5.2):
"Service to the great is said to be the door to liberation; association with those attached to women is the door to darkness."
Those who are great are even-minded, tranquil, free from resentment, and virtuous friends.
In the eleventh book (*ekādaśa-skandha*), in the response to Uddhava’s questions given by the Blessed One (11.11.29–31):
"Compassionate, free from malice toward all embodied beings, patient, having truth as his essence, blameless in nature, equanimous, and a benefactor to all. (Hbhv 10.18)
One whose intellect is unassailed by desires, self-controlled, gentle, pure, possessing nothing,
free from longing, moderate in eating, tranquil, steadfast, and taking refuge in me— such a person is a sage.
Vigilant, profound in nature, steadfast, and having conquered the six internal enemies; free from pride yet bestowing honor upon others, capable, friendly, compassionate, and wise.
In the Viṣṇu Purāṇa, in the dialogue between Yama and his messenger [ViP 3.7.20]: "He who does not deviate from the duties of his own caste, who is even-minded toward himself, friends, and enemies,"
Know him to be a devotee of Viṣṇu whose mind is firmly established on the heights— he neither takes nor destroys anything.
The cause of devotion toward the wise is their possession of knowledge.
As stated in the eleventh book, in the *Havi-yoga* and *Yogeśvarottara* sections (*Bhāgavata Purāṇa* 11.2.45, 52):
"He who perceives the nature of the Blessed Lord within all beings as his own self..."
This best of devotees regards all beings as the Blessed One within his own self.
He for whom there is no distinction between "self" and "other," nor any division regarding possessions or his own person;
who is equal toward all beings and tranquil—he indeed is the best of devotees.
In the eleventh book, in the words of the Blessed Lord (BhP 11.11.33):
"Whether knowing or not knowing Me—My extent, My nature, and My form—those who worship Me with undivided devotion are considered by Me to be the best of devotees. (Hbhv 10.24)
In that very context, regarding the *Havi-yoga* section of the *Uttara-khaṇḍa* [BhP 11.2.46–47]:
"He who exercises love toward the Lord, friendliness toward those dependent on Him, compassion toward the ignorant, and equanimity toward enemies—he is the middling [devotee]. (Hbhv_10.25)
He who strives with faith only for worship of Hari in the form of an image, and not toward His other devotees, is considered a common, materialistic devotee. (Hbhv 10.26)
The cause of devotion among those who possess enjoyments is non-attachment to those enjoyments;
as stated in the *Havi-yogeśvarottara* (BhP 11.2.48):
"He who, even while perceiving objects through his senses, neither hates nor rejoices..."
Beholding this as the illusory power (māyā) of Viṣṇu—he indeed is the best of devotees (bhāgavatottama).
The cause of devotion toward those who possess noble birth, learning, and so forth, is freedom from pride. Regarding that very point, [BhP 11.2.51]:
"He for whom the sense of 'I' does not cling to this body because of his birth or actions, nor because of his caste, stage of life, or lineage—he indeed is dear to Hari" (Hbhv 10.28).
Qualities such as knowledge, non-attachment, and humility arise in some way only through devotion;
since they become the means for reaching the culmination of devotion, they are therefore declared to be superior.
Among the Śaivas, there are those who create a distinction between Śrī Śiva and Kṛṣṇa;
as stated in the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*:
"In Śiva, the Supreme Lord, and in Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self..."
Those who act with equanimity are indeed the best of Bhāgavatas.
Furthermore, their primary characteristic—consisting essentially of direct devotion, such as being intent upon the meaning of the Blessed One’s teachings—is now being described. (Hbhv 10.31)
In the Skanda Purāṇa:
"Those men for whom the Bhāgavata scripture always remains in their presence, and who constantly worship it, they shall be true devotees (bhāgavatas). (Hbhv 10.32)
Those for whom the Bhāgavata scripture is more dear than life itself—these men are declared by Viṣṇu to be the most excellent and great devotees (mahā-bhāgavatas). (Hbhv 10.33)
The steadfastness of honoring Vaiṣṇavas is described in the *Liṅga Purāṇa*:
"Upon seeing a devotee of Viṣṇu who has arrived, one who is well-disposed and dear [to him] should indeed offer salutations and so forth, just as one would toward Vāsudeva himself."
He indeed should be known as a devotee; he purifies the three worlds.
One who, upon hearing harsh words spoken by a devotee of the Lord, forgives them with a prostration and speaks [only kindly] in return—he indeed is a Vaiṣṇava. (Hbhv 10.35)
He who, according to his ability, constantly provides all food and clothing for a devotee of Viṣṇu is indeed remembered as a Bhāgavata. (Hbhv 10.36)
In the *Garuḍa-purāṇa*:
"He by whom devotion to Viṣṇu has been established with his whole being, and who has surrendered his self to the Vaiṣṇavas—he indeed is a great Bhāgavata. (Hbhv 10.37)
Devotion to the service of Śrī Tulasī:
Those men who, upon seeing a grove of Tulasī, offer obeisances, and those whose ears are marked with its wood—they are indeed the best of Bhāgavatas. (Hbhv 10.38)
Those who feel satisfaction upon smelling the fragrance of tulasī, and those by whom its root has been uprooted—they are indeed the best of the bhāgavatas. (Hbhv 10.39)
Devotion to the topics of the Blessed Lord is described in the *Bṛhan-nāradīya-purāṇa* (1.5.52), in the dialogue between the Blessed Lord and Mārkaṇḍeya:
"Those whose minds are characterized by goodness (*sāttvikī*) regarding the hearing of My stories..."
And those who are devotees of His devotees—those indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.
In the *Skānda-purāṇa*, in the dialogue between the Blessed Lord and Arjuna:
"He who narrates My stories, he who listens to My stories, and he who rejoices in My stories—he indeed is the best of devotees. (Hbhv 10.41)
In that very same place, in the Third Skandha [BhP 3.25.23]:
"Those whose minds are fixed on Me listen to and narrate the refined stories concerning Me; various afflictions do not torment them. (Hbhv_10.42)

In that very same *Bṛhan-nāradīya* [1.5.64]: "Those whose minds are fixed on me, who are my devotees, who long for my devotees, and who are intent on hearing my name—they indeed are the supreme *bhāgavatas*. (Hbhv 10.43)
Those who, upon hearing the names of Hari, rejoice with great delight and have their bodies covered in horripilation— they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.
In that very same place, elsewhere [1.5.61]:
"Those men who, seeing the rise of others, rejoice, and those who are devoted to the name of Hari—they indeed are the most excellent Bhāgavatas. (Hbhv 10.45)
Devotion to remembrance therein consists of remembering through steadfastness in one's own duty and the cessation of passion and hatred.
As stated in the *Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa* (3.7.20–26) in the dialogue between Yama and his messengers:
"He who does not waver from the lofty lotus feet of the Blessed Lord..."
Know him to be a devotee of Viṣṇu whose mind is tranquil.
That man of pure intellect whose soul has not been defiled by the impurity of the Kali age's turbidity—
he is a human being who has taken Janārdana to heart.
Know him to be one who is constantly and exceedingly devoted to Hari.
He who, even upon seeing gold in secret, regards it with his intellect as if it were a blade of grass because it belongs to another,
and whose mind is devoted to no other than the Blessed One— [he is truly wise].
Know him to be the best of men, a devotee of Viṣṇu.
Where is Viṣṇu, pure as a crystal mountain peak, and where is the defect of envy and the like in the minds of men? Indeed,
these do not coexist with a mass of moonbeams.
There arises a splendor born from the blazing of the sacrificial fire.
Possessing stainless intelligence, free from envy, serene, pure in conduct, and a friend to all sentient beings,
may he be one whose speech is pleasant and beneficial, and who is devoid of pride and deceit.
Vāsudeva always dwells within his heart.
When that eternal one dwells within the heart, a person becomes the very embodiment of happiness for this world;
he experiences the most delightful essence of the earth within himself.
And the young *śāla* tree spoke with its very loveliness.

And regarding the remembrance [of the Lord] through detachment (*vairāgya*) and other means for the sake of victory over others, it is stated in the *Havi-yogeśvarottara* of the eleventh book of the *Bhāgavata Purāṇa* (11.2.49, 53–54): "He who [is the master] of the body, senses, vital breaths, mind, and intellect..."
Unconfused by the worldly conditions of birth, death, hunger, fear, thirst,
and suffering, he is the foremost of the Bhāgavatas through his mindfulness of Hari.
Even for the sake of the sovereignty of the three worlds,
his mindfulness remains unshaken from the lotus feet of the Blessed One, which are sought after by the unconquered self, the gods, and others.
He who [remains so] even for half a moment or a blink of an eye is indeed the foremost among Vaiṣṇavas.

How could that distress ever again approach the hearts of those who have taken refuge with the Lord, whose heat has been dispelled by the moonlight of the jewel-like nails on the toes of His feet of great prowess?
The heat of the sun does not prevail when the moon has risen.
In the Skanda Purāṇa, in that very same place:
"Those embodied beings who always worship Viṣṇu, the Lord of Sacrifice, the boon-granting Hari, and whose actions are meritorious—they are indeed eternal Bhāgavatas. (Hbhv 10.55)
In the *Liṅga-purāṇa*: "Filled with affection, he performs only auspicious deeds in the sacred field of Viṣṇu;
endowed with faith, he should worship the image of Hari constantly. (Hbhv 10.56)
O King, he who is constantly devoted to Nārāyaṇa in deed, thought, and speech—he indeed should be known as a devotee of Viṣṇu, a true Bhāgavata. (Hbhv 10.57)
Now, regarding the steadfastness in Vaiṣṇava dharma and so forth, it is stated in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Padma Purāṇa (6.253.27):
"One who has undergone the five purificatory rites beginning with *tāpa* and performs the rite of new worship..."
A Brahmin who knows the fivefold meaning is considered a great devotee of the Blessed One.
In the Gāruḍa [Purāṇa], there is absolute certainty: because they are always single-mindedly devoted to the god Viṣṇu as their supreme refuge.
Therefore, those whose minds are devoted to Him are declared to be single-minded devotees.
The state of being focused on nothing else through that knowledge is described in the eleventh book (*BhP* 11.11.33), in the response to Uddhava’s question:
"Whether knowing or not knowing Me— whatever My extent may be and whatever My nature— I am..."
Those who worship with undivided devotion are indeed considered true Bhāgavatas.
In the eleventh book [of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 11.2.50]:
"He in whose mind the seeds of desire and karma do not arise, and who has Vāsudeva as his sole refuge—he indeed is the best of devotees. (Hbhv_10.61)
And that single-mindedness is fourfold;
therein, regarding the disregard for material phenomena, it is stated in the very response to the question of the illustrious Uddhava [BhP 11.11.32]:
"Having thus understood both the qualities and the defects, even those pertaining to Me which have been ordained by Me..."
But he who, having abandoned all phenomena, should devote himself to me—he indeed is the most excellent of beings.
In the Śrī Bhagavad Gītā (18.66):
"Abandoning all duties, come to Me alone as your refuge;
I shall liberate you from all sins; do not grieve. (Hbhv 10.63)
In the fourth book [of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 4.29.47]:
"When the Blessed One, who has realized the Self, bestows his grace upon someone, he does not abandon his mind that is firmly established in both worldly knowledge and the Veda. (Hbhv 10.64)
The state of being entirely independent of anything else is described in the dialogue between the Blessed Lord and Uddhava (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.26.27) in the narrative of Aila:
"The saintly are indifferent to worldly things, their minds fixed on Me, peaceful, and possessing equal vision."
Free from "mine-ness," free from egoism, free from the pairs of opposites, and free from possessiveness.
Therefore, in the dialogue between Śrī Kapiladeva and Devahūti (3.25.24): "O virtuous lady, these saintly persons are free from all attachment;
you should seek association with them, for they remove the defects of attachment. (Hbhv 10.66)
Even when beset by obstacles, the mind remains intent on devotion to Kṛṣṇa;
as stated in that very same section of the Skanda Purāṇa:
"The mind of one who delights in Keśava, even when fallen into distress..."
And whose devotion never falters—he indeed is a man devoted to the Blessed One.
That man whose devotion here remains unwavering even when he has fallen into calamity,
and whose mind finds no pleasure elsewhere— he indeed is a true devotee of the Lord (bhāgavata).
The state of having love as the sole essence is described in the *Śrī-Ṛṣabhadeva’s Instruction to His Sons* (BhP 5.5.3):
"Or those who have established their purpose in friendship toward Me, the Lord..."

Among people who are preoccupied with maintaining their bodies, in houses filled with attachment to wife and children, and among those in the world who seek only as much wealth as they desire— none are truly possessed of joy.
The single-minded devotion to love is threefold according to the gradations of that love;
it is distinguished as superior, middling, and inferior. (Hbhv 10.70)

Among these, the highest is as follows, in the *Havi-yoga* section of the *Ekādaśa-skandha* of the *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam* (11.2.45–46): "He who perceives within all beings the nature of the Blessed Lord as his own self..."
This best of devotees [perceives] all beings within the Blessed Self.
"He who perceives the nature of his own chosen deity in all beings, and causes them to perceive it in him—this is the meaning accepted by the wise. (Hbhv 10.72)
In the dialogue between Śrī Kapila and Devahūti (3.25.22):
"Those who practice firm devotion unto Me with undivided intent, having renounced their ritual duties for My sake and abandoned their own kinsmen and relatives... (Hbhv 10.73).
In the *Śrī-havi-yogeśvarottara*:
"He whose heart does not release itself even when Hari— the destroyer of the flood of sins— is directly addressed by those who lack self-control..."
He whose lotus feet are held by the cord of affection is declared to be the foremost among the devotees of the Lord.
Among these, the middling [devotion] is described in the *Śrī-havi-yogeśvarottara* (BhP 11.2.46): "Toward the Lord, toward those dependent on Him, toward the ignorant, and toward enemies..."
He who practices love, loving-kindness, compassion, and equanimity is of middling capacity.
Among those, the lowest is described in that very same passage (BhP 11.2.47):
"He who, with faith, endeavors to perform worship of Hari in an image alone."
Nor toward others who are devotees of Him; such a devotee is considered to be of the ordinary type.
Worship performed with faith indicates love; one is thus called a devotee.
Furthermore, those characteristics of devotion which are to be written about later shall also be mentioned.
Those in whom acts such as salutation are found are indeed Bhāgavatas;
these are their characteristics, categorized thus according to the distinctions of secondary and primary types.
In this manner, the characteristics [of other types of persons] should also be inferred and distinguished.
People possessing such characteristics would be difficult to find in great numbers;
for it is evident that divine jewels do not circulate here and there.
Therefore, it is said in the *Nārāyaṇīya* section of the *Mokṣadharma* (*Mahābhārata* 12.336.68):
"For that person whom Madhusūdana beholds at the moment of birth should be known as being of *sāttvika* nature; he shall be certain of liberation. (Hbhv_10.81)
Thus, from the characteristics of the Vaiṣṇavas as briefly described, their greatness should also be understood; how much more could be written of it? (Hbhv 10.82)
Now, regarding the greatness of the devotees of the Blessed One,
it is stated by Śrī Śakra in the *Śauparṇa*:
"In the Kali age, that man in whom the *Bhāgavata* arises..."
By that, the mother becomes one who has a son, and he is the bearer of the burden for his ancestors.
In the Kali age, the scripture named Bhāgavata is indeed difficult to obtain;
it was told to me by my Guru, and it surpasses even the stations of Brahmā and Rudra. (Hbhv 10.84)
O Sage, those in whom the mark of a Bhāgavata is seen, and who sing of Hari in the Kali age, O gods, they should be known as such; of this there is no doubt.
In the *Śrī-Mārkaṇḍeya-purāṇa* it is said:
"If a Vaiṣṇava stands near someone even at the time of death, that person goes to the supreme abode, even if he were a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa. (Hbhv 10.86)
In the *Nāradīya Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Śrī Vāmadeva and Rukmāṅgada [NārP 2.10.37]:
"O protector of the earth, even a dog-eater who is a devotee of Viṣṇu is superior to a twice-born;
but a twice-born who is devoid of devotion to Viṣṇu is inferior even to a dog-eater. (Hbhv 10.87)

In the *Revākhaṇḍa* of the *Skānda-purāṇa*, as spoken by Śrī Brahmā: "O Keśava, when you are pleased, even an outcaste indeed becomes Indra, Maheśvara, Brahmā, or the Supreme Brahman itself. (Hbhv 10.88)
O Acyuta, it is only when you turn your face away that even the gods, such as Brahmā and Īśāna, become more wretched than even a dog-cooker (outcaste).
O Keśava, he who is devoted to you is the doer of all righteous deeds;
O Acyuta, he who is not devoted to you is the doer of all sins. (Hbhv 10.90)
O Acyuta, even that which is dharma becomes adharma when performed by your devotees;
O Hari, even dharma becomes sin when performed by those who are not your devotees.
O Hari, even one who performs every possible dharma but lacks devotion remains forever in hell;
yet even a slayer of a Brahmin is purified if he is devoted to you.
O Janārdana, that unwavering devotion toward you is itself liberation;
for those devotees of yours, O Viṣṇu, O Hari, are indeed already liberated.
In that very same conversation between Durvāsas and Nārada, it is said:
"O great sage, the devotees of the Lord in this world, who are experts in protecting the world, surely proceed as directed by Viṣṇu, who dwells within their hearts. (Hbhv 10.94)
O Nārada, it is Hari himself, the Blessed One, who out of compassion for all beings wanders through the worlds in the form of a devotee for their protection.
In that very same *Śrī-Brahma-Nārada-Saṃvāda*:
"But he who is eternally devoted to Viṣṇu, possessing firm devotion and having conquered his senses, goes to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu even while dwelling in his own home. (Hbhv 10.96)
Even one who performs a thousand times a thousand horse sacrifices does not obtain that fruit which is attained by those devoted to Him.
In that very same *Amṛtasāroddhāra*, in the dialogue between Śrī Yama and his messenger:
"Vaiṣṇavas are indeed to be worshiped everywhere—in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld—by gods, humans, as well as by serpents and rākṣasas. (Hbhv 10.98)
By the mere remembrance of these high-souled Vaiṣṇavas, hundreds of lakhs of sins are consumed; of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv 10.99)
By the mere dust of whose feet the waters of the Jāhnavī,
the Narmadā, and the Yamunā are attained— how much more so, then, the water from their very feet?
By the flood of whose words a human being is purified— even without the waters of the Gaṅgā and without a thousand sacred fords (tīrthas).
In that very same [text] on the greatness of the Cāturmāsya:
"The ancestors wander in saṃsāra, intent upon the funeral cakes (piṇḍa), as long as no son endowed with devotion is born into the family. (Hbhv 10.102)
He alone is truly possessed of knowledge in this world, for he is the foremost among yogis—
he who, endowed with devotion to Hari, is the performer of great sacrifices.
In the *Kāśī-khaṇḍa*, within the account of Dhruva:

"Because they do not fall even during the great calamity of universal dissolution through devotion to him, he alone is Acyuta (the Unfallen) in all the world—the omnipresent and imperishable one. (Hbhv 10.104)
One should never fear anyone at any time on account of that devotee of the Blessed One;
for those who are devoted to Viṣṇu are certainly scorers of their enemies.
In that very same place, it is stated further on:
"Whether he be a Brāhmaṇa, a Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya, a Śūdra, or even someone else—if he is endowed with devotion to Viṣṇu, he should be known as the most excellent among all. (Hbhv 10.106)

If one whose body is marked with the conch and the discus, who bears a cluster of blossoms upon his head, and whose limbs are smeared with gopīcandana is seen, then whence can there be sin? (Hbhv 10.107)
In the *Mahābhārata*, in the *Rājadharmaparvan*:
"Those who are devoted to Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of all beings, the source and dissolution of the world—that god—they cross over all difficulties. (Hbhv_10.108)
In the Viṣṇudharmottara:
"He who, having risen from his bed, glorifies Madhusūdana—by that glorification, his sins go to destruction without remainder. (Hbhv 10.109)
In that very place:
"He who possesses supreme devotion toward the infinite Lord of the worlds, the God of gods of the Yādavas— "
Therefore, O hero among men, there is no other recipient whatsoever in the three worlds who is superior to him.
In the *Dvārakā-māhātmya*, within the dialogue between Śrī Prahlāda and Bali:
"O Bali, those Vaiṣṇavas who, having risen daily at dawn, perform the glorification (*kīrtana*) of the Vaiṣṇavas in the Kali age, are true devotees of the Lord (*bhāgavatas*) equal to Kṛṣṇa himself."
In the *Haribhaktisudhodaya*:
"By means of seeing, touching, and worshipping him, the virtuous Vaiṣṇava [destroys] darkness, just as one does before an image of Viṣṇu."
Shaking off [all worldly ties], he dwells here; that which he does for people is not for his own sake, but for the benefit of the world, like a lamp.
In the *Itihāsa-samuccaya*, in the words of Śrī Lomaśa:
"O best of kings, for those who worship Vāsudeva, the eternal source of the world, there exists no sacred site superior to them. (Hbhv 10.113)
Know that to be a superior sacred ford (tīrtha), which purifies all sins, where the devotees of the Lord (bhāgavatas), whose refuge is purity, perform their ablutions.
O King, wherever those who are free from passion and the like are devoted to Vāsudeva, there Viṣṇu is present; of this there is no doubt.
The Lord does not manifest His presence through perfumes, nor likewise through waters, nor even with captivating flowers,
where Vaiṣṇavas do not exist.
Even though Viṣṇu is constantly propitiated there with offerings, fasts, dances, songs, and the like, he is not satisfied. (Hbhv 10.117)
Therefore, these highly fortunate Vaiṣṇavas, free from all impurity, purify all the worlds; consequently, that sacred ford is superior even to them.
If one looks upon a Śūdra who is a devotee of the Blessed One, or likewise a Niṣāda or a Śvapaca, because of the commonality of their birth, he certainly goes to hell. (Hbhv 10.119)
Therefore, for the sake of Viṣṇu’s grace, one should satisfy the Vaiṣṇavas;
by that very act, Viṣṇu becomes favorably disposed toward one—of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv 10.120)
In that very same [text], in the dialogue between Śrī Nārada and Puṇḍarīka:
"Even those who are cruel, evil-minded, and always devoted to sinful conduct, they too go to the supreme abode if they take refuge in Nārāyaṇa. (Hbhv 10.121)
Devotees of Viṣṇu who are intent upon Viṣṇu are not stained by sin;
like the risen sun, they purify all the worlds. (Hbhv 10.122)
He who, throughout thousands of other births, should possess such an understanding as this—
"I am the servant of Vāsudeva"— shall uplift all the worlds.
That person goes to the same world as Viṣṇu; there is no doubt about this.
How much more so those men who have offered their life-breaths to Him and whose senses are restrained? (Hbhv 10.124)
O best of the twice-born, even a devotee of the Blessed One who is a caṇḍāla purifies [others] by chance—whether remembered, spoken to, or even worshipped. (Hbhv 10.125)
In the words of Śrī Vyāsa:
"One who is a devotee of Viṣṇu is not tainted even after thousands of births;
by the mere sight of him, sin is reduced to ashes. (Hbhv 10.126)
In the *Itihāsa-samuccaya*, in the words of the Blessed Lord:
"One who is learned in the four Vedas is not dear to me; my devotee, even if he be a dog-cooker (outcaste), is dear to me.
To him gifts should be given, from him they should be accepted, and he is to be honored just as I am. (Hbhv 10.127)
In that very same passage from the Brahma-vākya:
"Whether she has a husband or is a widow, she who practices devotion to Viṣṇu uplifts herself and one hundred and one generations of her lineage. (Hbhv_10.128)
In the *Dvārakā-māhātmya*, within the dialogue between Prahlāda and Bali:
"Those born of mixed castes who are purified through devotion to Madhusūdana are truly of noble birth;
whereas those who are not devotees of Janārdana, even if they are of high lineage, are equal to barbarians. (Hbhv 10.129)
In the *Ādi-purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna:
"O son of Kuntī, worship the Vaiṣṇavas; do not worship other deities.
Indeed, all Vaiṣṇavas purify this entire world, which consists of all the gods."
A devotee of mine is rare; he alone is difficult for me to find.
O Dhanañjaya, it is the truth, the absolute truth, that there is nothing more difficult to attain than being devoted to Him.
We are the gurus of the worlds, and we are the gurus of our devotees.
Just as we are gurus everywhere, so too are our devotees gurus.
Our kinsmen are devoted; we are the kinsmen of those who are devoted.
Our teachers are devoted to us, and we are the teachers of our devotees.
O King, wherever my devotees go, there I go;
for liberation follows after the devotees along with the sacred scriptures.
O Pārtha, those who are devotees of mine are not truly my devotees;
rather, those who are devotees of my devotees are considered by me to be my most excellent devotees.
O Dhanañjaya, whatever living beings are my devotees and have renounced their kinsmen for my sake, I am purchased by them; I am not purchased by anyone else.
Listen to my definitive conclusion regarding their food;
there are two kinds of sustenance for these devotees: leavings and remnants. (Hbhv 10.135)
Certain people who bear my name and are endowed with another birth bring me such pleasure as those who have mastered the Vedas do not.
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, within the words of the Blessed Lord spoken to Mārkaṇḍeya [1.4.96, 98]:
"The wise always say that Viṣṇu is the kinsman of His devotees;
I shall protect that very fact, for one who has taken refuge in Me would not speak a falsehood. (Hbhv_10.137)
The family into which I am born truly attains liberation;
O best of sages, when I am pleased, what is there that cannot be accomplished within the three worlds? (Hbhv 10.138)
But he who is devoted to me, who sacrifices to me, who is intent on my stories,
and who meditates upon me— he leads his entire family to the state of being the Imperishable One.
A person who performs actions for my sake, who is intent on bowing to me,
and whose mind is fixed on me, leads his entire family to the state of the Imperishable One.
O best of the twice-born, it is I alone who, eternally concealing my true form,
always protect the worlds in the guise of a devotee of the Blessed One.
In that very same [work], within the *Aditimāhātmya* as spoken by Śrī Sūta: "O brāhmaṇas, listen to the majesty of those whose souls are devoted to the worship of Hari;
for who is capable of obstructing those intent on meditation upon Hari? (Hbhv 10.142).
Wherever one is devoted to the service of Hari, there reside Brahmā, Hari, and Śiva;
there the gods, Siddhas, and other excellent beings always dwell.
Wherever the most excellent beings remain for even a moment or half a moment, right there all blessings reside; that is a sacred ford, that is a forest of asceticism.
In that very place, in the reply of the Blessed One to Aditi [NārP 1.11.57–58]:
“Those who are free from attachment and aversion, my devotees who are intent on me, they constantly speak of me, being devoid of malice and free from hypocrisy. (Hbhv 10.145)
Averse to harming others, devoted to the worship of Śiva,
and intent on listening to my stories, they indeed carry me constantly.

In that very same context, regarding the greatness of raising the flag, it is stated in the *Śrī-Viṣṇu-dūta*: "Even sinners, if they merely look upon those ascetics who are devotees of Viṣṇu and are intent on serving them, go to the supreme goal. (NārP 1.20.73) — Hbhv_10.147.
In that very same place, in the dialogue concerning the manner of pleasing the Blessed Lord, it is said:
"Enemies do not harm him, nor do planetary spirits afflict him;
neither do Rākṣasas even look upon that man who is devoted to Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 10.148)
For one whose devotion to Janārdana, the God of gods, becomes firm, their spiritual perfections are accomplished; therefore, those possessed of devotion are superior.
In that very place, further on [NārP 1.34.63]:
"Even now, O best of sages, even the deities beginning with Brahmā do not fully comprehend the power of those whose souls are devoted to Viṣṇu. (Hbhv_10.150)
Furthermore:
"O best of the twice-born, the goals of human existence known as dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa are indeed attained by those devoted to Hari; of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv 10.151)
In that very same place, at the beginning of the story of the hunter [NārP 1.37.9,12]:
"Those who are devoted to Viṣṇu, peaceful, intent on favoring the world, and endowed with compassion for all beings, are proclaimed to be the very form of Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 10.152)
Those who are devoid of devotion to Viṣṇu are proclaimed to be outcasts;
yet even outcasts are indeed superior if they are devoted solely to Hari.
In that very place, at the beginning of the narrative concerning Yajñadhvaja, the words of Śrī Sūta are as follows:

"I pay homage to those best of men who are delighted by the savoring of the rasa of devotion to Hari, through association with whom a person becomes a partaker of liberation. (NārP 1.39.3–4, 8) — Hbhv 10.154.
But those who are devoted to devotion to Hari and dedicated to the name of Hari—
whether they be of bad conduct or of good conduct— to them, eternal salutations, salutations!
Oh, what fortune! Oh, what fortune for those whose souls delight in devotion to Viṣṇu!
For them, liberation—which is difficult even for yogis to attain—is already within their grasp. (Hbhv 10.156)
In that very context regarding the Kali age:
"When the terrible Kali Yuga has arrived, which is devoid of all righteousness, those mortals who are devoted to Vāsudeva have achieved their purpose; of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv 10.157)
In the Kali age, devotion to Hari is said to be difficult to find within;
indeed, for those who are devoted to Hari, the bond of sin does not arise.
All those who delight in the recitation of the Vedas and likewise those who frequent sacred bathing places do not equal even a sixteenth part of those devoted to the worship of Hari.

Therefore, it was said by the gods in that very context, in the section concerning Bhāratavarṣa (*Nārada Purāṇa* 1.3.53): "One who is habituated to chanting the glories of Hari, or one who is dear to His devotees, or even one who desires to serve the great—such a supreme person is worthy of our salutation. (Hbhv 10.160)
In the *Padma-purāṇa*, in the dialogue between the Blessed One and Brahmā:
"By means of sight, meditation, and touch, mortals, tortoises, and birds nourish their own offspring; so too do I, O Lotus-born One. (Hbhv_10.161)
Although I am capable of destroying even the Dānavas in a mere moment,
I perform various activities for the sake of the amusement of my devotees.
In that very same *Māgha-māhātmya*, in the dialogue between the divine messenger and Vikuṇḍala:
"The Vaiṣṇavas certainly do not see Yama, nor the world of Yama, nor the messengers of fearsome appearance; this truth, indeed, has been spoken by me. (Hbhv_10.163)
One should not look upon a Brahmin who is not a Vaiṣṇava in this world, as one would a dog-cooker;
for a Vaiṣṇava, even if outside the [social] castes, purifies the three worlds. (Hbhv 10.164)
Śūdras who are devotees of the Blessed One are considered to be [true] bhāvanās;
among all castes, those people are Śūdras who are not devotees of Janārdana.
O Vaiśya, those who are servants of a devotee of Viṣṇu and those who eat the food of Vaiṣṇavas,
they too go, free from distress, to the same destination as the enjoyers of the sacrificial offerings.

In that very same [text], within the *Vaiśākha-māhātmya*, it is said regarding five persons: "Blessed beings, having come into existence, move through the world for the sake of helping others. (Hbhv 10.167)
Likewise:
"The virtuous are the support for the destitute whose misfortunes have arisen through fate;
they are the destroyers of the suffering of the afflicted by their very sight. (Hbhv 10.168)
In that very same section, in the dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī (*Padma Purāṇa* 6.229.58–59):
"For Vaiṣṇavas, there exists neither the bondage of karma nor rebirth;
indeed, the wise declare that service to Viṣṇu is liberation. (Hbhv 10.169)
Service to the Lord of the Immortals is not proclaimed to be bondage;
the servants of Hari are liberated from all bonds and free from affliction.

In the *Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa*, within the section on the greatness of the Janmāṣṭamī vow, it is stated by Śrī Citragupta: "By merely seeing, touching, conversing with, or dwelling together with them for even a moment, the devotees of Kṛṣṇa purify even a *pukkaśa*—that is, one born of the lowest caste. (Hbhv_10.171)
Even a man who has abandoned all family traditions and is guilty of great sins does not deserve torment if he takes refuge in a devotee of Viṣṇu.
In the *Vāsiṣṭha*:

"In whatever desert-like region there is no tree of a virtuous person who knows the truth—a tree that bears fruit and provides cool shade—one should not dwell there for even a single day. (Hbhv 10.173)
The virtuous should always be approached even if they do not offer instruction,
for whatever casual conversation they may have becomes their teaching.
In the Gāruḍa [Purāṇa]: "One who has mastered all the Vedāntas is superior to thousands of performers of sacrificial sessions;
one who is a devotee of Viṣṇu is superior to ten million knowers of all the Vedāntas. (Hbhv 10.175)
Among thousands of Vaiṣṇavas, one who is single-mindedly devoted (ekāntin) is distinguished;
indeed, those persons who are single-mindedly devoted go to the supreme station.
Śrī Bhagavad-gītā [9.30–33]: Even if one of very wicked conduct worships Me with undivided devotion, he should be regarded as righteous indeed, for he has rightly resolved. (Hbhv_10.177)
He quickly becomes righteous in nature and attains eternal peace;
O Kaunteya, know for certain that my devotee never perishes.
For even those who may be of low birth— women, Vaiśyas, and likewise Śūdras— by taking refuge in me, O Pārtha, they too attain the supreme goal;
how much more so, then, the meritorious Brāhmaṇas and devoted royal sages!
Moreover, in that very same place [Gītā 6.47]:
"Among all yogis as well, he who, with his inner self absorbed in Me, worships Me with faith—he is deemed by Me to be the most disciplined. (Hbhv_10.180)

In the first book of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, as spoken by Śrī Parīkṣit [BhP 1.19.33]: "By the mere remembrance of whom the homes of men are instantly purified—how much more so by seeing them, touching them, washing their feet, or offering them seats and the like! (Hbhv 10.181)
In the third canto, regarding Śrī Vidura [BhP 3.13.4]:
"Indeed, for men who have labored long over sacred learning, the goal praised by the wise is attained directly."
Those in whose hearts the lotus feet of Mukunda dwell, for them there is the constant hearing of his various qualities.
Regarding Devahūti, Kapiladeva said (BhP 3.25.38):
"Those who are devoted to Me shall never perish in this peaceful form; nor does My unblinking weapon devour them."
For those to whom I am a beloved self, a son,
a friend, a teacher, a well-wisher, and their chosen deity.
In the fourth [chapter], regarding Śrī Dhruva [BhP 4.9.10]:
"The bliss that embodied beings may obtain from meditating upon Your lotus feet, or from hearing the narrations concerning Your devotees..."
O Lord, let her not fall even from Brahman, who is his own majesty;
rather, let her fall from the celestial chariot shaken by the sword of Antaka.
"One who is steadfast in his own duty for a hundred births attains the state of Viriñca; thereafter, he indeed reaches Me. (Śrī Rudra, Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.24.29)
O wise ones, the state of Bhagavat or Vaiṣṇava is indeed indeterminate, just as I have described it at the end of the kalpa.
In the fifth [canto], regarding Śrī Jaḍa Bharata [BhP 5.12.12]:
"O Rahūgaṇa, this is not attained by austerity,
nor by sacrifice, nor by giving away from the house."
Neither by mere desire, nor by water, fire, or the sun,
can one attain it without the consecration of the dust from the feet of the Great One.

In the sixth [chapter], regarding the illustrious Parīkṣit: "The living beings here on earth are equal in number to the particles of dust; among them, only a few humans and others truly strive for the highest good. (Hbhv_10.187)
O best of the twice-born, those who desire liberation are few among them;
indeed, among thousands of seekers of liberation, perhaps one may be liberated and attain success.
O great sage, even among those who are liberated and perfected, one whose self is tranquil and who is devoted solely to Nārāyaṇa is extremely rare, even among tens of millions.
"O Śiva, all those who are devoted to Nārāyaṇa do not fear anything from any quarter; they view heaven, liberation, and hell as equal in their significance. (BhP 6.17.28) — Hbhv 10.190.
In the seventh [canto], regarding Śrī Prahlāda [BhP 7.5.32]:
"The intelligence of these [demigods] does not touch the feet of the Wide-striding Lord as long as there is no cessation of that misfortune for which they strive."
As long as one does not accept the consecration by the dust of the feet of the great ones, being free from all possessions.
Moreover:
"Better than a Brahmin endowed with the twelve qualities who is averse to the lotus-feet of the one whose navel is a lotus is even a dog-eater."
I believe that one who has dedicated their mind, speech, actions, wealth, and life to Him purifies their lineage; but not one who is full of great pride.
In the eighth [canto], regarding Śrī Gajendra: "Those who have indeed taken refuge in the Blessed One, the single-minded devotees, do not desire any object whatsoever."
Singing of that most wonderful and auspicious life-story, they were immersed in an ocean of bliss.
In the ninth [canto], from the Śrī Bhāgavatam (BhP 9.4.63–66, 68):
"O twice-born one, I am indeed dependent on my devotees, as if lacking independence;
for my heart is captivated by saintly devotees, and I am dear to those who are devoted. (Hbhv 10.194)
O Brahmin, I do not desire for myself ultimate prosperity without my virtuous devotees, for whom I am the supreme refuge. (Hbhv 10.195)
How could I bear to abandon those who have come to me for refuge, having forsaken their wives, homes, sons, kin, lives, and even this supreme wealth? (Hbhv 10.196)
The virtuous, who possess equal vision and have fixed their hearts upon me,
bring me under their control through devotion, just as virtuous wives do for a good husband.
The virtuous are my heart, and I am the heart of the virtuous;
they know nothing other than me, nor do I know even the slightest thing other than them.
In that very context, Śrī Durvāsas said (BhP 9.5.15):

"What indeed is difficult for the virtuous to perform, or what is difficult for the great-souled to renounce, by whom the Blessed Lord Hari, the bull among the Sātvatas, has been embraced? (Hbhv 10.199)
When a person becomes stainless by the mere hearing of his name,
what more remains for the servants of that Tīrthapada?
In the tenth book, in the hymn to the Lord (BhP 10.2.33):
"O Mādhava, those who are yours and who have bound their affection to you never fall away from the path."
Protected by you, O Lord, they wander fearlessly upon the crests of the hosts of Vināyakas.
Śrī Bādarāyaṇa [BhP 10.9.21] states:

"The Blessed Lord, the son of the cowherd woman, is not so easily attained by embodied beings who are merely wise and have realized the Self as He is here by those possessed of devotion. (Hbhv 10.202)

In that very context, the Blessed Lord says: "What is the use of wealth—those pillars of falsehood—which are to be disregarded by the virtuous who possess equanimity and seek the feet of Mukunda, since they are unreal and provide no true refuge? (BhP 10.10.41). Hbhv_10.203 //
Furthermore:
"For holy places do not consist of water, nor are the gods made of clay or stone;
the virtuous purify by their mere sight, whereas those others [purify] only after a long time. (BhP 10.84.11) [Hbhv 10.204]
Moreover: "Neither fire, nor sun, nor moon and stars, nor earth, water, space, wind, speech, or mind [could perceive it]."
Those wise ones who serve the makers of distinctions take away their sin; by serving them for even a moment, they destroy it.

He who perceives the notion of "self" in this corpse-like body composed of the three elements, the notion of "own" in wife and other possessions, the notion of a "deity to be worshipped" in the earth,
and the notion of a "sacred ford" in water— never [possesses such notions] elsewhere.
Among people who possess supernormal knowledge, he is indeed that very ox or donkey.
In the *Śrutistuti* (BhP 10.87.27):
"Those who wander about You because You are the abode of all beings indeed trample upon the head of Destruction (*Nirṛti*), disregarding it."
With your song you tend the wise as if they were cattle;
indeed, those who have established friendship with you purify themselves, whereas those who turn away from you do not.
In the eleventh [canto], regarding Śrī Vasudeva [BhP 11.2.5–6]:
"The conduct of the gods toward living beings leads to both suffering and happiness;
however, for the virtuous such as you, whose souls are fixed on Acyuta, it leads only to happiness. (Hbhv 10.208)
Just as people worship the gods, so too do the gods reciprocate;
for the virtuous, who are compassionate toward the distressed, follow their actions like a shadow.

In that very regard, the Blessed Lord [BhP 11.20.36] says: "For those who are single-mindedly devoted to Me, for the virtuous ones whose minds are equanimous and who have reached that which is beyond the intellect, there are no qualities arising from virtue or vice. (Hbhv_10.210)
Thus, those who follow these paths ordained by me find security and reach my station, which they know as the supreme Brahman.
For those sinking and surfacing in the terrible ocean of worldly existence,
the virtuous knowers of Brahman who are peaceful are the supreme refuge, just as a boat is for those drowning in water.
For food is the life-breath of living beings; I am the refuge for the afflicted;
dharma is the wealth of men after death; and the virtuous are the protection for those who fear in this world.
The virtuous grant eyes; the sun has risen from without; the virtuous are deities, the virtuous are kinsmen, and the virtuous are my very self. (Hbhv 10.214)
Moreover:
"The virtuous, steadfast, and my exclusively devoted bhaktas do not desire even *kaivalya*—the state of non-return—though it be granted by me. (BhP 11.20.34)
And in the twelfth [chapter], regarding Śrī Parīkṣit:
"I do not consider it at all extraordinary that those great souls whose very selves are Acyuta show favor toward ignorant beings tormented by suffering. (Hbhv 10.216)
And regarding the Śrī-Rudra hymn concerning Mārkaṇḍeya [BhP 12.10.25]:
"By hearing or even by seeing it, even you who are great sinners and even those of the lowest castes would be purified; how much more so by conversation and other such means! (Hbhv 10.217).
Therefore, in the sixth canto of the *Śrī-Dharmarāja’s Instruction to His Own Messengers* (BhP 6.3.27), it is said:
"Those saintly persons who are impartial toward all and have taken refuge in the Blessed Lord are the ones whose pure songs are celebrated by gods and perfected beings."
Do not approach them, for they are protected by Hari’s mace;
neither we nor our strength have the power to punish them.
Likewise, in the Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa [3.7.26, 32–34]:
"For those whose impurities have been shaken off by *yama* and *niyama*,
and whose minds are day by day attached to Acyuta..."
O soldier, go far away from those men who are devoid of pride and stinginess.
"This entire universe, and I myself, am Vāsudeva— the Supreme Person, the one Supreme Lord"—
when such an unshakable conviction arises toward the Infinite One, [then one has attained the goal].
Having entered the heart, depart from them, leaving them far behind.
"O lotus-eyed Vāsudeva, Viṣṇu,
Supporter of the Earth, Acyuta, you who hold the conch and discus in your hands—
those who indeed cry out, 'Be our refuge!'"
O soldier, abandon those sinless ones from a great distance.
O Discus-bearer, for that Supreme Person in whose mind that Imperishable Self dwells, there is no path for you, nor for me, within the range of his vision.
For one whose strength of vigor has been thwarted, that [attainment] is beyond the world.

In the *Nārasiṃha Purāṇa* and the *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* (3.7.15), it is said: "I was appointed as Yama by the Creator, who is worshipped by the immortals, for the sake of determining what is beneficial and harmful for the world."
I am subject to Hari and my Guru; I am not independent, for Viṣṇu has power even over my restraint.
O Vāsudeva, I desire a happy rebirth;
my inner self is established in the Bhāgavata [dharma],
yet I am subject to Madhuvara and am not independent.
Kṛṣṇa has power even over my restraint.
For the moon, with its complexion like a hare-mark, never undergoes defeat by darkness;
and so it is with one whose mind is fixed on no other than the Blessed Lord Hara.
Even if he is extremely soiled, a person still shines.
In the *Padma Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Devadyuti and Vikuṇḍala [PadmaP 3.31.100, 102–3]:
Yamunā’s brother said to us again and again: "You must always avoid those who are Vaiṣṇavas; they should not come within my range. (Hbhv_10.226)
Even if he is of evil conduct and a doer of wicked deeds, that man who is devoted to Viṣṇu and delights in virtuous conduct must always be avoided by you. (Hbhv 10.227)
Those in whose house a Vaiṣṇava eats, and those who have the company of a Vaiṣṇava— they too should be honored by you, for their sins have been destroyed by that association.
In the *Skānda-amṛtasāroddhāra*:
"If you always desire my welfare, you must avoid those who do not eat on the eleventh day, even if they are burdened with hundreds of sins. (Hbhv 10.229)
Those people who, at the time of death, remember Janārdana, the Lord of the World,
shall not be seized by me by my command, even if they are burdened with hundreds of millions of sins.
Neither Brahmā, nor Śiva, Agni, or Indra, nor I, nor any other inhabitants of heaven,
are capable of effecting the restraint of the high-souled Vaiṣṇavas.
Therefore, I am indeed afraid of Vaiṣṇavas at all times;
you must always avoid those who are Vaiṣṇavas.
The Vaiṣṇavas are to be honored like Viṣṇu himself; they are especially worthy of my respect.
Even if they are treated with contempt, their destruction will certainly come to pass. (Hbhv 10.233)
Moreover:
"By the mere remembrance of those high-souled Vaiṣṇavas, hundreds of thousands of sins are burned away; of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv 10.234)
Even by the mere dust of their feet, one attains the waters of the Jāhnavī, the Narmadā, and the Yamunā; how much more so, then, the water from their feet themselves?
By the flood of whose words a human being becomes bathed, even without the waters of the Gaṅgā and without a thousand sacred fords (tīrthas).
Moreover:
"I have no dwelling in the world of Brahmā, nor do I have a dwelling in the abode of Hara; nor in the abode of the world-protectors, nor in the defeat of the Vaiṣṇavas. (Hbhv 10.237)
Neither the gods, nor the gandharvas, nor the yakṣas, uragas, and rākṣasas,
nor even the ṛṣis are capable of protecting [a person] when the devotees of Viṣṇu are being overcome.
O highly fortunate ones, through deed, word, and even thought, I do nothing displeasing to the Vaiṣṇavas, out of fear of the Sudarśana discus itself.
The wheel rolls in one direction, the chariot drawn by tawny horses in another, and the messengers of Viṣṇu in yet another, when I have afflicted a Vaiṣṇava. (Hbhv 10.240)
And in the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, in the section on the majesty of Ekādaśī (*Ekādaśī-māhātmya*), [it is said]:
"Those who are devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, self-restrained, grateful, intent upon the vow of Ekādaśī, and have conquered their senses..."
"O Nārāyaṇa, O Acyuta, O Hari, be our refuge!"—thus do the peaceful ones constantly say; therefore, abandon [worldly attachments] with all your might.
Those whose minds are dedicated to Nārāyaṇa, who are devoted to the devotees of Hari, who are intent on the path of virtuous conduct, who serve their gurus,
who are dedicated to giving to worthy recipients, and who are devoted to the glories of Hari— [may they be blessed].
O messengers, abandon those who are constantly attached to the name of Hari.
Those who are free from association with heretics, satisfied by devotion to Hari, intensely longing for the company of the virtuous, and likewise exceedingly meritorious;
and those who possess an even-mindedness toward Śambhu and Hari alike.
O messengers, abandon those men who are indifferent to doing favors.
Those who are beheld by those serving the nectar of Hari’s stories, whose minds are devoted to the remembrance of Nārāyaṇa,
and who are greatly delighted by serving the water from the feet of the best of Brahmins;
And you, O soldiers, must always abandon even those who are sinful.

Therefore, it was said by Śrī Nārada at the conclusion of the Fourth Skandha (BhP 4.31.22): "He who is self-perfected [does not seek] the Goddess of Fortune who follows him, nor the lords of men, nor the gods who desire her."
How could a grateful man, who is devoted to the circle of his own servants, ever abandon such a person?
Therefore, there is this prayer in the *Nārāyaṇa-vyūha-stava*:
"O Hari, may I not even become Brahmā if I am devoid of devotion to you."
But may I, even as a mere insect, be devoted to you in birth after birth.
And in the *Śrī-Brahma-stuti* (the prayer of Brahmā) in the Tenth Canto [BhP 10.14.30]: "O Lord, let that same abundant fortune be mine, whether in this birth or another, even among the animals."
By which, though I am but one among the people of this world, I may serve the sprout-like feet of Your Honor.

Therefore it is said in the *Śrī-Nārāyaṇa-vyūha-stava*: "Salutations again and again forever to those who, having renounced worldly duties and goals, have come under the sway of devotion to Viṣṇu and worship the Supreme Self. (Hbhv 10.248)
Thus, who other than one whose mind wavers with greed is worthy of this series of diverse waves from the nectar-ocean of the majesty of the Lord’s devotees? (Hbhv 10.249)
Therefore, those who desire to conquer both worlds should always strive with every effort to associate with the devotees of the Blessed Lord. (Hbhv 10.250)
Now, on the greatness of association with the devotees of the Blessed Lord:
"Salutations to the sandals of the lotus feet of the Blessed Lord's devotees;
for association with them is the means and the entirety of the supreme goal. (Hbhv 10.251)
In that regard, the power of liberating one from all sins is described at the conclusion of the *Yajñamālya* episode in the *Bṛhan-nāradīya-purāṇa* (NārP 1.36.60):
"But for those devoted to Hari, by the mere association with their companions..."
One is liberated from all sins, even if one has committed the great transgressions.
In general, [the purpose of dharma] consists in averting what is harmful and attaining what is beneficial.
In the *Vaiśākha-māhātmya* of the *Padma-purāṇa*, it is stated in the speech of the pretas to Śrī Muniśarman:
"It destroys ill-repute and also clarifies the intellect."
He generally establishes the Vaiṣṇava doctrine among men.
In that regard, in the dialogue between Śrī Yama and the Brāhmaṇa, it was said by the great chariot-warrior king:
"Just as for one who takes refuge in the Lord Vibhāvasu (Fire), cold, fear, and even darkness depart; so too it is for one who constantly serves the virtuous. (Hbhv 10.254)
In that very same account of the pretas, regarding the description of the pretas [PadmaP 5.98.57]:
"Association with Vaiṣṇavas quickly dispels the evil of men, bestows prosperity, and spreads their fame. (Hbhv_10.255)
Now, regarding the superiority of this very place over all other holy sites, it is said in the Padma Purāṇa (5.98.78):
"The man who desires to bathe in meritorious holy sites such as the Gaṅgā..."
Between one who associates with the virtuous and the two [types of association], association with the virtuous is superior.

In that very place, King Bhagīratha said: "For one who has bathed in the Gaṅgā of the company of the virtuous, which is white with peace—for such a person, what is the use of gifts, what use are sacred fords, what use are austerities, or what use are sacrifices? (Hbhv 10.257)
Now, regarding the accomplishment of all desired goals:
whatever things on the surface of the earth are difficult to obtain that one desires, those very things are attained solely through association with the virtuous. (Hbhv 10.258)
Now, regarding how even that which is not an object of value is brought to the state of being an object of value, it is said in the *Vāsiṣṭha*:
"The void attains fullness; even death becomes like immortality."
In the assembly of learned people, misfortune appears like prosperity.
In the Third Skandha [BhP 3.23.55]:

"That very attachment which, when directed toward the wicked, is the cause of worldly existence by means of the intellect, becomes conducive to freedom from attachment when it is directed toward the virtuous. (Hbhv 10.260)
As stated by Śrī Kapiladeva [BhP 3.25.20]:
"The wise know association to be an unaging bond for the self;
that very same [association], when directed toward the saintly, becomes the open door to liberation. (Hbhv 10.261)
For it is said:
An enemy becomes a friend, poison becomes wholesome, and unrighteousness turns into righteousness; yet when the Lotus-Eyed Lord is displeased, the reverse occurs.
Furthermore, there is the word of the Blessed Lord:
"Even a sin committed for my sake becomes dharma;
conversely, even dharma becomes a sin by my power if it is performed in disregard of me. (Hbhv 10.263)

In the fourth canto, in the words of Śrī Dhruva (BhP 4.9.12): "They do not remember at all that mortal Lord who is exceedingly dear to them— those who are instead attached to children, friends, home, wealth, and wives."
But those who have formed an attachment to those whose hearts are greedy for the fragrance of your lotus feet, O Lotus-navelled One, [attain liberation].
In that very same section of the *Padmapurāṇa*, regarding the hungry ghosts (*preta*), it is said:
"Consisting of elixir (*rasāyana*), cool, and bestowing supreme bliss—whom indeed does this moonlight resting upon the Vaiṣṇavas not delight? (Hbhv 10.265)
Now, regarding the quality of bestowing liberation: in the tenth book, in the *Śrī-mucukunda-stuti*, [BhP 10.51.53] it says:
"When, for one wandering in saṃsāra, there may arise liberation from existence..."
O Acyuta, for a person, the association with the virtuous is indeed the meeting with the good; for when there is such association with the good,
then alone does the mind arise toward You, the Lord of the high and the low, the goal of the righteous.
Therefore it was said by the venerable Pracetās in the Fourth Canto [BhP 4.30.35–37]:
"Where delightful stories are celebrated, from which thirst is assuaged, where there is enmity toward no living beings, and where there is no agitation whatsoever. (Hbhv_10.267)
Where Nārāyaṇa, the Lord himself, the goal of those who have renounced,
is praised again and again in sacred discourses by those free from attachment.
For those who travel on foot with the desire to purify sacred fords,
would the meeting with your followers not be pleasing to one who is afraid?
Now, regarding the state of being the essence of all:
in the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, in the dialogue between the venerable Nārada and Sanatkumāra, it is said [NārP 1.4.13]:
"O son of the Self-born, in this world-cycle which is devoid of essence, this alone is the essence."
Association with the devotees of the Blessed One, devotion to Hari, and forbearance.
In that very same *Pādmapurāṇa*, the great chariot-warrior king said:
"Nectar does not arise from the ocean; it is a non-substantial remedy for calamity.
And the meeting of the virtuous is indeed joy that extends to the furthest limits of light. (Hbhv_10.271)

Furthermore, in the *Padma Purāṇa*, within the *Māhātmya* of Vaiśākha as spoken by Śrī Nārada, it is stated incidentally that for the virtuous, [these narrations] are the elixirs for their own minds and ears, serving solely as the cause for drinking the nectar of the Lord’s discourse:
"In this context, they are the elixirs for the self, mind, and hearing of the wise. (*Padma Purāṇa* 5.84.37)
The stainless stories of Kṛṣṇa, who is worthy of praise, come forth.

In the third book [of the Bhāgavatam, 3.25.25], as spoken by Śrī Kapiladeva: "From association with the virtuous, there arise stories that bring knowledge of My prowess; they are a nectar for the heart and the ears."
From delighting in that, faith, attachment, and devotion will follow in succession on the path to liberation.

In the fourth canto, in the words of Śrī Nārada (BhP 4.29.39–40): "O King, those places where the bhāgavatas— saintly persons of pure intent, whose minds are ever-absorbed in hearing and narrating the qualities of the Lord— " Hbhv_10.274.
In that place, great rivers— the remnants of the nectar of the life stories of the slayers of Madhu— flow everywhere with loud resounding waves;
those who drink from them with their ears fixed intently, O King, remain forever free from thirst.
Hunger, thirst, fear, sorrow, and delusion do not touch them.

In the fifth [chapter], in the dialogue between the venerable Brāhmaṇa and Rahūgaṇa (BhP 5.12.13): "Where the chanting of the qualities of the Lord of Excellent Fame is introduced, there worldly talk is destroyed."
When practiced daily, it bestows a virtuous mind upon the seeker of liberation regarding Vāsudeva.
In the eleventh book, in the dialogue between the Blessed Lord and Uddhava at the conclusion of the narrative of Aila [BhP 11.26.28–29]:
"O most fortunate one, among those great souls who are constantly devoted to My stories, those stories indeed arise; for those who take pleasure in them purify their sins. (Hbhv 10.277)
Those who hear this, sing it, and indeed rejoice in it with respect—
being devoted to me and full of faith— they find devotion toward me.
In that very same work, the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, it is said: "Devotion arises through association with the devotees of the Blessed One;
such association with the virtuous is attained by men through their previously accumulated merits. (Hbhv 10.279)
In the eleventh book, during the dialogue between the Blessed Lord and Uddhava [BhP 11.11.49–51]:
"Now, O delighter of the Yadus, I shall speak this supreme secret, which is most difficult to conceal, even as you listen; for you are my servant, my well-wisher, and my friend."
Neither yoga, nor Sāṅkhya, nor even dharma restrains me; neither Vedic study, austerity, renunciation, nor sacrifices, charitable works, nor ritual fees restrain me. (Hbhv 10.281)

Vows, sacrifices, Vedic meters, sacred fords, observances, and restraints—association with the virtuous indeed encompasses all these, for it removes attachment to everything else and leads me [to liberation]. (Hbhv 10.282)
Therefore, it was said by Vidura in the Third Canto (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.7.19):
"By service to that Lord, the immutable Madhudviṣ, may there arise an intense outpouring of delight at His feet, which destroys all calamities. (Hbhv 10.283)
In the first book, in the speech of Śrī Śaunaka and others (BhP 1.18.13), and in the fourth book, in the speech of the Śrī Pracetasas (BhP 4.30.34):
"We do not weigh even a fraction of heaven or liberation from rebirth against it."
What need is there to mention the blessings for mortals who associate with those who associate with the Blessed One?
And in the fourth [canto], there is the instruction of Śrī Śiva to Śrī Pracetas [BhP 4.24.57]:

"I do not value even heaven or liberation from rebirth for half a moment as much as the association of mortals with those who are attached to the Blessed Lord; how much less, then, other blessings? (Hbhv 10.285)
In the twelfth book, in the narrative of Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya, regarding Śrī Śiva [BhP 12.10.7]:
"Nevertheless, O Bhavānī, we shall converse with this virtuous man;
for the company of the saintly is the supreme gain for human beings. (Hbhv_10.286)

Therefore, it was said by Śrī Dharaṇī to Śrī Prahlāda in the Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya: "Indeed, the fruit of the eyes is the sight of one such as you; the fruit of the body is contact with the limbs of one such as you."
Indeed, the fruit of the tongue is the chanting of your praises;
for those devoted to the Lord (bhāgavatas) are very rare in this world.

Therefore, Vidura said in the Third Canto (BhP 3.7.20): "Indeed, service on the paths to Vaikuṇṭha is difficult to attain for those of meager austerity, where Janārdana, the God of gods, is eternally praised. (Hbhv 10.288)
Śrī Videha also said in the Eleventh Canto [BhP 11.2.29]:
"A human body is difficult for embodied beings to obtain, as it is fragile and momentary;
even so, I consider the sight of the beloved of Vaikuṇṭha to be even more difficult to attain. (Hbhv_10.289)

For this very reason, Śrī Dhruva prayed in the Fourth Canto [BhP 4.9.11]: "O Infinite One, may I have constant association with those great souls of pure intention who flow ever more deeply in devotion unto You."
By which I, intoxicated by drinking the nectar of the stories of your virtues, may be led straight across the vast ocean of existence with its many calamities.
And in the *Pratyupadeśa* of the Pracetasas, it is stated by Śrī Śiva:
"Now, for those whose sins have been washed away by bathing internally and externally in the sacred waters of Your glory, O sinless-limbed One..."
For those whose nature is characterized by compassion for living beings and excellent virtue,
this meeting with you shall be a source of favor to us.
And by the venerable Pracetās:
"As long as we are touched by Your illusory power and wander here due to our karmas, may we have association with those who are devoted to You in birth after birth. (Hbhv 10.292)

Śrī Prahlāda also said in the Seventh Canto (BhP 7.9.24): "Therefore, I do not desire those blessings for embodied beings— longevity, prosperity, power, and sensory enjoyment— extending even as far as Brahmā."
"I do not desire your disheveled [hair], O you of great prowess;
lead me to the side of your own servant, whose nature is Time. Thus [ends the verse].
Now, the faults of association with the wicked:

In the words of the venerable Kātyāyana: "It is better to dwell within the cage of the flames of the fire-god than to endure the calamity of living among people who are averse to the meditation on Śauri."
In the *Pādma Purāṇa*, in the *Uttara-khaṇḍa*, within the dialogue between Śrī Umā and Maheśvara:
"Those Brahmins who are not Vaiṣṇavas are considered lower than even the Cāṇḍālas;
one should avoid conversing with them, touching them, or [sharing] the drinking of Soma and other such rites with them. (Hbhv 10.296)
In the third book, in the dialogue between Śrī Kapiladeva and Devahūti (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.31.33–35):
"Truth, purity, compassion, silence, intelligence, fortune, modesty, fame, forgiveness, tranquility, self-control, and majesty—these perish through association with him. (Hbhv_10.297)
One should not form an attachment to those who are unpeaceful, deluded, self-destructive, and wicked, nor to those pitiable ones who are like playthings for women. (Hbhv 10.298)

His delusion would not be as great, nor his bondage resulting from association with others, as that of a man arising from contact with a woman, or from contact with one who is associated with her. (Hbhv 10.299)
And in the eleventh book, in the dialogue between the Blessed Lord and Uddhava (BhP 11.26.3):
"One should never associate with the wicked, who are satisfied only by their genitals and bellies;
following them, one falls into blind darkness like a blind man following other blind men. (Hbhv_10.300)
Those who are devoid of devotion to the Blessed One are indeed the foremost among the wicked;
their end will never be auspicious, even through virtuous deeds. (Hbhv 10.301)
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, at the conclusion of the section on expiations (*prāyaścitta-prakaraṇa*):
"What is the use of the Vedas, or what use the scriptures, or what use the frequenting of sacred fords?
What is the use of austerities or what use sacrifices for those who are devoid of devotion to Viṣṇu? (Hbhv 10.302)
In the Śrī-Gāruḍa:
"Even if one has reached the end of the Vedas and knows the meaning of all the scriptures, if he is not devoted to the Lord of All, know him to be the lowest of men. (Hbhv 10.303)
In the third *skandha* [BhP 3.9.10]:
"By day, their senses are distressed by constant activity; at night, lying down, their sleep is shattered in an instant by thoughts of various desires."
O Lord, even the sages, whose compositions regarding worldly aims have been struck down by fate, continue to wander in this saṃsāra because they are averse to devotion toward you.

Therefore it is said in the sixth book [BhP 6.1.18]: "O King of kings, expiatory rites performed by one who is averse to Nārāyaṇa do not purify him, just as rivers cannot cleanse a jar of liquor. (Hbhv_10.305)
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"Whence can there be the destruction of sin for them, and whence can there be auspiciousness for them, in whose hearts Hari—the abode of all auspiciousness—is not established? (Hbhv 10.306)
Therefore, at the beginning of the "Story of the Hunter" (Lubdhakopākhyāna) in the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, it is said:
"Those who are devoid of worship of Hari, as well as those who hate the Vedas, and those who hate the twice-born and cows, are proclaimed to be Rākṣasas. (Hbhv_10.307)
Therefore, the instruction of Dharmarāja to his own messengers is found in the Sixth Canto [BhP 6.3.28–29]:
"Bring those who are wicked and turned away from the nectar-flavor of the lotus feet of Mukunda."
From this home, which is frequented by unattached paramahaṃsas who possess nothing, [I turn away] those whose thirst is bound to the path of hell.
The tongue does not utter the names and qualities of the Lord, the mind does not remember His lotus feet,
and the head does not bow even once to Kṛṣṇa.
Bring them here—those who are non-existent and have not performed their duties toward Viṣṇu.
In the *Skanda Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Bhagīratha, it is said:
"O best of kings, for whoever mocks the world of the *Bhāgavata*, his wealth, dharma, fame, and sons perish. (Hbhv 10.310)
Those fools who revile the high-souled Vaiṣṇavas fall, together with their ancestors, into the hell known as Mahāraurava. (Hbhv 10.311)
He strikes, reviles, hates, does not rejoice in Vaiṣṇavas, becomes angry, and feels no joy upon seeing them; these are the six falls. (Hbhv 10.312)
In that very work, the *Amṛtasāroddhāra*, it is stated by the venerable Yamaka:
"Whatever merit has been accumulated since birth—all of that goes to destruction if one should harass Vaiṣṇavas. (Hbhv 10.313)
In the *Dvārakā-māhātmya*, within the dialogue between Prahlāda and Bali:
"Those sinful ones who revile the high-souled Vaiṣṇavas are split apart by the extremely fierce saws of Yama’s command. (Hbhv 10.314)
Even if the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu, the soul of the universe, has been worshipped for hundreds of lifetimes,
he does not become pleased if a Vaiṣṇava is insulted.
And in the Tenth Canto (BhP 10.74.40):
"He who hears the censure of the Blessed Lord, or of one devoted to Him, and does not depart from it, he too goes downward, fallen from his merit. (Hbhv 10.316)
Therefore it is said in the Viṣṇudharmottara:
"The life of one devoted to Viṣṇu for even five days is better than a thousand kalpas of life for one devoid of devotion to Keśava. (Hbhv 10.317)
Therefore it is said at the end of the Aila-upākhyāna in the Śrī-Bhāgavata (BhP 11.26.26):
"Then, having abandoned bad association, the wise person should attach himself to the virtuous; for only the virtuous sever one's mental attachment through their instructions. (Hbhv 10.318)
Now, the procedure for meeting with Śrī-Vaiṣṇavas:
Having gone to those devotees of the Blessed Lord who are adorned with the auspicious marks, and having seen them from afar, one should joyfully prostrate like a staff. (Hbhv 10.319)
In the *Tejodravinapañcarātra*:
"A Vaiṣṇava, upon seeing another Vaiṣṇava, should prostrate like a staff upon the ground;
for between the two stands Viṣṇu, bearing the conch, the discus, and the mace. (Hbhv 10.320)
And regarding this, there is a specific point stated in the *Bṛhan-nāradīya* (1.25.41):
"A single act of disrespect toward an assembly hall, a sacrificial shed, or even a temple destroys the merit accumulated in the past. (Hbhv 10.321)
At a field of merit, at a sacred ford, and likewise at the time of Vedic study,
even a single prostration destroys previously accumulated merit.
Seeing a Vaiṣṇava who has arrived from another country, they should approach and embrace that Vaiṣṇava,
pleasing him by showing him their own Vaiṣṇavas.
And so it was said by the venerable Brahmā in the *Tejo-draviṇa-pañcarātra*:
"One should please a devotee who has taken refuge in Nārāyaṇa and arrived from another land by showing him those things that take refuge in Nārāyaṇa with devotion. (Hbhv 10.324)
Then, having satisfied a Vaiṣṇava with the nectar of his words, he should honor him like a true kinsman; otherwise, it is remembered that there is great fault.
Now, regarding the necessity of honoring Vaiṣṇavas,
it is stated in the Skanda Purāṇa, in the dialogue between Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya and Bhagīratha: "Indeed, he who, having seen a devotee of the Lord by chance, does not go toward him..."
Hari does not accept his twelve-year-long worship.
O protector of the earth, that house which does not receive a Vaiṣṇava who has come to it is abandoned by the ancestors and becomes as terrifying as a cremation ground. (Hbhv_10.327)
Alternatively, O tiger among kings, there is no one more devoted to sin than he who does not honor a Vaiṣṇava who has arrived from afar according to his own ability.
Seeing a weary devotee of the Lord, if the mind of one does not become softened but remains harsh, that evil-souled person is indeed worse than a dog-cooker (outcaste).
Upon seeing a brahmin who is a devotee of the Lord, yet distressed and troubled in mind,
Keśava does not grant him protection and does not become gracious toward him.
If one sees a brāhmaṇa who is a devotee of the Lord and does not honor him with a salutation, Hari indeed does not forgive the sin of that embodied being. (Hbhv 10.331)
O King, when a Vaiṣṇava departs from the householder's home unhonored,
he departs taking with him the merit accumulated over a hundred lifetimes.
O King, that sin which arises from transgressing against Vaiṣṇavas is incurred by those who eat on the day of Hari without first worshipping the ancestors and the gods. (Hbhv 10.333)
O protector of the earth, he who first shows honor but then treats Vaiṣṇavas with contempt goes to destruction along with his entire lineage. (Hbhv 10.334)
In the *Padma Purāṇa*, in the *Māhātmya* of Vaiśākha, within the dialogue between Yama and a Brāhmaṇa [PadmaP 5.96.69]:
"O Brāhmaṇa, that man who, upon seeing a Vaiṣṇava person, does not rise to greet him out of affection and respect, becomes a guest of hell. (Hbhv_10.335)
And in the Fourth Skandha [BhP 4.22.11]:

"Those houses which are devoid of the water from the feet of Him whose feet are the source of all holy places are indeed like trees in the lair of a serpent, lacking every kind of prosperity. (Hbhv_10.336)
Now, the praise of Viṣṇu in the Skanda Purāṇa:
"I am fortunate, I have accomplished my purpose, since you have come to my home."
The sight of Vaiṣṇavas is indeed as difficult to obtain as that of Hari himself.
Indeed, heaps of merit equal to Mount Meru and Mandara have been accumulated by me, since I have obtained the sight of the high-souled Vaiṣṇavas. (Hbhv 10.338)
In the tenth book, Śrī Nanda’s words to Śrī Gargācārya (BhP 10.8.4):
"O Blessed One, the great agitation of householders whose minds are dejected leads to their ultimate welfare; it never leads to anything else. (Hbhv 10.339)
In the Fourth Skandha [BhP 4.22.7, 10, 13–14]:
"O you who are the refuge of all auspiciousness, what auspicious deed of mine has occurred that there has been the sight of you, who are difficult even for yogis to behold? (Hbhv 10.340)
Even those householders who possess no wealth are truly fortunate and virtuous,
for their homes are masters over the water, grass, and ground that are most worthy of the noble ones.
O Protectors, is all well with us who perceive the objects of the senses, yet have fallen into this calamity brought about by our own karma? (Hbhv 10.342)
An inquiry regarding welfare is not appropriate for you who delight in the self,
wherein there exist no mental fluctuations of either wholesome or unwholesome nature.
Now, regarding the greatness of approaching Vaiṣṇavas,
in the Skanda Purāṇa, in the dialogue between the venerable Mārkaṇḍeya and Bhagīratha:
"O King, for one who goes face-to-face with Vaiṣṇavas..."
The twice-born experts in the Purāṇas declare that at every step one obtains the fruit of a sacrifice.
Now, the greatness of the praise of Vaiṣṇavas: In that very same place it is said—
"Whether directly or indirectly, whoever praises a Vaiṣṇava [is purified],
even if he is among men always a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa, a drinker of intoxicants, a thief, or one who violates his teacher's bed."
O best of kings, Viṣṇu has said that one is instantly liberated from sin. (Hbhv 10.345)
Furthermore:
"Whether directly perceived or beyond perception, those who indeed praise the Vaiṣṇava [path] cross the ocean of existence through the grace of Vāsudeva. (Hbhv 10.346)
Now, regarding the majesty of honoring Vaiṣṇavas:
in that very same *Amṛtasāroddhāra*, it is said—
"Food given with faith is digested within the fires of the Vaiṣṇavas."
And that food becomes equal to Mount Meru day after day.
Whoever offers even a mere drop of water to the Vaiṣṇavas during rites for the gods or the ancestors,
it becomes equal to the seven oceans and reaches the ancestors.
In the Viṣṇudharma:
"What is the use of gifts, or of austerities, or of various sacrifices performed?
Everything is accomplished for men by the worship of those devoted to Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 10.349)
A wise person should diligently honor these Vaiṣṇavas;
whatever is given to the Vaiṣṇavas according to one's own capacity shall become inexhaustible. (Hbhv 10.350)
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, within the narrative of Yajñamālya (NārP 1.36.59):
"O best of Brahmins, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are pleased with him who, with a mind fixed on Hari, honors those devoted to devotion for Hari. (Hbhv_10.351)
Even those who are sinners attain the supreme goal if they are devoted to the worship of Hari, whose souls delight in the name of Hari, and who are intent upon service [to them]. (Hbhv 10.352)
In that very place, at the beginning of the narrative of Yajñadhvaja (NārP 1.39.5):
"O best of sages, he who wishes to cross the ocean of saṃsāra should indeed devote himself to the devotees of Hari, who remove all sins. (Hbhv_10.353)
And at the conclusion of that [rite] (NārP 1.39.61–3, 65):
"He who, endowed with faith, feeds those devoted to Viṣṇu who are free from desire, goes to the abode of Hari together with twenty-one generations of his kin. (Hbhv 10.354)
Whoever gives even water or a fruit to a high-souled devotee of Viṣṇu who is free from desire, that person alone is dear to the Blessed One.
But those who perform service for those devoted to Viṣṇu go to the abode of Viṣṇu until the dissolution of all beings.
In whosever house one devoted to the worship of the gods always dwells,
all the gods as well as Śrī Hari abide right there.
In the Liṅga Purāṇa: "The wise man who is devoted to Nārāyaṇa, whose food he eats with a pleased mind—there is no doubt that his food has entered the mouth of Hari. (Hbhv 10.358)
Mādhava, the soul of the universe, becomes pleased even more than by all other forms of worship;
seeing the food of a devotee of the Lord, he who is affectionate toward his devotees partakes of it.
In the *Brahma-purāṇa*, the Blessed Lord spoke these words:
"O Lotus-born One, as soon as I saw the food offering placed before me, I accepted it; with the tip of my tongue, I taste the essence of the devotee. (Hbhv 10.360)
In the *Pādmottara-khaṇḍa* (253.176–8),
in the dialogue between Śrī Śiva and Umā:
"Of all forms of worship, the worship of Viṣṇu is supreme."
Therefore, O Goddess, the worship of those belonging to him is even more supreme than that.
Even after worshipping Govinda, if one does not worship His devotees in turn, he should not be known as a Bhāgavata; he is remembered merely as a hypocrite.
Therefore, a person should always worship the Vaiṣṇavas with great effort;
by honoring the great devotees of Viṣṇu, one crosses over the entire flood of suffering. (Hbhv 10.363)
In the eleventh [canto], there is the word of the Blessed Lord: "In a Vaiṣṇava, one should show hospitality toward kinsmen. (BhP 11.11.44, 11.19.21) // Hbhv_10.364 //
The worship of my devotees is superior.
Furthermore, in the *Skanda-purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya and Bhagīratha, it is said:
"Those who always worship Hari through action, mind, and speech—their word must be followed by men, for those men are equal to Viṣṇu. (Hbhv_10.366)
