For this very reason, there is the speech of Markaṇḍeya to Dhruva in the Skanda Purāṇa:
"By whomsoever the God of gods, Janārdana, has been worshipped even once, he attains the supreme station; this which I have spoken is the truth. (Hbhv 11.213)
Likewise, Aṅgīrasa said:
"Worship that Govinda, within whom all this exists and who has no end, if you desire the supreme state. (Hbhv 11.214)
Pulastya said:
By propitiating Hari—who is the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, and that eternal Puruṣa—one attains even liberation, which is exceedingly difficult to achieve. (Hbhv 11.215)
Regarding Pulaha:
Indra attained the supreme station of Indra by worshipping Viṣṇu, the Lord of the universe and Lord of sacrifice; therefore, O observer of noble vows, worship Him. (Hbhv 11.216)
Vasiṣṭha says:
When Viṣṇu is propitiated by the mind, one obtains whatever one desires, even a station within the three worlds—how much more so the most excellent of all? (Hbhv 11.217)
Whatever desires a woman or even a man may long for,
they attain those vast objects by propitiating Janārdana.
In the Agastya-saṃhitā:
"By worshipping Viṣṇu with his mind alone, a person obtains whatever fruit he desires—whether it be great or even small—without fail. (Hbhv 11.219)
A similar passage is found in the Viṣṇu Purāṇa as well, with this slight addition:
"O Prince, for those men who have not worshipped Govinda, there is no place [in heaven], O son of Marīci."
For the supreme state is not attained otherwise; therefore, worship the Imperishable One.
Furthermore, in that very same [text]:
"When Viṣṇu is propitiated, one attains terrestrial desires, heaven, as well as a station venerable even in heaven, and even the supreme nirvāṇa. (Hbhv 11.221)
Likewise, in the Brahmavaivarta [Purāṇa]: "Having placed the water from whose feet upon his head, Śiva dances;
from the lotus of whose navel arose Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds. (Hbhv 11.222)
Worship that Govinda, from whose agitation of the power of will arise the creation and destruction of the cosmic egg, if you desire the supreme state.
In the *Nārasiṃha-purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Sahasranika:
"O lord of men, he who constantly worships Narasiṃha shall partake in heaven and liberation; no doubt should be entertained in this matter. (Hbhv_11.224)
Therefore, having become single-minded through a vow for as long as life lasts, one attains one's desired goal by worshipping Narasiṃha. (Hbhv 11.225)
In that very place, within the dialogue between Śrī Vyāsa and Śuka, following the conversation between Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya and Mṛtyuñjaya:
"But while being cooked in hell, he was rebuked by Yama:
'Why was the Lord Keśava, the destroyer of afflictions, not worshipped by you? (Hbhv 11.226)
If even water cannot be obtained when material goods are unavailable, why was that Lord—
who gives his own world— not worshipped by you?
Why was that Narasiṃha, the Lord of the Senses (Hṛṣīkeśa), whose eyes resemble lotuses, who grants liberation to men upon being remembered—not worshipped by you? (Hbhv 11.228)
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, within the section on the majesty of Aditi, it is stated by Śrī Sūta:
"Where one is devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, there obstacles do not cause affliction;
indeed, neither kings, nor thieves, nor diseases exist there. (Hbhv 11.229)
Pretas, piśācas, kuṣmāṇḍas, grahas, and likewise bālagrahas,
as well as ḍākinīs and rākṣasas, do not afflict one who worships Acyuta.
In that very same [text], in the dialogue between Yama and Bhagīratha:

"Having worshipped Acyuta even with leaves, flowers, or fruits, yet devoid of formal ritual worship, he goes to the realm of Viṣṇu's presence (sālokya), accompanied by seventy generations of his lineage. (Hbhv 11.231)

In that very same context, regarding the greatness of hoisting the banner, it is said in the *Śrī-Viṣṇudūta*: "Even those who merely hear one's name once at the time of death attain the supreme abode; how much more so for one who is devoted to serving [the Lord]? (Hbhv 11.232)
He who stays in the temple of Hari for even a moment or half a moment goes to the supreme abode; how much more so one who is devoted to his service?
In that very place, the sage Vibhāṇḍaka spoke to King Sumati:
"O Indra among kings, even a deed performed involuntarily yields a very great fruit for men; how much more so, then, a proper act of worship? (Hbhv_11.234)
At the conclusion of the section on expiation:
"Whether through association or out of delusion, he who worships Hari is liberated from all sins and goes to the supreme state. (Hbhv 11.235)
When Janārdana is worshipped, all obstacles perish, purity of mind arises, and one indeed attains supreme liberation. (Hbhv_11.236)
The eternal human goals known as dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa are accomplished for those devoted to the worship of Hari; of this there is no doubt.
All sacred fords, sacrifices with their constituent parts, and the Vedas, O most virtuous ones—
even these do not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of the worship of Nārāyaṇa.
In the *Śrī-Viṣṇu-toṣa-vidhi-praśnottara*:
"I speak the truth; I speak what is beneficial; I speak the essence again and again.
In this world where the non-essential is predominant, the worship of Viṣṇu is the only essence. (Hbhv 11.239)
Regarding the greatness of the anointing:
even for those who perform the worship of Viṣṇu but once, even unintentionally, the bondage of worldly existence never arises again for them. (Hbhv 11.240)
At the conclusion of the narrative of Yajñadhvaja:
"Therefore listen, O best of Brahmins: the imperishable Lord Nārāyaṇa grants liberation to those who worship him, whether they know him or not. (Hbhv 11.241)
Those who worship Mahāviṣṇu, the destroyer of the distress of those who have sought refuge in him, are to be saluted, they are to be honored, and especially to be prostrated before. (Hbhv 11.242)
Those bulls among the wise who, free from longing, worship either Hari or Hara—
they alone purify the entire world.
In the *Padma-purāṇa*, within the dialogue between Śrī Nārāyaṇa and Nārada concerning the procedure for worship:
"For my devotee who performs my worship according to the prescribed injunctions, no obstacle arises even in a dream; indeed, he is fearless. (Hbhv 11.242)
In that very same [text], within the *Vaiśākha-māhātmya* during the dialogue between Nārada and Ambarīṣa:
"The Unconquered One (Ajit), when worshipped with devotion, bestows sons, wives, long life, sovereignty, heaven, and liberation—indeed, everything desired. (Hbhv 11.245)
Even those ancestors in both lineages who have long been submerged in hell go to heaven right there when one worships Hari through the recitation of the Sūta [Purāṇa]. (Hbhv 11.246)
In that very same *Śrī-Yama-Brahma-Saṃvāda*:
"O wise one, who could attain the worlds without worshiping Hari with devotion?
When Hari is worshiped, all desires are held in the palm of one's hand. (Hbhv 11.247)
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*, within the *Śrīkṛṣṇāmṛtastotra*:
"Even he who worships Acyuta but once is most blessed in this world; how much more so one who, endowed with faith, worships him every day with flowers. (Hbhv 11.248)
Even those who constantly behold and worship Vaiṣṇavas go to the abode of Viṣṇu; how much more so, then, those who serve Viṣṇu himself?
He is a yogi, he is one whose self is purified, he is peaceful, he is of great intelligence;
he is pure and he is perfected—the man who serves Kṛṣṇa.
In the Agastya-saṃhitā: "Those whose minds are focused on no other, constantly counting with their rosary beads while chanting 'Rāma, Rāma,' fix their minds upon the ocean of the nectar of bliss."
Some, having dissolved [themselves] and become nectar-like, abide in bliss.
Some, devoted to his service, sleep in palaces and other dwellings;
they look upon him as if he were a human being and interact with him like kinsmen.
Furthermore:
Just as injunctions and prohibitions do not approach one who is liberated,
so too, O Rāma, they do not touch a devotee who has practiced according to the prescribed rule.
In the Śrī Bhagavad Gītā (12.1):
"Of those who, thus constantly disciplined, worship You as the Personal Being, and those who worship the Imperishable and Unmanifest—the former among them are the best knowers of yoga. (Hbhv 11.254)

Thus questioned by Arjuna, the Blessed Lord said: "Those who, fixing their minds on Me, worship Me with constant discipline, endowed with supreme faith—they are considered by Me to be the most perfectly disciplined. (12.2)
In the Fourth Skandha [BhP 4.21.31]:
"The desire for service at whose feet [removes] the impurity of the intellect accumulated over all births of even the ascetics..."
It destroys instantly while increasing day by day,
just like a river flowing from the big toe of the foot.
Furthermore, in the words of Nārada (BhP 4.31.14): "Just as by watering the root of a tree, its trunk, branches, and twigs are all satisfied,"
Just as the sacrifice of the vital breath is the supreme offering for the senses,
so too is the worship of the Imperishable the highest honor for all.
And in the eleventh book, the words of the poet Yogeśvara [BhP 11.2.33] state:
"I consider the constant service to the lotus feet of Acyuta here to be free from fear from any quarter."
When the mind is free from agitation due to the non-existence of a self-nature, fear ceases there along with the notion of a universal self.
And from the Śrī Bhāgavatam (BhP 11.27.49):
"Thus, by means of the paths of ritual yoga—both Vedic and Tantric—a person worshipping me on both fronts attains from me his desired perfection. (Hbhv 11.259)
Moreover:
"He who worships me in this way attains bhakti-yoga; he indeed finds me alone through the yoga of devotion with complete detachment. (BhP 11.27.53) (Hbhv 11.260)
In the Gautamīya Tantra, it is said that Śrī Nārada,
who is affectionate toward his devotees, sells his own self to his devotees for the mere price of a single tulasī leaf and a handful of water. (Hbhv 11.261)
Now, regarding the constancy of worship, it is said in the Mahābhārata:
[He who] protects like a mother, the agent of creation and destruction.
One who does not worship the Lord of Gods, one should know him to be a slayer of Brahman.
Therefore, it is said at the beginning of the account of the greatness of the water from the feet (pādodaka) in the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*:
"O twice-born one, that house in which the procedure for the worship of Hari is not performed, one should know to be like a cremation ground; one should never enter it. (Hbhv 11.263)
For this very reason, it is said in the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"Whether with flowers, or with leaves, or with fruits, or even with water, one should worship the Lotus-eyed Lord, having abandoned hundreds of other duties. (Hbhv 11.264)
Furthermore, in the Nāradīya [Purāṇa]:

"And on all auspicious occasions, according to the specific requirements of each particular time, one should worship the Lord of the God of Gods, having diligently procured the necessary materials. (Hbhv 11.265)
Therefore, it was said by the Blessed Lord Hayagrīva in the *Hayashīrṣapañcarātra*: "An installed image must not be abandoned; one should worship it for as long as one lives.
It is better to give up one's life or even to have one's head cut off. (Hbhv 11.266)
Through worship, constancy was written [in him], as well as the prior consumption of the food offering;
and the supreme majesty [of the Lord] was attained through the context of the Śālagrāma discus. (Hbhv 11.267)
Whatever greatness of the constituent elements of worship was previously described, all of that indeed naturally culminates here in this very worship. (Hbhv 11.268)
How many elephants intoxicated by the greatness of their own worship, roaming the forest of the scriptures, can be captured by an insect without the power of Śrī Hari? (Hbhv 11.269)
Now, one should always and in every way serve the name of the glorious Blessed One; its greatness, which is renowned everywhere, is here written down in brief.
Now follows the majesty of the name of the Blessed Lord and the practice of its specific aspects,
as instructed out of compassion by the sages for those whose souls are afflicted by various desires. (Hbhv 11.271)
Now, regarding the greatness of serving the specific names of the Blessed Lord according to one's particular desire,
therein, for the purpose of destroying sin,
in the Śrī-Kūrma [Purāṇa]:
Preceded by the word "Śrī," with the word "Jaya" in the middle,
and likewise followed by two instances of "Jaya," the name "Narasiṃha" was thus recited twenty-one times.
When recited, it shall destroy even the sin of killing a Brahmin.
For the purpose of warding off great fear,
Śrīnarasiṃha is located in that very place; he is twice victorious, and furthermore, he is to the north.
For one who recites it twenty-one times, it wards off great fear.
However, for the sake of auspiciousness at a specific time,
it is stated in the *Viṣṇudharmottara*, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra:
"The Person, Vāsudeva, and likewise the powerful Saṅkarṣaṇa..."
One should recite Pradyumna and Aniruddha in successive years.
One should likewise praise Balabhadra and Kṛṣṇa during both solstices;
as well as Mādhava, Puṇḍarīkākṣa, and indeed Bhogasaṃyina.
O tiger among men, one should sequentially praise Padmanābha, Hṛṣīkeśa, and likewise the god Trivikrama during the spring and other seasons.
And Viṣṇu, the slayer of Madhu, as well as the god Trivikrama,
Vāmana, Śrīdhara, and likewise Hṛṣīkeśa.
Dāmodara, Padmanābha, Keśava— the best of the Yadus—
Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, and likewise Govinda, in due order.
And during the months beginning with Caitra, one should recollect the God of gods—
Pradyumna and Aniruddha— during the dark and light fortnights respectively.
One should thus recollect [the Lord] in sequence among the foremost [deities] beginning with Aditi: as Sarva, Śarva, Śiva, Sthāṇu, Bhūtādi, Nidhi, and Avyaya. (Hbhv 11.280)
Viṣṇu is the universe, the utterance *vaṣaṭ*, and the Lord of the past, the future, and the present;
he is the sustainer of beings, the creator of beings, existence itself, the self of all beings, and the abode of all beings.
The unmanifest, the lotus-eyed, the architect of the universe, the pure-flowing,
the source of existence, the creator, the sustainer, the origin, the lord, and the sovereign.
Immeasurable, Lord of the Senses, Lotus-navelled, Lord of the Immortals, Ungraspable, Eternal, Sustainer, Kṛṣṇa—let one remember the Consciousness;
these are the names of the God of Gods, O Yādava, beginning with Kṛttika. (Hbhv 11.283)
Brahmā, Śrīpati, Viṣṇu, Kapila, the Lord Śrīdhara,
Dāmodara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Govinda, and Madhusūdana.
O Great King, one should meditate upon the Lord as the Supporter of the Earth, holding a mace, a conch, and a lotus, and likewise as the wielder of the discus, starting from the first [mudrā].
Or rather, O Yādava, everything at all times indeed belongs to the God of gods.
All names belong to Janārdana,
and all time belongs to the hero among men;
therefore, the name of the omnipresent one is always [to be recited].
O King, one may choose whatever is desired from the Granter of Boons.
And regarding the accomplishment of various desires, it is stated by Pulastya: "Kāma, Kāmaprada, Kānta, Kāmapāla, and likewise Hari."
Ānanda and Mādhava should likewise recite [the mantra] for the complete attainment of their desires.
Rāma, Paraśurāma, Nṛsiṃha, Viṣṇu,
and Vikrama— these and others should be recited by those desiring to conquer their enemies.
One should constantly practice the sacred knowledge; Puruṣottama is to be recited as a mantra.
A man who has fallen into bondage should always recite the name Dāmodara.
One should indeed constantly recite the name Keśava Puṇḍarīkākṣa for all afflictions of the eyes, and Hṛṣīkeśa in times of fear.
One should recite the *acyuta* and *amṛta* mantras during medicinal rites;
when going forth to face battle, one should call to mind the *aparājita*.

One who travels abroad constantly seeking security should always remember the wielder of the discus, the wielder of the mace, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, and likewise the wielder of the sword, in the directions beginning with the east.
A person should always remember Ajita, Adhipa, Sarva, and likewise Sarveśvara with devotion during all worldly activities.
One should always invoke Nārāyaṇa during sneezing, stumbling, and the like,
as well as when afflicted by planets or constellations, and in all instances of distress caused by deities.
In the face of enemies such as bandits, in the presence of dangers from tigers, lions, and the like,
and in blinding darkness or intense gloom, one should recollect Narasiṃha.
When a fire has broken out, one should call to mind the One who reclines upon the waters;
by recollecting the one whose banner is Garuḍa, the potency of poison is dispelled.
During bathing, worship of the deity, burnt offerings, prostration, and circumambulation, one who is devoted to Him should proclaim the name of the Blessed One as "Vāsudeva. (Hbhv 11.298)
When wealth, grain, or other possessions are being established, or when malice born of wickedness arises, one should, with a focused mind, perform the chanting of the names of Ananta and Acyuta.
In a bad dream, one should always remember Nārāyaṇa, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, the bearer of Śrī, the Supreme Person, Vāmana, and Khaḍgin. (Hbhv 11.300)
A person should remember Balabhadra reclining on a couch in the great ocean and other such places;
for the sake of prosperity, one should likewise remember him performing all his various deeds.
One who praises the Lord of the World with devotion for the sake of offspring does not come to grief;
one should quickly glorify the Lord of Śrī in rites intended for all-encompassing prosperity.
Indeed, when all portents of death appear, one should always recite the Viśoka mantra;
in the face of deaths caused by wind-storms, precipices, fire, water, imprisonment, and the like—
whether occurring through one's own agency or that of another— the wise person should recite the name of Vāsudeva.
One should proclaim the name of the God of gods, the wielder of the discus, who is endowed with the power for all purposes, whichever name he himself prefers for all purposes.
One attains the accomplishment of all goals through the single meaning of these names;
for all these names belong to the Supreme Brahman, Hari. (Hbhv 11.304)
Likewise, in the Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, it is said:
"Furthermore, one should remember the Tortoise, the Boar, or the Fish when crossing water;
for kindling fire, one should mutter the name unbrokenly. (Hbhv 11.306)
By recollecting the one whose banner is Garuḍa, a person is liberated from calamities;
moreover, fever, head diseases, and the potency of poisons are pacified. (Hbhv 11.307)

O King, one who desires victory in battle should worship Balabhadra at the commencement of agriculture; one who desires success in trade should worship Halāyudha; and one who desires prosperity should worship Rāma during the northern course of the sun.
One should praise Viṣṇu, the auspicious one among all auspicious things;
rising, a man should praise Viṣṇu, and while sleeping, Madhava;
at the time of eating, Govinda, and everywhere, Madhusūdana.
In that very same work, it is stated elsewhere:
"One should contemplate Viṣṇu while taking medicine, Janārdana while eating, Padmanābha while sleeping, and Prajāpati during sexual intercourse. (Hbhv 11.310)
One should meditate on Cakrin when enraged in battle, Trivikrama when facing displacement from one's station, Nārāyaṇa during the ritual release of a bull, Śrīdhara upon meeting with a beloved,
Vārāha in the midst of water, and Jalaśāyin within the sacrificial fire.
In the forest, remember Narasiṃha; on the mountain, the joy of the Raghus; for a bad dream, Govinda; for purity, Madhusūdana;
for illusions, the divine Vāmana; and in all undertakings, Mādhava. (Hbhv 11.312)
Furthermore:
"O Yādava, one should invoke Vāsudeva even when he has not been specifically mentioned;
likewise, O King, at the commencement of any undertaking, one may invoke his name as one pleases. (Hbhv 11.313)
O King, indeed all names belong to Him;
they lead to the accomplishment of every goal for a person.
Therefore, the name of Kṛṣṇa may certainly be used according to one's desire.
In all undertakings, one should recite with devotion.
In that regard, the quality of uprooting all sins,
as well as the general majesty of chanting the holy name of the Blessed Lord, has been described by Nārada in the *Viṣṇu-dharma* and the *Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya*:
Oh, how perfectly pure you are! For passion indeed arises in those who chant the glories of Hari, dispelling all darkness for men like the rising sun. (Hbhv 11.315)
O Garuḍa, let men not fear the blazing fire of sin;
it is destroyed by the drops of water from the masses of clouds that are the name of Govinda. (Hbhv 11.316)
By the mere recitation of whose name even one who is powerless is instantly liberated from all sins, just as deer are freed when terrified by a lion. (Hbhv_11.317)
The chanting of the Name with devotion is the unsurpassed dissolution of all sins, O Maitreya, just as fire is for the elements.

He upon whom the mind is fixed does not go to hell; even heaven is an obstacle when he is being contemplated; and for one whose self and mind are absorbed in him, even the world of Brahmā seems insignificant. He, the Imperishable, dwelling in the hearts of men of pure intellect, bestows liberation.
What wonder is there that sin goes to its dissolution when Acyuta is glorified? (Hbhv 11.319)
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"By thus performing the glorification of the God of gods in the evening and in the morning, one is liberated from all sins and is honored in the heavenly world. (Hbhv_11.320)
In the Vāmana [Purāṇa], it is said that on earth there was a man named Nārāyaṇa, renowned as a thief among men.
It removes, without exception, the entire accumulation of sins gathered over many lifetimes, merely by being heard.
In the Skanda Purāṇa it is said:
"Whether uttered with devotion or devoid of devotion, the cry 'Govinda' burns away all sins like the fire that arises at the end of an eon. (Hbhv 11.322)
Whosoever on the surface of the earth bears the name Govinda,
even his sin goes away in a thousand ways through the mere chanting of it.
In the *Kāśī-khaṇḍa*:
"Just as even a spark of fire might burn if touched through negligence, so too the name of Hari, when merely touched by the lips, burns away evil. (Hbhv 11.324)
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, at the conclusion of the narrative concerning the hunter:
"For men blinded by sense objects and whose minds are agitated by the sense of 'mine,' the single name of Hari alone is the destroyer of all sins. (Hbhv_11.325)
For this very reason, it was said by Yama in that same place: "Alas, alas! Those men who have uttered 'Hari' even once under the pretext of being a thief..."
Mortals whose path has been lost within the womb of their mother do not enter into my cloth-painting.
In the *Pādmapurāṇa*, within the *Māhātmya* of Vaiśākha, at the conclusion of the narrative of Devaśarman, in the words of Śrī Nārada:
"Ten thousand killings, a thousand acts of drinking [liquor],
and the violation of ten million teachers' wives— "
Many thefts were instantly destroyed by the one dear to Hari, who bears the name Govinda.
Just as fire burns when touched even against one's will,
so too does the name of Govinda burn, even if uttered under a pretext.
In that very same work, in the dialogue between Śrī Yama and the Brāhmaṇa, it is said:
"By the mere chanting of the names of Kṛṣṇa Viṣṇu, whose splendor is immeasurable, all sins dissolve like darkness at the rising of the sun. (Hbhv 11.329)
O best of the twice-born, I see no other expiation for living beings that pacifies all sins than the chanting of the name of the Elephant (Gajendra). (Hbhv 11.330)
In the sixth book [of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 6.2.7–11]:
"For this person has indeed exhausted the consequences of even ten million births of sins, since, though helpless, he uttered the name of Hari, which is the source of all well-being. (Hbhv_11.331)

A thief, a drinker of liquor, a betrayer of friends, a slayer of a Brahmin, one who violates the teacher’s bed, a killer of women, kings, ancestors, or cows, and others who are perpetrators of mortal sins (pātakin). Hbhv_11.332.
For all who have committed sins, this alone is the perfect atonement:
the utterance of the name of Viṣṇu, since it directs the mind toward Him.
A sinner is not purified by expiations, nor by the recitation of Vedic hymns, nor likewise by vows and other such rites,
in the same way as he is purified by the utterance of the name-words of Hari.
That [faith] brings about the perception of the qualities of the One of Excellent Renown.

Whether used as a conventional sign, in jest, as a rhythmic filler (stobha), or even in derision, they know that the utterance of the name of Vaikuṇṭha removes all sins without exception. (Hbhv 11.335)
Whether fallen, stumbled, broken, bitten, tormented, or struck,
a person who involuntarily utters the name "Hari" does not deserve the torments of hell.
Whether through ignorance or through knowledge, the chanting of the name of the One of Supreme Renown burns away a person's sin, just as fire consumes fuel.

Even a killer of a Brahmin, a killer of a father, a killer of a cow, a killer of a mother, or a killer of a teacher, as well as one who eats dog-meat or a Pulkasa, may be purified by the chanting of his name. (Hbhv 11.338)

Whatever sin exists in the present, whatever has occurred in the past, and whatever will occur in the future— all that is swiftly consumed by the chanting of the name of Govinda, which is like a fire. (Laghu-bhāgavatam 11.339)
But he who is always intent on harming virtuous people on this earth becomes pure and blessed by the chanting of the name of Hari. (Hbhv 11.340)
In the *Kūrma Purāṇa*:
"Whatever millions of purifying sites exist upon the surface of the earth, they do not equal even a fraction of the merit found in the chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s name. (Hbhv_11.341)
In the *Bṛhad-Viṣṇu Purāṇa*:
"A sinful person cannot commit a transgression that would equal the power of this name of Hari in the removal of sin. (Hbhv 11.342)
In this supreme history,
even one who relishes [worldly pleasures] is unable to commit sins with effort to the same extent as the power of Viṣṇu’s name exists for the destruction of inauspiciousness.
Especially in the Kali age, as stated in the Skanda Purāṇa:
"In this world, there is no deed born of body, speech, or mind that does not destroy sin in the Kali age, except for the chanting of Govinda's name. (Hbhv 11.344)
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:

"Water is sufficient for the quenching of fire; the rising of the sun is for the dispelling of darkness; but for the pacification of the flood of sins in the Kali age, the chanting of the names of Hari is [the remedy]. (Hbhv 11.345)
By chanting the names of Hari, a person, liberated from the flood of sins, goes to the further shore of saṃsāra;
that man is truly born in the Kali age despite its defects.
Having swiftly destroyed evil—what is there to wonder at in this?
In the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa:
"O Giver, such purification of the self does not occur here through miserable cāndrāyaṇa or tapta-kṛcchra penances."
In the Kali age, whatever [merit] arises here by the single act of chanting the name of Govinda, O Mādhava— [that is what is attained].
Regarding the purification of the lineage and assembly of those who perform *kīrtana*,
it is said in that very same place:
"Even one burdened with great sins should chant the name of Hari incessantly."
Having become pure in his inner heart, he becomes a sanctifier of the assembly.
He who, with single-minded devotion, joyfully chants "Govinda," by that purifying and auspicious person this earth is sustained. (Laghu-bhāgavata 11.349)
In the *Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya*:
"And thus, the Vaiṣṇava tongue does not protect its speaker alone;
for by proclaiming the fame of the Lord, it purifies the entire world. (Hbhv 11.350)
In the tenth book (10.4.17): "By merely uttering Your name, one instantly purifies all listeners as well as oneself; how much more so, then, for one who has been touched by Your foot? (Hbhv 11.351).

Therefore it was said by Prahlāda in the Nārasiṃha Purāṇa: "O Nṛsiṃha, those virtuous ones who, filled with joy, loudly sing Your name, are the unconditional kinsmen of all living beings. (Hbhv 11.352)
Regarding the destruction of all diseases,
the *Bṛhan-nāradīya-purāṇa*, in the context of pleasing the Blessed One, states:
"Terrified by the utterance of the names Acyuta, Ānanda, and Govinda..."
All diseases perish; I speak the truth, the absolute truth.
In the *Parāśara-saṃhitā*, in the words of Vyāsa addressed to Sāmba: "O Sāmba, suffering born of disease is not to be abandoned even by other medicines;
having drunk the medicine that is the name of Hari, the disease is to be cast off—of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv 11.354)
In the Skanda Purāṇa:
"I bow to that Ananta, by whose remembrance and whose name-recitation mental afflictions and physical diseases dissolve at that very moment. (Hbhv_11.355)
In the Vahni Purāṇa:
"A man covered by a great disease or afflicted by the threat of being killed by a king shall become free from fear upon chanting the name 'Nārāyaṇa'. (Hbhv 11.356)
Regarding the quality of pacifying all suffering,
the *Bṛhad-Viṣṇu-Purāṇa* states:
"It is the pacifier of all diseases and the destroyer of all calamities."
The chanting of the names of Hari brings peace and removes all calamities.
In the Brahmavaivarta [Purāṇa]:
"The chanting of Hari’s name pacifies all sins, destroys all calamities, and brings about the end of all suffering. (Hbhv 11.358)
In the twelfth chapter (12.12.48):
"The Blessed One Ananta, whose majesty has been heard, when glorified, indeed [destroys] the calamities of men."
Having entered the mind, it shakes off everything without exception, just as the sun dispels darkness or a strong wind scatters the clouds.
In the Viṣṇudharmottara:
"Those who are afflicted, despondent, weak, and terrified, and those who are beset by terrible diseases,"
By chanting even once the single word "Nārāyaṇa," they become happy, freed from suffering.
Through the chanting of the praises of Viṣṇu, the God of gods, who possesses immeasurable splendor,
there is the subduing of yakṣas, rākṣasas, vetālas, bhūtas, pretas, and vināyakas.
The ḍākinīs flee, as do others such as the Siṃhaka;
the recitation of his name is known to remove all misfortunes. (Hbhv 11.362)
Furthermore:
Having performed the recitation of the name during hunger, thirst, stumbling, and so forth, one swiftly attains freedom from all misfortunes; of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv 11.363)
In the *Pādmapurāṇa*, within the hymn of Devahūti:
"In worlds that are always ablaze with the flickering flames of delusion, one who has entered the shade of the cloud that is His name is never burned. (Hbhv_11.364)
Regarding the destruction of the Kali age, it is stated in the Skanda Purāṇa:
"Let there be no fear of the sharp-fanged, wicked serpent that is the Kali age."
Burnt by the forest fire of the name Govinda, he will be reduced to ashes.
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya-purāṇa*, in the section concerning the dharma of the Kali age:
"Those men who are devoted to the name of Hari in the terrible Kali age have indeed accomplished all that is to be done; for the Kali age does not afflict them. (Hbhv_11.366)
"Hari! Keśava! Govinda! Vāsudeva! O you who are composed of the universe!"—those who constantly utter these names are indeed not afflicted by the Kali age.
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
“O tiger among men, Kali does not afflict those people who constantly perform the glorification of Vāsudeva, the sustainer of the world. (Hbhv 11.368)
Regarding the power of delivering those in hell,
as described in the *Nārasiṃha-purāṇa*:
"In whatever manner the denizens of hell chant the name of Hari,"
In that very manner, carrying devotion toward Hari, they went to heaven.
In this supreme history,
it is said that for men of sinful deeds who are being cooked in hell,
liberation from there arises through the chanting of the names of Hari. (Hbhv 11.370)
The destruction of *prārabdha* karma is described in the sixth chapter [of the Bhagavad Gītā] (6.2.46):
"There is no means superior to this for severing the bondage of karma."
For those desiring liberation, by the chanting of the names of the Lord whose feet are the source of all holy places,
the mind— which otherwise would be turbid with passion and ignorance— is no longer attached to worldly actions. (Hbhv 11.371)
And in the twelfth [chapter] (12.3.44): "Whatever name a man, while dying, afflicted, falling, or stumbling, utters involuntarily— "
With the bolt of karma removed, he attains the supreme destination;
people will not worship him in the Kali age.
Having been described as "bound by karma" and likewise as "the thorn of karma," it culminates in *prārabdha* (commenced karma),
because its state of being necessarily experienced has been reached.
Therefore, in the *Bṛhannāradīya*:
"The person who, with senses restrained, chants 'Govinda' every day, becomes liberated from all sins and shines like a god. (Hbhv 11.374)
Regarding the state of being the recipient of all offenses,
it is stated by the Blessed Lord in the *Viṣṇuyāmala*:
"He who shall proclaim my names in this world with faith..."
I shall indeed forgive even ten million of his offenses; of this there is no doubt.
The quality of effecting the fulfillment of everything is found in the eighth book (8.23.16), in the words of Śrī Śuka addressed to the Blessed Lord:
Through the recitation of your praises, every deficiency—whether arising from mantras, tantras, place, time, or appropriate materials—is rendered entirely flawless. (Hbhv 11.376)
And in the Skanda Purāṇa:
"I bow to that Acyuta, by whose remembrance and utterance of his name, whatever is deficient in asceticism, sacrifice, ritual acts, and so forth, immediately attains completeness. (Hbhv 11.377)
Regarding its superiority over all the Vedas,
it is stated in the *Viṣṇudharmottara* in the words of Śrī Prahlāda: "Indeed, the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and also the Atharvaveda..."
He by whom the two syllables "Ha-ri" have been uttered has truly studied the Vedas.
In the *Skānda-purāṇa*, in the speech of Śrī Parvatī, it is said:
"O dear one, do not recite any Ṛg-verses, Yajus-formulas, or Sāman-chants;
instead, sing constantly the name of Hari, 'Govinda,' as a song. (Hbhv 11.379)
And in the *Pādmapurāṇa*, in the *Śrī-Rāmāṣṭottara-śata-nāma-stotra*, it is stated: "Even a single name of Viṣṇu is considered superior to all the Vedas;
yet the name of Rāma is remembered as equal to the *Rg-veda’s* Thousand Names (*Rg-veda-sahasranāma*). (Hbhv_11.380)
Regarding its superiority over all other holy places, the Skanda Purāṇa states:
"What need has he for Kurukṣetra, or what need for Puṣkara?"
He on whose tip of the tongue the two syllables "Ha-ri" reside—Hbhv_11.381.
Vāmana:
One obtains all those thousands of millions and hundreds of millions of sacred fords simply by chanting the name of Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 11.382)
In the *Viśvāmitra-saṃhitā*:
"Many well-known holy places (*tīrtha*) exist in great numbers, yet they are not equal even to a ten-millionth part of [the merit gained] from chanting the name of Hari. (Hbhv 11.383)
In the Laghu-bhāgavatam: What is the use of the extensive Vedas, Āgamas, and Śāstras, or even of numerous holy fords? What purpose do they serve?
If you desire the cause of liberation for yourself, cry out clearly, "Govinda! Govinda! 11.384.

The performance of every meritorious deed, the gift of ten million cows, and residing for a kalpa in the waters of the Gaṅgā at Prayāga during the transit of the sun— [all these are surpassed by this].
Ten thousand sacrifices and the gift of gold as vast as Mount Meru are not equal to even a hundredth part of Govinda’s glory.
In the Baudhāyana Saṃhitā:
"Even though very many ritual acts of sacrifice and public works have been performed, they are indeed causes for worldly existence; however, the name of Hari alone grants liberation. (Hbhv 11.386)
In the *Garuḍa Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Śrī Śaunaka and Ambarīṣa:
"O protector of the earth, if you constantly desire the fruit of thousands of Vājapeya sacrifices, rise in the morning and perform the glorification of Govinda. (Hbhv_11.387)
O leader of men, what will you achieve through Sāṅkhya, and what through Yogas? O king of kings, if you desire liberation, perform the glorification of Govinda. (Hbhv 11.388)
In the third book (3.33.7), in the speech of Devahūti to the illustrious Lord Kapila:
"Oh, alas! Even a dog-eater is more venerable than this."
Those who hold your name upon the tip of their tongue have performed austerities, offered oblations, practiced sacred rites, and recited the Veda; they are the noble ones who invoke your name.
Regarding the granting of all spiritual goals,
it is stated in the *Skanda Purāṇa*, within the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada concerning the greatness of the four-month period (*caturmāsya-māhātmya*):
"This [practice] is the supreme means for removing the company of the wicked and for subduing enemies."
For this chanting of the names of Viṣṇu has its root within the self.
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"Having thus placed his desired wish in his heart, O best of the twice-born, he who recites even a single name [of the Lord] shall obtain a hundred wishes. (Hbhv 11.391)
In that very work, the *Śrī-Kṛṣṇāmṛta-Stotra*, it is said:
"The divine glorification of Vāsudeva is the most auspicious of all auspicious things, bestowing long life, destroying disease, and granting both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (Hbhv 11.392)
In the *Śrī-Nārāyaṇa-Vyūha-Stava*:
"Those men who take up the name of Viṣṇu even through jests, mockery, and the like, have achieved their life's purpose; let there be salutations again and again to them as well. (Hbhv 11.393)
And in the Vārāha [Purāṇa]:
"Blessed are they, successful are they, and by them alone has merit been performed—those who, having reached the attainment of birth, proclaim me at the proper time. (Hbhv 11.394)

Especially in the Kali age, those who utter this name of Hari even once—which is difficult for those of unrefined self to obtain—are undoubtedly successful in their purpose; of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv 11.395)
And in the eleventh book (11.5.36):
"The noble ones, born of virtue and partaking of the essence, celebrate the Kali age, wherein every goal is attained through mere chanting. (Hbhv 11.396)
In the Skanda Purāṇa, in that very same place: "Likewise, the chanting of the glories of Śrī Hari is the supreme austerity in the world;
one should especially practice it in the Kali age for the sake of pleasing Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 11.397)
The possession of all powers is as stated in the Skanda Purāṇa:
"And those [powers] which reside in giving, vows, austerity, pilgrimage to sacred sites, and so forth..."
The auspicious powers of the great gods are removers of all sins.
Having drawn forth all the [meanings] of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices, as well as of knowledge and the inner spiritual reality, Hari established them within his own names. (Hbhv 11.399)
Therefore, even the wind from the name of Hari is unbearable for the wicked, just as the sun is to all masses of darkness. (Hbhv 11.400)
Therefore, in the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa it is said:
"One should employ whatever name is pleasing to the God of gods, the wielder of the discus, who is endowed with the power for all purposes, in all matters. (Hbhv 11.401)
Regarding the state of being the source of joy for the world, it is said in the Śrīmad-Bhagavad-gītā (11.36): "O Hṛṣīkeśa, it is fitting that by Your glorification..."
The world rejoices and is filled with affection;
the *rākṣasas* flee in fear toward the quarters,
and all the hosts of *siddhas* pay homage.
The quality of being worthy of worship by the world is stated in the Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa:
"O Nārāyaṇa, O Lord of the World, O Vāsudeva, O Janārdana!"
Those who constantly utter this are indeed honored everywhere.
In that very place, at the conclusion of the account of Yajñadhvaja, the illustrious Sūta said:
"Whether sleeping, eating, walking, standing, or speaking, those who utter the name of Hari—to them, eternal salutations, salutations! (Hbhv 11.404)
In the *Śrī-Nārāyaṇa-vyūha-stava*:
"Whether they be women, Śūdras, Pukkaśas, or others born of sinful wombs—whoever chants the name of Hari with devotion, to them also, here, salutations again and again! (Hbhv 11.405)
The state of having no other refuge but this single refuge is stated at the beginning of the recitation of the *Bṛhatsahasranāma* in the *Padmapurāṇa*:
"O scorcher of foes, even those mortals who enjoy worldly pleasures have no other refuge [than you]."
Devoid of knowledge and dispassion, and lacking celibacy and other such virtues.
Even all those who are righteous do not reach that destination which those who have abandoned all phenomena and who utter only the name of Viṣṇu attain with ease.
The state of being always and everywhere worthy of service is established in the Viṣṇudharma within the narrative of the Kṣatriya:
"In that [dharma], there is no restriction of place, nor likewise any restriction of time."
O hunter, there is no prohibition against eating the remnants [of food] regarding the name of Śrī Hari. (Hbhv 11.408)
In the Skanda Purāṇa, in the Vaiśākha-māhātmya of the Padma Purāṇa,
and in the Viṣṇu-dharmottara, it is said:
"One should always and everywhere chant the names of the one whose weapon is the discus."
There is no impurity in reciting it, because he is one whose hands are purified.
Furthermore, according to the *Skandha*:
"It does not depend on purity and so forth regarding place, time, or state; rather, this name is independent and grants whatever is desired. (Hbhv 11.410)
In the Vaiśvānara-saṃhitā:
"There is no restriction of place or time, nor any determination of purity or impurity;
O Rāma, one is liberated simply by the supreme recitation of 'Rāma, Rāma'. (Hbhv_11.411)
In the *Vaiṣṇava-cintāmaṇi*, the words of Śrī Nārada to Śrī Yudhiṣṭhira:
"O King, there is no restriction of place, nor likewise any restriction of time;
there is no doubt in this matter regarding the chanting of the names of Viṣṇu. (Hbhv_11.412)

There is a proper time for giving and for sacrifice; there is a proper time for standing and for the recitation of mantras; but for the chanting of the names of Viṣṇu, there is no such time on this earth.
In the second book [of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 2.1.11]:
"O King, for those yogis who are weary of worldly existence and desire freedom from fear from all quarters, the chanting of the names of Hari has been determined as the means. (Hbhv_11.414)
Regarding the bestowing of liberation,
it is stated in the Vārāha-purāṇa:
"That man who [calls upon] Nārāyaṇa, Acyuta, Ananta, and Vāsudeva..."
If one constantly recites [this], one indeed goes to the state of being a wrestler.
In the Gāruḍa [Purāṇa]: "O leader of men, what will you achieve through Sāṅkhya, and what through Yogas?
O king of kings, if you desire liberation, perform the glorification of Govinda. (Hbhv 11.416)
As it is said in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Padma-purāṇa:
"By whomsoever the two syllables 'Ha-ri' have been uttered even once, the girdle has been fastened by him for the journey toward liberation. (Hbhv 11.417)
In the *Brahma-purāṇa*:

"Even one who is impure or whose mind is distracted, if he should constantly chant the name of Hari, shall obtain liberation through the destruction of his faults, just like the Lord of Cedi. (Hbhv_11.418)
In the *Pādmapurāṇa*, within the hymn of Devahūti, it is said:
"He who, unwearied, utters the name Nārāyaṇa even once, having become pure in his inner self, attains liberation. (Hbhv_11.419)
Even one who is addicted to the wives of others or who commits injury against others becomes pure and attains liberation through the chanting of the names of Hari. (Hbhv 11.420)
In the Vaiśampāyana-saṃhitā:
"One who has fallen outside of all dharma and is likewise devoted to every kind of sin is liberated by the recitation of Viṣṇu’s name; there is no doubt in this matter. (Hbhv 11.421)
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya* (1.2.49):
"Whatever is non-existent, whether it be proclaimed or even merely heard, by that means even sinners become purified; those who are already pure attain liberation. (Hbhv 11.422)
In this division of Bharata,
the two syllables "Ha-ri" are the provisions for the journey at the departure of life, the medicine for the disease of saṃsāra, and the protection against suffering and grief. (Hbhv 11.423)
In the Nāradīya [Purāṇa]:
"Whatever new and ever-fresh names belong to Murāri, each of which is nourished by the nectar of song,"
Those who, having cast off shame, sing with joy, are liberated while living; of this there is no doubt.
In the first book [of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa]:
"He who, having fallen into this terrible cycle of transmigration, utters its name while powerless, is instantly liberated from it—that which even fear itself fears. (BhP 1.1.14) Hbhv_11.425.

In the third [chapter], in the *Brahma-stuti* (BhP 3.9.15): "Those who, at the time of the departure of life, being helpless, chant the names of Him whose incarnations, qualities, and activities are mere imitations [of worldly forms]..."
Having suddenly cast off the impurities of many births, they go to that unveiled immortality; I take refuge in that Unborn One.
In the sixth [chapter] (BhP 6.3.24): "For men, this much is sufficient for the removal of sin:
the congregational chanting of the qualities, deeds, and names of the Blessed One."
Even the sinful Ajāmila, while calling out to his son as he was dying, attained liberation by crying "Nārāyaṇa! (Hbhv_11.427)
And the power of leading one to the realm of Śrī-Vaikunṭha is stated in the *Laiṅga Purāṇa* by Śrī Śiva to Śrī Nārada: "Whether walking,
standing, sleeping, eating, breathing, or in the completion of speech..."
The chanting of Viṣṇu’s name destroys the Kali age even when done casually;
by doing so, one attains one's true nature, and being endowed with devotion, one goes to the Supreme.
In the Nāradīya, the venerable Brahmā said:
"A brāhmaṇa who eats the food of a dog-cooker, especially one who is menstruating, or who eats cooked food prepared with liquor, attains Hari upon death by chanting His name. (Hbhv 11.429)
Having abandoned the accumulation of a flood of sins born from eating forbidden food and approaching those who should not be approached, he,
liberated from the bonds of existence, attains the same world as Viṣṇu.
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya* [1.11.101], Śrī Bali said to Śukra:
"He on whose tip of the tongue the two syllables 'Ha-ri' reside attains the world of Viṣṇu, from which a return [to this world] is difficult to obtain. (Hbhv 11.431)
In the *Padma*:
"Whether standing anywhere at all, one should chant 'Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa';
with his soul purified of all sins, he shall go to the supreme goal. (Hbhv 11.432)
In that very same *Vaiśākha-māhātmya*, Nārada said to Ambarīṣa:
"That alone is the supreme merit and the most purifying document for going to the abode of Govinda."
That alone is the sole sacrificial session of merit in the world which is called by the mere name of Keśava.
In the Brahmavaivarta [Purāṇa], having thus uttered the name of Hari under the pretext of naming his son Saṅgrahaṇī,
he went at the time of death to that supreme abode of Hari. (Hbhv 11.434)
Even Ajāmila, though a vessel of impurity, went to the abode of the Lord by uttering the name "Nārāyaṇa" under false pretenses; how much more so for one who recites it with faith?
In the Sixth Canto [BhP 6.2.49]:
"Even Ajāmila went to the abode of Hari while dying, chanting the name of Hari as it was uttered by his son; how much more so for one who chants it with faith! (Hbhv_11.436)
In the Vāmana [Purāṇa]: "Those who glorify the boon-granter, whose feet are excellent, who has the lotus as his navel,
and who holds in his hands the conch, lotus, discus, arrow, bow, mace, and sword..."
Those whose eyes are like bees to the lotus-face of Padmālayā surely go to the abode of the Slayer of Madhu.
In the Āṅgirasapurāṇa:
"A person who, out of fear of worldly existence, utters the name 'Vāsudeva,' is liberated from that [fear] and attains the very station of Viṣṇu; of this there is no doubt. (Hbhv 11.438)
In the Nandipurāṇa:
"Even those who commit sins at all times and on every occasion, by chanting the Name, go to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 11.439)
Especially in the Kali age, as stated in the twelfth book [of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 12.3.51]: "O King, in this Kali age, which is a storehouse of defects, there is indeed one great virtue."
By the mere chanting of Kṛṣṇa's names, one whose attachments have been liberated shall go to the Supreme.
As it is said in the *Garuḍa*:
"O King of Kings, if you desire supreme knowledge, or that state which is higher than knowledge, then with diligence perform the glorification of Govinda. (Hbhv 11.441)
Regarding the fact that it pleases the Blessed Lord,
the *Vārāha-purāṇa* states: "By chanting the names of Vāsudeva, even one who has drunk liquor or is afflicted by disease [is purified]."
One who is liberated will certainly be born [as such], for Mahāviṣṇu is pleased.
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya* (1.34.23):
"O Brahmins, when one constantly chants the names of Viṣṇu during hunger, thirst, stumbling, and so forth, Adhokṣaja becomes truly pleased with him. (Hbhv 11.443)
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"O fortunate one, Keśava is pleased with whoever utters the name of Viṣṇu even during moments of hunger, thirst, or stumbling. (Hbhv 11.444)
Now, regarding the power of subjugating the Blessed Lord, it is said in the *Viṣṇu-rahasya*:
"That which is attained by worshipping Hari with devotion in the Kṛta age— even through hundreds of sacrifices— "
In the Kali age, one obtains the complete fruit through the chanting of Govinda’s names.
In the Ādipurāṇa:
"And having sung my names, one shall wander in my presence;
I tell you this truth, O Arjuna: I am purchased by him. (Hbhv 11.446)
"And having sung my names, one shall wander in my presence;
I tell you this as the truth, O Arjuna, for I have been purchased by him. (Hbhv 11.447)
Thus, having heard my names in this way, and so forth... [Hbhv_11.448]
In the Viṣṇudharma, Prahlāda said:
"Victory is his, victory is his, victory is truly his—of him for whom the two syllables 'Ha-ri' reside at the tip of the tongue. (Hbhv 11.449)
Its status as the supreme human goal by its very nature is stated in the Kāśī-khaṇḍa of the Skanda Purāṇa and in the Vaiśākha-māhātmya of the Padma Purāṇa.
For this alone is auspiciousness, this alone is the acquisition of wealth, and this alone is the fruit of life: the chanting of Dāmodara’s praises.
In the *Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa*:
This most sweet and auspicious essence, the very nature of consciousness, is the true fruit of all the creepers of the Vedas and the most auspicious among all auspicious things.
O best of the Bhṛgus, even if recited but once— whether with faith or even playfully— the name of Kṛṣṇa can deliver even an ordinary human being.
In the *Viṣṇurahasya*:
"This alone is the supreme knowledge; this alone is the supreme austerity;
this alone is the supreme reality—the glorification of Vāsudeva. (Hbhv_11.452)
In the *Vaiṣṇavacintāmaṇi*, within the dialogue between Śrī Śiva and Umā: "The remembrance of Viṣṇu, which cuts away sins, is accomplished with great effort;
however, glorification (*kīrtana*) by the mere movement of the lips is superior to that. (Hbhv_11.453)
And elsewhere it is said:
"O Bhārata, in the mouth of one by whom Vāsudeva was worshipped in former hundreds of births, the names of Hari always abide. (Hbhv 11.454)
Especially in the Kali age, as stated in the Rahasya:

"By worshipping Hari with devotion in the Kṛta age even through hundreds of sacrifices, one obtains the complete fruit; in the Kali age, that same fruit is obtained by chanting the names of Govinda. (Hbhv 11.455)
In the Viṣṇu Purāṇa (6.2.17):

"Whatever one attains by meditating in the Kṛta age, by sacrificing with rituals in the Tretā, and by worshipping in the Dvāpara, that one attains in the Kali age simply by chanting the name of Keśava. (Hbhv_11.456)

That which is achieved by meditating upon Viṣṇu during the Kṛta age, by worshipping Him with sacrifices during the Tretā age, and by ritual service during the Dvāpara age, is attained in the Kali age through the chanting of Hari’s names. (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 12.3.52)
In the eleventh [chapter] (BhP 11.5.32):

"The wise indeed worship Him who is dark-complexioned, yet not black by luster, together with His limbs, secondary limbs, weapons, and attendants, primarily through sacrifices consisting of congregational chanting. (Hbhv 11.458)
And in the Skanda [Purāṇa]:
"In the Kali age, the great devotees of the Lord constantly perform kīrtana."
In the *Bṛhannāradīya* [1.40.115], it is stated by Nārada:
"The name of Hari alone, the name alone, the name alone is my life;
in the Kali age, there is no other way, indeed there is none, indeed there is none. (Hbhv 11.460)
Therefore it has been said:
"Even as they utter but once the name of Hari, which is of the nature of consciousness, even the thousand-faced Brahmā is not capable of describing its fruit. (Hbhv 11.461)
In the *Pādmottara-khaṇḍa*, within the *Śrī-rāmāṣṭottara-śata-nāma-stotra*, Śrī Śiva said:
"O Goddess, as one hears the names beginning with the letter 'ra' in this hymn, my mind constantly experiences joy through the contemplation of Rāma’s name. (Hbhv_11.462)
In the Vaiṣṇava-cintāmaṇi:
"I am the lord of all worlds, for I am the reciter of the names of Viṣṇu;
I speak the truth, the absolute truth: this name of Hari is the refuge of men. (Hbhv 11.463)
And in the *Ādi-purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna:
"O Pārtha, those living beings who chant my name with faith or even in jest—my heart always dwells within their hearts. (Hbhv_11.464)
There is indeed no knowledge equal to it, no vow equal to it,
no meditation equal to it, and no fruit equal to it.
Truly, there is no renunciation like this; truly, there is no tranquility like this;
truly, there is no merit like this; truly, there is no destiny like this.
Furthermore:
Name alone is supreme liberation; name alone is the supreme goal;
name alone is supreme peace; name alone is supreme stability.
The name alone is supreme devotion; the name alone is supreme understanding;
the name alone is supreme joy; the name alone is supreme mindfulness.
Name alone is the cause for a living being; name alone is the lord;
name alone is the supreme object of worship; and name alone is the highest teacher.
Furthermore:
"The man who feels affection upon seeing people endowed with virtuous names goes to the supreme abode and rejoices together with Viṣṇu. (Hbhv 11.470)
Therefore, O Kaunteya, with a firm mind, take refuge in the names;
one who is joined with the Name is dear to us—be joined with the Name, O Arjuna! (Hbhv 11.471)
Now, the majesty of chanting the name of the Blessed Lord, as well as that of remembering and hearing it, is briefly written down according to their slight distinctions.
Now, regarding the majesty of chanting the holy names,
in the *Viṣṇu-rahasya* it is stated by the Blessed Lord:
"O men, I speak the truth with my arms raised high."
To him who, while living, daily recites "Mukunda, Narasiṃha, Janārdana," I grant his desired object at the time of death, even if he is like a stone or a piece of wood, as if I were a debtor.
In the *Kāśī-khaṇḍa*, within the hymn to Agnibindu: "O Nārāyaṇa! O Savior from the ocean of hell! O Dāmodara! O Slayer of Madhu! O Four-armed One!"
"O Viśvambharā! O Virajā! O Janārdana!"—for those who chant these names here, where is birth, and where is the fear of Death?
In the *Pādma Purāṇa*, within the *Māhātmya* of Vaiśākha, in the dialogue between Yama and a Brāhmaṇa:
"O Brāhmaṇa, even those people who are doers of evil, if they are intent upon the chanting of Vāsudeva, the terrible messengers of Yama do not approach them. (Hbhv_11.475)
In the *Bṛhad-Viṣṇu Purāṇa*:
"Where is the ascent to the vault of heaven, which is characterized by rebirth?
Where is the recitation of 'Vāsudeva,' the unsurpassed seed of liberation? (Hbhv 11.476)
The greatness of remembering the names of the Blessed One is found in this supreme history:
even in a dream, there is remembrance of the name of the Original Person.
It brings about the destruction of the accumulated heap of evil;
how much more so, then, when the fire of Janārdana, the Primordial Being, is invoked with effort?

O King, those among men who remember the name of Hari and cause others to remember it during the Kali age are certainly fortunate and have achieved their life's purpose; thus says the *Laghu-bhāgavata*. (Hbhv 11.478)
In the *Devahūti-stuti* of the *Pādma-purāṇa*:

"Salutations to that Self of Consciousness, by the remembrance of whose name the flood of sins of men is instantly destroyed, both at the time of departure and at the time of non-departure. (Hbhv_11.479)

In that very same Northern Section: "By the mere remembrance of whose name, even for sinners, liberation occurs swiftly—a liberation that is extremely difficult even for those such as Brahmā to attain. (Hbhv 11.480)
In the Brahmavaivarta [Purāṇa]:
"The man whose grass-like karma has been consumed by the forest fire of meditation upon Him becomes purified and beholds Keśava, both manifest and unmanifest. (Hbhv 11.481)
Therefore, for this living being fallen into the ocean of existence,
none other than Hari is skilled in granting the support of a hand.
In the Jāvāli-saṃhitā:
"The name of Hari is the supreme object to be chanted, meditated upon, sung, and praised in manifold ways by one who desires various forms of liberation. (Hbhv 11.483)
Now, regarding the majesty of the name of the Blessed Lord,
as spoken by Śrī Nārada in the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*:
"Even those who are great sinners, by merely hearing His name..."
How shall I, with a weary mind, praise those who have attained such purity?
In this supreme history, whether heard or even merely recited, the wondrous deeds of Hari burn away all sins; how much more so when done with devotion through incidental association? (Hbhv 11.485)
In the sixth book [BhP 6.16.44], in the words of Citraketu:
"O Blessed One, it is indeed not impossible that through the sight of You, all the sins of men are destroyed."
Indeed, by hearing [this] even once,
even a Pukkaśa is liberated from saṃsāra.
Thus,
although the majesty of all the glorious names is equal,
there is nevertheless a certain distinction regarding the incarnations of Kṛṣṇa himself for some [devotees].
Now, specifically regarding the majesty of the incarnation of Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
as stated in the *Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa* within the *Śrī Kṛṣṇāṣṭottara-śata-nāma-māhātmya*:
"Whatever fruit is obtained by reciting three times the thousand meritorious names..."
But by a single repetition, it bestows even one name of Kṛṣṇa.
Having recited this, the victorious Kirīṭin,
who possessed the Pāśupata weapon and was the very life-breath of Kṛṣṇa, obtained Kṛṣṇa as his charioteer.
What is the use of speaking at length? One who is filled with human bliss, having finally attained the bliss of Brahmā, shall reach union with Kṛṣṇa.
And in the *Vārāha-purāṇa*, within the *Śrī-Māthura-māhātmya*, it is said:
"In that place, O my beloved, there shall be secret names of mine—meritorious, purifying, and destroyers of saṃsāra. (Hbhv 11.491)
In that very context, specifically within the *Dvārakā-māhātmya* in the dialogue between Prahlāda and Bali, the greatness of the name "Śrī-Kṛṣṇa" is described:
"Seven generations of men have passed away, and fourteen are yet to come."
In the Kali age, a person delivers all beings by chanting "Kṛṣṇa."
Whether sleeping, waking, or walking, he who constantly utters "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa,
Kṛṣṇa" during the Kali age shall indeed become one whose very form is Kṛṣṇa.
In the *Brahmavaivarta*, it is said:
"Having intentionally killed a Brahmin or having drunk liquor, O Kṛṣṇa, one shall attain purity by chanting 'Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa' day and night. (Hbhv 11.494)
In the Viṣṇudharma:
O King of kings, for whomsoever the auspicious name "Kṛṣṇa" proceeds upon the tongue, millions of great sins are reduced to ashes. (Hbhv 11.495)
In the *Nārasiṃha Purāṇa*, as spoken by the Blessed Lord:
"Whoever remembers me constantly, saying 'Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa,' I lift him out of hell, just as a lotus rises up after piercing through the water. (Hbhv 11.496)
In the *Garuḍa* and *Padma* [Purāṇas]:
"A man bitten by the serpent of saṃsāra, for whom there is no other remedy, shall be liberated upon hearing the Vaiṣṇava mantra 'Kṛṣṇa'. (Hbhv 11.497)
In the *Prabhāsa-purāṇa*:
"O scorcher of foes, my name known as Kṛṣṇa is the most preeminent of all names;
it is the supreme expiation for all sins and the liberator from them. (Hbhv 11.498)
In the *Pādmapurāṇa*:
"Wherever one may be situated, if one should chant 'Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa,' with one's self purified of all sins, that person shall go to the supreme goal. (Hbhv_11.499)
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*, within the *Śrīkṛṣṇasahasranāmastotra*:

"O Beloved of the Cowherd women, O Kṛṣṇa, what is the use of those various other means? Rather, your name, when awakened and present at the tip of the tongue, indeed wards off great fear. (Hbhv 11.500)
In that very same place, elsewhere it is said:
"O Śambhu, I tell you the truth: this which I must conceal from others, known as Kṛṣṇā and called 'The Reviver from Death,' take heed of it. (Hbhv 11.501)
O descendant of Bharata,
at the time of death, whatever living being gives up its life while uttering "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa," [attains the Supreme].
The first word is conceived for his liberation;
the other two remain standing, bowed with shame, as if covering themselves.
Elsewhere it is also said:
"Kṛṣṇa is the wish-fulfilling gem, the embodiment of the essence of consciousness;
he is full, pure, and eternally liberated because of the distinction between name and the named. (Hbhv 11.503)
Therefore it has been said:
"Homage be to them, whose sandals are expert in delivering those submerged in the thick mud of the ocean of existence."
For those who, upon hearing the two syllables "Kṛṣṇa," experience a surge of bliss and their hair stands on end, [there is no need for further practice]. (Hbhv 11.504)
Furthermore, in the second book [of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 2.3.24]: "Alas, this heart is as hard as stone,
since it is not shattered even when seized by the names of Hari!"
When there is no transformation, nor tears in the eyes, nor horripilation on the body hairs; Hbhv_11.505 //
And in the *Itihāsottama*:
"That man in whose body no horripilation arises when the name of Viṣṇu is proclaimed would be like a thunderbolt. (Hbhv 11.506)
In the Kātyāyana-saṃhitā:
"Those men who do not increase the merit born from the chanting of the Name shall be afflicted by various diseases throughout a hundred births. (Hbhv 11.507)
That is a loss, that is a great flaw, that is delusion and that is confusion,
when Vāsudeva is not meditated upon for even a moment or an instant.
In the *Pādmapurāṇa*, within the *Māhātmya of Vaiśākha* during the dialogue between Yama and a Brāhmaṇa:
"Those men who depart while disregarding the glorification of the Blessed One go to a terrible hell because of that sinful deed. (Hbhv_11.509)
The Śrutis:
"O Viṣṇu, we who know your name, which is indeed distinguished by greatness, partake of your benevolent thought. (Hbhv 11.510)
Oṃ tat sat oṃ. Approaching the station of the god with reverence, they have attained glory and renown;
they have assumed even the names worthy of sacrifice.
At the end of the auspicious [state], they rejoice upon seeing one another.
Oṃ! O singers, fulfill from birth that ancient germ of Cosmic Order (ṛta) as you know it;
knowing him, discern even his name.
O Viṣṇu, we partake of your great benevolence.
"Thus, etc. means: "Those who, regarding such greatness of the Name as is determined by the Śrutis and Smṛtis, imagine it to be mere *arthavāda*, go to terrible torments. (Hbhv 11.513)
Now follows the refutation of the theory that the names of the Blessed Lord are *arthavāda*,
from the *Śrī-Kātyāyana-Saṃhitā*:
"The man who imagines the name of Hari to be mere *arthavāda*..."
That most wicked among men clearly falls into hell.
In the *Brahma-saṃhitā*, in the words of the Blessed Lord addressed to Baudhāyana:
"Having heard of the various fruits resulting from chanting His names, one who does not have faith in them, but considers them to be mere empty words..."
Whosoever is human, him I cast here into this heap of suffering, his limbs tormented by the various agonies of the terrible cycle of existence.
And in the Jaimini-Saṃhitā:

"Those who declare that the passages in the Śrutis, Smṛtis, and Purāṇas which speak of the greatness of the Name are merely *arthavādas* (laudatory statements), for them there is no end to their stay in hell. (Hbhv 11.516)
And regarding that name, O Blessed One, which brings benefit to the world as a whole and is to be served by all the universe,
a wise person should avoid transgressions.
For it has been said by Sanat-kumāra to Śrī Nārada in the Pādma [Purāṇa]:
"Even one who has committed every offense is liberated by taking refuge in Hari. (Hbhv 11.518)

Even one who commits offenses against Hari— if he should ever take refuge in the Name— he certainly crosses over by means of that Name alone, for the dust of the feet of the twice-born is [the very ground] upon which the Name rests.
For even from an offense against one who is a friend to all, by [offending] the Name, one falls downward.
Now, regarding the offenses against the Name,
they were stated by that very [author]:
"Censuring the virtuous constitutes the supreme offense against the Name."

For how could one endure the censure of that which has attained renown? Indeed, he who perceives with his intellect any part of Śiva or Śrī Viṣṇu—be it their qualities, names, or anything else—as distinct, truly brings harm to the name of Hari. (Hbhv 11.521)

Disrespect toward the guru, reviling the Vedas and the scriptures, as well as interpreting the name of Hari according to its literal meaning— if one possesses such a sinful intellect despite the power of the Name— [he is lost].
For him, purification through the restraints does not exist.
Even the equality of all auspicious activities— such as religious observances, vows, renunciation, and burnt offerings—
is negligence when directed toward one who lacks faith, is averse, or does not listen.
And that instruction which is an offense against the name of Śiva.
Even when the greatness of the Name has been heard, that base person who is devoid of affection,
being preoccupied with "I" and "mine," commits an offense against the Name as well.
Even when some offense against the Name has occurred through negligence,
one should always chant the Name and remain with that alone as one's sole refuge.
The destruction of offenses has been stated by that very same [author] in that very place: "For those possessed of the offense of [not using] the Name, the names themselves remove the evil."
When applied without interruption, those very same [practices] are effective for achieving their purpose.

That single name, whether it has entered the path of memory or reached the root of the ear— whether its syllables are pure or impure, and whether it is uttered clearly or indistinctly— truly delivers one,
even if that name is situated amidst the body, wealth, worldly people, greed, and heresy.
O Brahmin, once it has been cast away, it would not quickly produce fruit in this world.

Therefore it has been said by the venerable Nārada in the Bṛhan-nāradīya: "Since even the great gods are unable to reach the further shore of His names, how can one of meager intellect worship Him, when even the Manus and the lords of sages [cannot do so]? (Hbhv 11.528)
Thus:
In this manner, devotion to the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa should always be practiced by the wise;
and that [devotion] arises through His grace, which results from great merit. (Hbhv 11.529)
Now, regarding the rarity of glorious devotion,
it is stated by Śrī Parāśara in the Skanda Purāṇa: "Indeed, [this devotion] does not arise in this world for those who lack merit, for the deluded, or for those of crooked nature."
Devotion arises toward Govinda, as well as mindfulness and chanting of his name.
In that very place, it is stated by the venerable Brahmā:
"O Nārada, in this world, for mortals who have not burnt away all their sins, devotion to Keśava does not arise even for a moment or half a moment. (Hbhv 11.531)
In the Yoga-vāsiṣṭha:
Through austerity, knowledge, and meditative absorption over thousands of previous births, devotion to Kṛṣṇa arises in those men whose sins have been exhausted. (Hbhv 11.532)
In the Ādivārāha [Purāṇa]:
"Having propitiated the Bull-bannered Lord over thousands of other births, the wise man attains the state of a Vaiṣṇava once all his sins have been destroyed. (Hbhv 11.533)
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya-purāṇa* (1.39.51–52), at the conclusion of the narrative of King Yajñadhvaja:
"Only for those who have accumulated merit over thousands of millions of births will there arise pure devotion toward Janārdana, the God of gods. (Hbhv 11.534)
Bathing in the Ganges is easily accessible, as is the honoring of guests;
all sacrifices are likewise easy to perform, but devotion to Viṣṇu is extremely difficult to attain.
In the *Itihāsa-samuccaya*, in the passage concerning the practice of gathering gleanings (*śiloñcha-vṛtti*), it is said:
"Death in the Gaṅgā, firm devotion to Keśava, and the awakening of the knowledge of Brahman—these are not the fruit of minor austerity. (Hbhv 11.536)
In the Agastya-saṃhitā:

"Because [the goal] is not accomplished even in ten million lifetimes through vows, fasts, and observances, nor by various sacrifices, devotion to Keśava arises [only through another means]. (Hbhv 11.537)
In the *Viṣṇudharmottara*:
"Whether for a day, half a day, or even for a single *muhūrta*, through the destruction of all sins, devotion toward Keśava arises. (Hbhv 11.538)
After thousands of various births in different wombs,
devotion to Keśava arises in a living being who is free from defilement.
In the tenth book, in the speech of Uddhava to the gopīs (BhP 10.47.24):

"Indeed, devotion to Kṛṣṇa is accomplished through multitudes of gifts, austerities, fire-offerings, recitations, Vedic study, self-restraint, and various other means of spiritual welfare. (Hbhv 11.540)
In the Śrī Bhagavad-gītā (7.28):
"But those people of meritorious deeds whose sin has come to an end—they, freed from the delusion of dualities, worship Me with firm resolve. (Hbhv 11.541)
Regarding what was examined in the fifth book, Śrī Bādarāyaṇa said [BhP 5.6.18]:
"O King, he who is the lord, the guru, the sufficient protector, the deity, the beloved, and the head of the clan of you Yadus— where is he now, and where are you, his servants?"
Let it be so, my dear; the Blessed One Mukunda grants liberation to those who worship him, but never indeed the yoga of devotion.
At the end of the Vṛtra episode in the sixth book [BhP 6.14.2]:
"Devotion to the feet of Mukunda generally does not arise among the gods, who are composed of pure *sattva*, nor among the sages of stainless soul. (Hbhv 11.545)
Salutations to that glorious devotion, by whose power even this restless worm desires to lift up Mount Mandara, the final peak of the churning. (Hbhv 11.546)
Now, regarding the majesty of devotion to the Blessed Lord (*śrī-bhagavad-bhakti-māhātmya*),
first is the fact that for one possessing devotion, even if some sin should somehow occur, there is no need for any other atonement (*prāyaścitta*).
This is stated in the *Vaiśākha-māhātmya* of the *Padma-purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Nārada and Ambarīṣa (*PadmaP* 5.85.31):
Just as a fire with well-kindled flames reduces fuel to ashes, so too does devotion to the Blessed One burn away all evils in that very instant. (Hbhv 11.547)
At the beginning of the story of Ajāmila in the sixth book (BhP 6.1.15):
"Some, solely through devotion, being devoted to Vāsudeva, shake off their sin entirely, just as the sun dispels the mist. (Hbhv 11.548)

And in the eleventh book, in the dialogue between the Blessed Lord and Uddhava (BhP 11.14.19): "Just as a fire with well-kindled flames reduces fuel to ashes, so too, O Uddhava, devotion directed toward Me completely consumes all sins. (Hbhv 11.549)
Therefore, it has been stated in that very same place by the venerable Karabhājana (Śukadeva Gosvāmī):
"To his beloved devotee who worships at the root of his own feet and has renounced all other inclinations, Hari, the Supreme Lord... [BhP 11.5.42].
And whatever improper action has arisen in any way, he who is seated within the heart shakes it all off.
In the *Dvārakā-māhātmya*, the Blessed One said to Candraśarman:
"For those men who carry devotion to me, whether in this world or in the next, no inauspiciousness exists; it shall lead even ten million generations of their lineage to liberation. (Hbhv 11.551)
Even while experiencing sense objects, the state of one's devotee being free from their defects is described in that very same Eleventh Skandha [BhP 11.14.28]:
"Even when assailed by sense objects, my devotee whose senses are unsubdued..."
Generally, one is not overcome by sense objects when possessed of bold devotion.
Regarding the state of abandoning the authority over ritual action,
it is said in that very same place [BhP 11.20.9]:
"One should perform ritual actions as long as one does not become weary of them."
Or rather, until faith arises toward listening to my teachings and so forth.
Therefore it is said in the First Canto [BhP 1.5.17]:
"If one who has abandoned his own duty and is yet immature should fall after worshiping the lotus feet of Hari,"
Wherever it may have been, what good fortune has accrued to him, or what purpose has been achieved by those who have followed their own dharma?
And that which has been written regarding the characteristic of single-mindedness and the taking of refuge—
this document shall attain great firmness through those very words.
The quality of clarifying the mind is stated in the First Skandha [BhP 1.2.6]: "That indeed is the supreme dharma for men, from which devotion toward Adhokṣaja arises."
It is causeless and unimpeded, by which the self becomes perfectly serene.
Therefore it is said in the Eleventh Canto [BhP 11.14.22]:
"Indeed, dharma endowed with truth and compassion, or knowledge accompanied by austerity, does not properly purify the self if it is devoid of devotion to Me. (Hbhv 11.557)
In that very context [BhP 11.14.21]:
"Devotion fixed upon me purifies even dog-cookers from the moment of their birth. (Hbhv 11.558)
In the sixth [chapter] (BhP 6.3.22):
"In this world, this alone is remembered as the supreme duty for men:
the yoga of devotion toward the Blessed One through the chanting of His names and other such means. (Hbhv_11.559)
Thus it is said in the Padma Purāṇa:
"What is the use of many mantras for him, or what use are scriptures with great elaboration?
What is the use of thousands of Vājapeya sacrifices for one who has devotion to Janārdana? (Hbhv 11.560)
The quality of being served by all virtues and so forth is found in the fifth book (*pañcama-skandha*) in the speech of Prahlāda (*BhP* 5.18.12):
"He who possesses unselfish devotion to the Blessed Lord..."
There, the gods abide together with all their virtues;
but for one who is not devoted to Hari, how can there be great virtues,
as he runs outward after that which does not exist even in his imagination?
In the fourth [skandha], regarding Śrī Dhruva, Manu said to him (BhP 4.11.30):
"Then you [should meditate] upon the Lord within the inner self, who is infinite, consisting of pure bliss, and endowed with all potencies."
Having cultivated supreme devotion, you will gradually sever the deeply rooted knot of ignorance consisting of "I" and "mine."
To Śrī Pṛthu, the venerable Sanaka and others said:
"By devotion to the playful grace of the petals of whose lotus feet, the virtuous untie the tightly knotted accumulation of karma."
In the same way, even ascetics whose minds are not empty and who have blocked the flow of the senses [cannot reach Him]; therefore, resort to that Vāsudeva, the source of no fear.
The superiority of all paths is stated in the third [canto] of the Śrī-Kapila [Bhāgavatam] (3.25.19):
"By means of devotion directed toward the Blessed One, the Self of all, which is not being practiced..."
There is no path like Śiva for yogins seeking the realization of Brahman.
And in the sixth [chapter] (BhP 6.1.17):
"For this path in the world is favorable, secure, and free from fear on all sides, wherein the virtuous and saintly ones find their ultimate refuge in Nārāyaṇa. (Hbhv_11.565)
Therefore, it was said by the venerable Bādarāyaṇa in the Second Book [of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa]:
"Indeed, there is no other auspicious path for one entering into this cycle of worldly existence than this:
that from which devotion (bhakti-yoga) toward the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva arises. (BhP 2.2.33–34)
The Blessed One, having scrutinized Brahman in its entirety three times with his wisdom, determined it; being established in that which is immovable, one should therefore find delight in the Self.
In the *Bṛhan-nāradīya*, as spoken by Śrī Nārada (1.4.4, 30):
"Just as water is remembered as the life-force of all worlds, so devotion is held to be the life-force of all spiritual perfections. (Hbhv_11.568)
Just as all living beings live by depending upon their mother,
so too do all righteous people live by relying upon devotion.
Regarding the greatness of raising the banner, it is stated in the *Śrī-Viṣṇudūta*:
"Whether one is burdened by great sins or burdened by all sins, through devotion to the Blessed One, one attains the desired supreme goal. (Hbhv 11.570)
In the *Pādmapurāṇa*, within the *Māhātmya of Vaiśākha* during the dialogue between Yama and the Brāhmaṇa:
"Offspring, wealth, a wife, necklaces, mansions, horses, and elephants—happiness, heaven, and even liberation are not far from devotion to Hari. (Hbhv_11.571)
In the first book [of the Bhāgavatapurāṇa] (BhP 1.2.7):
"Devotional yoga directed toward the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva quickly generates dispassion and that knowledge which is without cause. (Hbhv_11.572)
And in the eleventh [book] (BhP 11.20.32–33):

"Whatever is attained through ritual acts, through austerity, through knowledge and dispassion, through yoga, through the duty of self-restraint, and through other means of excellence... (Hbhv 11.573).
Through the yoga of devotion to me, my devotee easily attains everything—
both heaven and liberation, as well as my own abode— if he so desires.
Therefore it is said in the Second Canto [BhP 2.3.10]:
"Whether free from desire, or desiring all things, or desiring liberation, one of noble intellect should worship the Supreme Person with intense yoga of devotion. (Hbhv_11.575)
Regarding the superiority of liberation, in the third book of the *Kāpileya* [Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.25.32]:
"Unmotivated devotion to the Lord is greater than spiritual perfection."
It quickly consumes the treasury, just as fire consumes what has been swallowed.
At the conclusion of the life of Śrī Ṛṣabhadeva in the fifth book [BhP 5.6.17]:

"In that very [devotion], the sages incessantly bathe their souls—which are being scorched by the various afflictions of saṃsāra—at every moment; and by that supreme satisfaction alone, they attain liberation, which is the ultimate and final goal of human life."
